screening_results.reason: This is an fMRI study of social cognition (impression formation/updating of others) using a task with faces and behaviors. Sample: 24 healthy adults, ages 18–45, meeting the adult healthy sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (interaction and L2>F3 contrasts) with voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction, figures and tables of results. Whole-brain results are clearly described for the healthy/control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental materials are referenced but not required. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social perception (visual processing of dyadic interactions), using healthy adult participants (N=21, ages 18–35). The authors performed whole-brain preprocessing and GLM estimation to generate run-wise whole-brain beta maps and report group-level statistical analyses (one-sample t-tests) and whole-brain searchlight analyses. Results include group-level voxelwise classification/searchlight findings and discussion of whole-brain effects. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses/maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or resting-state-only) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines understanding of others' regret (a social-related ‘perception and understanding of others’ task) using task-based BOLD fMRI. Participants are healthy adults (two samples of 24 each; ages reported within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., IP minus IF and OP minus OF), parametric and conjunction analyses, and reports activation foci/coordinates and whole-brain statistical maps described in the text and figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and acquisition/analysis details).

Exclusion E4: The study includes fMRI social tasks and a healthy control group aged 50–60 (I3 and I4 are satisfied). However, the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Reported whole-brain maps are for the combined sample (whole group) and ROI/small-volume corrected analyses and between-group contrasts (Cocaine > Control). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task effect reported) and meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an ecological social-related task (listening to film excerpts and inferring characters’ mental states), including a healthy adult group (HC-S1, n=28; ages 18–65). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for the healthy control group (INT>HIN contrast; one-sample t-test, p<0.05 FWE) with tables and figures of activation peaks and maps, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Results for the healthy group are clearly separable from the patient group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

The study uses task-based fMRI with a social vs non-social incentive delay paradigm and includes a healthy adult control group, but the paper reports results primarily as between-group contrasts and interactions (BPD vs HC) and ROI analyses. The manuscript does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone (e.g., HC social>non-social whole-brain contrast). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without a standalone whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participant group reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Full text appears complete.

The paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (Animated Triangles Task) probing mentalizing (Perception/Understanding of Others). It includes a healthy adult control group (N=17, ages matched to patients within 18–30), and reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (within-group control activations and cluster-corrected Z maps are described and shown). Reporting of whole-brain results for the healthy group appears in text and figures. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of perception and understanding of self/others (social-related task), meeting the review scope. Sample: 30 healthy adult participants (15M/15F), ages ~26, within 18–65, with results reported separately for healthy participants. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and contrasts (thresholds, cluster correction, coordinates, and tables/figures), not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This empirical fMRI study (n=51 healthy adults, mean age 22.5) directly investigates social processing (perception of others’ dynamic facial expressions). It reports group-level, whole-brain, voxel-wise task activation contrasts (dynamic facial expressions vs. dynamic mosaics) with appropriate random-effects analyses and FWE-corrected thresholds, with results shown in tables and figures. All inclusion criteria (I3: fMRI social-related task; I4: healthy adult sample 18–65; I5: whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps; I6: results clearly reported in text/figures/tables) are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used fMRI during a clearly social task (Socio-emotional Preferential Task; liking/appraisal of faces) and reports results for a healthy control group. The paper presents whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses with corrected thresholds and reports task-related activations (e.g., dmPFC/ACC) attributed to HC (text and figures/Supplementary Figures), and provides peak coordinates and clusters. Healthy controls (n=13) are adults and results for the control group are reported separately/identifiably. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and hence is complete for screening purposes. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI experiment investigating social interaction and self-involvement using virtual characters (social communication and perception of self/others). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (18 right-handed males, mean age 25.9; analyses reported for n=17), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with reported stereotactic coordinates, tables and figures of main effects and interactions (e.g., SOC>ARB, ME>OTHER), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly presented. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses task-based fMRI during attractiveness comparisons (a social judgment of others), includes a healthy adult sample (25 right-handed British women, mean age 23.46), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain contrasts, conjunctions, and tables/figures with coordinates). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results clearly reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages are within range, empirical data are presented). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This paper reports an fMRI study of social decision-making in healthy adult participants (neuroimaging cohort: n=62 after exclusions; ages 18–53). The task manipulates social information (Locations, Points, Both, Isolated) and examines neural responses to social vs. reward-based influences. The manuscript describes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM analyses (SPM8, random-effects) with multiple-comparisons correction via SnPM and thresholded statistical maps; statistical maps are shared on NeuroVault. Thus it meets the fMRI social-task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

This is an fMRI study of social perception (perceiving person interactions), involving a social-related task (sex-categorization while viewing congruent/incongruent person dyads), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=12, ages 21–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses and exploratory whole-brain contrasts (voxelwise p<.001, cluster-based p<.05) with tables of peak coordinates and figures, clearly attributable to the healthy/control group. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for task fMRI of social processing in healthy adults and reports whole-brain results.

This empirical fMRI study investigates self- and mother-referential processing and an abstract social attribution task (SAT), which are social-related constructs (affiliation/attachment; perception/understanding of self and others). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=17 analyzed, mean age 21.5) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and statistics (composite t-maps, conjunctions, tables of peak coordinates, FDR-corrected maps and uncorrected contrasts) clearly from the healthy/control group. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, figures/tables/coordinates).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (implicit/explicit detection of eye-gaze and self-propelling motion; implicit mental-state inference task), conducted in healthy adult participants (ages 19–28). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and statistical maps/contrasts (e.g., E–O, S–X; PCA-based regressions) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; results are presented in tables and figures. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: social-related fMRI tasks; I4: healthy adult sample 18–65; I5: whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported; I6: results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore INCLUDE.

Although this is an empirical fMRI study of social-related tasks in healthy adults and reports voxelwise activation and peak coordinates, the group-level statistical analyses reported in the paper were restricted to a bilateral STS mask rather than presented as unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map from the healthy/control group) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample), I6 (coordinates/tables/figures reporting results). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in a healthy adult sample (24 males, ages 19–60) using a deception task that probes social-cognitive processes (deception, theory-of-mind/mentalising and manipulation). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (lie > truth and truth > lie) with statistical maps/tables and cluster coordinates, and applies small-volume corrections; results for the healthy/control group are reported directly. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This article is a non-empirical review (Japanese language) discussing fMRI methods and findings broadly; it does not present original fMRI data from a sample of healthy adults or report group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no original fMRI task data on social processing), I4 (no healthy adult sample reported), I5 (no group-level whole-brain statistical maps), I6 (no whole-brain results reported). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata/review summary provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines voice-identity processing (speaker recognition and vocal vs. non-vocal listening), which falls under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). The paper reports data from healthy adult control groups (n=32; age ranges ~29–34; individually reported and matched to cases) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM second-level contrasts for controls; within-group activation maps and tables of coordinates are reported for contrasts such as vocal>non-vocal and speaker>speech). Results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables, with significance thresholds described, and figures/tables showing control-group activations. Although the paper also includes single-case vs. control comparisons and PPI connectivity analyses, it clearly provides unmasked healthy-group task activation effects. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (Cyberball social exclusion), with healthy adult participants (Chinese university students, final N=42; screened for neurological history). It presents whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (exclusion vs inclusion) across all participants and separate within-group whole-brain analyses, with results reported in text, tables, and figures (P<0.05 FWE). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI investigation of social-related processing (intimacy, empathy, perspective taking toward Self/Loved-one/Stranger). Sample: 36 healthy adult participants (mean age 23), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (Pain vs Neutral contrasts across perspectives) with voxelwise thresholds and tables of coordinates (FDR-corrected maps and coordinate tables/supplementary tables). Whole-brain correlation and PPI analyses are reported but do not preclude whole-brain task activation maps. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (empathy, Theory of Mind, self–other differentiation) using task-based BOLD imaging in healthy adult participants (15 right-handed males aged 18–40). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts, cluster thresholds, peak coordinates, conjunctions, and figures/tables describing healthy-group task effects (sad vs neutral; condition contrasts). Thus it meets the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult samples, or non-empirical) are violated.

This paper reports task-based fMRI during a social task (processing social hierarchy), uses a healthy adult sample (n=72; analyses on 48 social participants; ages within 19–43 and 19–38 in experiments), and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses (random-effects SPM5, thresholded and FDR-corrected; tables of coordinates and figures). The results are clearly reported for the healthy/control participants (within-group contrasts such as ‘superior > inferior’) and whole-brain maps/coordinate tables are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates social-emotional processing (schadenfreude and fremdscham) using task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants (N=34, ages 19–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (SIT vs NEUT) with family-wise-error (FWE) whole-brain correction and provides coordinates and ROI-corrected results; parametric and connectivity analyses are also detailed. Results for the healthy/control group are reported explicitly (between-group design but healthy-group effects and within-group contrasts are presented). Thus the study meets the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level task-evoked results.

This is an fMRI study of emotion regulation using participant-generated autobiographical social situations and negative self-beliefs—i.e., social-related processing focused on perception/understanding of self in social contexts. Sample: 35 healthy adults aged 22.6–55.4, meeting the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (random-effects group maps), tables of activations, figures, and ROI analyses; whole-brain results are clearly identified as from the healthy/control group. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Experiments 1 and 2; mean ages ~20–21, within 18–65) that uses a social interactive task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) contrasted with a non-social control (Gamble), directly addressing social cognition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and random-effects contrasts (e.g., PD–Gamble) with thresholding and tables of activations (Figures/Tables and coordinate lists), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Results for the healthy/control group are presented (not limited to a narrow subgroup). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction perception in healthy adults (ages 18–34). The tasks are social-related (perception/understanding of others) and functional MRI was used. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (interaction > independent actions) with FDR-corrected clusters and whole-brain analyses described in the text and figures. Whole-brain results are clearly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not report task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults. The paper uses resting-state fMRI connectivity analyses and behavioral (out-of-scanner) social tasks in patient and control groups, but no whole-brain, task-evoked fMRI activation maps for the healthy/control group are reported. Exclusion ID met: E3 (resting-state analyses only without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (a healthy control group is included). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked map from the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social interaction (free online imitation), meeting the review objective. Participants were healthy adults (23 right-handed females, age 18–30). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts are reported (e.g., imitating vs rest, being imitated vs rest, observation vs rest) with correction for multiple comparisons (FWE p<0.05) and coordinates/tables provided. The study therefore provides whole-brain evidence for the healthy group rather than only ROI or connectivity-only results (although PPI is also reported). All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social-content valence classification task (agency vs. communion), satisfying the review’s focus on social-related processing. Sample: 42 healthy adult participants (ages 18–25), meeting the adult healthy sample requirement. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM8 with AlphaSim correction; conjunction and contrast maps (agency vs. fixation, communion vs. fixation, and direct contrasts) are reported and described (tables/figures of coordinates referenced). Thus the study provides qualifying whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore I include the study.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study examining self/other processing (social cognition) using a semantic self/other/letter judgment paradigm, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper includes a healthy typically-developing (TD) control group and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group activation maps and tables for the TD group (e.g., self vs. letter contrasts shown in figures and Table 2). Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described in the text, figures, and tables. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. Although the sample description includes some participants under 18 in the initial recruitment, the study reports separate healthy-group whole-brain task effects; this satisfies the requirement for a healthy adult control group for inclusion in the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This article is a narrative/review overview of a program of fMRI research rather than an original empirical fMRI study reporting new healthy adult whole-brain task activation maps. It synthesizes and reproduces results from prior empirical papers (e.g., Pelphrey et al. 2003, 2004, 2005, 2007) but does not present original group-level whole-brain statistical maps or new healthy adult fMRI data. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (the paper itself does not report an original fMRI experiment), I4 (does not present a new healthy adult sample 18–65 in original analyses), I5 (does not report at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from a healthy/control group). Inclusion criteria met: none.

The paper reports task-based fMRI during a faces-versus-houses task (socially relevant face perception), in a healthy adult sample (N=57 total; fMRI subset N=22; mean age ~18.9). The authors performed group-level, whole-brain second-level GLM analyses and report significant whole-brain activations and clusters (bilateral fusiform gyrus; suprathreshold voxel counts and cluster tables/figures), satisfying the requirement for healthy-group voxelwise task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, pediatric-only, or non-empirical) are violated.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI to investigate an imitation/urge-to-imitate paradigm (a social-cognitive process related to perception/understanding of others and social interaction), includes a healthy adult sample aged 18–25 with results reported for that group, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric modulation, SPM8) with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study directly investigating social-context vs. non-social episodic memory (social interaction / social scripts) using a task that manipulates social vs. solitary conditions. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=24, ages 18–28). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM5, voxelwise contrasts, thresholding, cluster correction) with tables/figures of activations. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of facial emotion perception (a social-related task: perception/understanding of others) that includes a healthy adult control group (ages 18–65) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses (within-group and between-group whole-brain contrasts, with results described for the control group). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not use fMRI during a social-related task (I3 not met). The fMRI paradigm measured motion processing (moving vs. stationary visual stimuli), not social processes (e.g., affiliation, social communication, perception/understanding of self or others). Although the paper includes healthy adult control groups (I4 met) and reports fMRI activation in motion-sensitive regions, the core review inclusion requirement of a social-related fMRI task is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) are clearly triggered by the provided full text. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I5 (task is not social-related so the required whole-brain, task-evoked social activation for the healthy group is not relevant/fulfilled), I6 (not applicable because task is non-social). Exclusion criteria applied: none ([]).

Full text is incomplete: provided content is a website privacy/cookie notice plus bibliographic metadata only. Exclusion IDs met: [] (none can be confirmed). Inclusion IDs met: [] (none can be confirmed). Inclusion IDs not met / not verifiable: I3 (cannot confirm the task is a social-related fMRI task from the truncated text), I4 (cannot confirm a healthy adult sample or separate reporting), I5 (cannot confirm availability of a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map), I6 (cannot confirm that whole-brain results are reported in any form). Because core article content (methods, results) is missing, I cannot assess eligibility; thus exclude pending full text.

Exclusion E2 met: the reported neuroimaging results are based on a priori ROI analyses with FWE correction performed within ROIs; no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation map is reported in this full text. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — physician–patient interaction, empathy/compassion) and I4 (healthy adult physician sample, ages 25–37). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked map from the healthy group is presented). The full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper reports task-based functional MRI of action observation and weight-discrimination tasks probing perception/understanding of others (social perception). Healthy adult participants are included (multiple experiments with n=79 healthy participants; controls for the SCA6 patient study are reported separately), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (ActionOBS–CtrlOBS; Sleeve/NoSleeve) are reported and described in the text, figures, and supplementary materials. Whole-brain analyses and coordinates are provided, satisfying reporting requirements. The study is empirical fMRI work in healthy adults and does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical methods. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This study used fMRI during a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–22), so it meets I3 and I4. However, the manuscript does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group. Analyses are restricted to ROI-based activation summaries and ROI/network-based task PPI (gPPI) connectivity with small-volume corrections and between-group contrasts (OT vs PL). Therefore it fails to meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and falls under exclusion criteria: E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results), E3 (reports task-based connectivity/seed analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map), and E4 (focus on between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Cyberball (virtual ball-toss) social interaction task (social reward/affiliation), with healthy adult participants (final N=31; ages ~21) and explicit reporting of group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-level FWE-corrected maps and peak coordinates in text/tables/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI during social-related processing (self- and other-evaluation of personality traits), includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately, and provides whole-brain group-level activation maps/contrasts for the control group (one-sample and between-group analyses reported and summarized in tables/figures). The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, age out of range, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This study uses fMRI during a social-related face encoding task (I3), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps for the typically-developing control group (I5, I6). However, it is unclear whether the healthy control group consists solely of adults aged 18–65. The methods describe adolescent consent and mock scanning for participants under 18 and provide a mean control age of 18.7 (SD=5.8), indicating that some control participants were likely minors. Inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult group 18–65) is therefore not clearly satisfied based on the provided full text; because at least one inclusion criterion is not met, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social working memory (trait-based ranking) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=25, mean age 21.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and contrasts of parametric modulation by load), thresholding and tables/figures of clusters/coordinates, and links neural activation to behavioral measures of perspective-taking. All required core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (cooperation vs. competition) in healthy adult participants (ages 21–38). The task is a social-related, interactive game probing theory-of-mind and social processing (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adults within the 18–65 range and reports group-level analyses for the healthy participants (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts and corrected voxelwise analyses (e.g., active>passive contrasts; meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study directly examines social-related processing (affective and cognitive Theory of Mind), satisfying the social-task requirement. The sample is 23 healthy participants recruited from the general population (healthy adult group reported separately), meeting the sample criterion for a healthy adult group. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain FDR-corrected cluster results, tables/figures described), providing the required healthy-group whole-brain evidence. Results for AToM and CToM are reported for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only samples, or non-empirical paper) are met. Note: exact participant ages are not explicitly listed in the provided text, but participants are described as healthy adults and age was used as a covariate; this introduces minor uncertainty reflected in the confidence score.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 19–36) that used a task probing animacy perception from visual motion — a precursor to perception/understanding of others and thus a social-related process. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise contrasts, FWE-corrected thresholds), figures and tables of results, and ROI and whole-brain MVPA/searchlight results. All inclusion criteria for the review are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition using a social-related task (trustworthiness judgments of faces) satisfying I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=18, mean age 32.2) reported separately from the clinical XXY group, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-group, whole-brain task activation analyses for the control group (whole-brain contrasts and tables/figures described), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported). Therefore the study meets all inclusion requirements for the review objective.

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study using a social interaction task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes retaliation/provocation—clearly a social-related process. Participants are healthy adult males (N=15; mean age 22.3), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise statistical maps, cluster correction, Talairach coordinates, and figures/tables of activation (i.e., whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group). Reporting format (tables/figures and text) satisfies acceptable evidence. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical work) are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Note: sample is small and male-only (limits generalizability) but does not violate inclusion requirements. Therefore include.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it reports an fMRI experiment of social-related processing (explicit mental simulation of others’ actions/feelings) in healthy adults (20 participants, ages 21–47), and it provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (GLM SPM-t maps, cluster-level FDR-corrected) and corresponding figures/tables. The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling verification of measures and analyses. Although the paper also reports connectivity (ISPS/SBPS), it additionally includes conventional whole-brain activation analyses, so no exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (valence judgments of naturalistic social interactions) in a healthy adult sample (N=38, ages 18–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., Social > Non-social contrasts; full-factorial ANOVA) with FWE correction and provides activation tables/figures and coordinates. Results are for the healthy/control group (no clinical subgroup only reporting). The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or out-of-range ages) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind / explaining others’ behavior) using an experimental Why/How task (I3). Samples are healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range across Studies 1–3 (ages 19–38; N=29, 10, 21), with analysis reported for the healthy groups (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (Why>How, How>Why, Belief>Photo) and provides whole-brain corrected results and tables of peak coordinates (Tables 2–4, cluster- and voxel-level FWE corrections), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental material is not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports task-based fMRI data including multiple social-cognition tasks (false-belief ToM, animacy/intentional triangles, eyes-intention, face trustworthiness, vocalizations), i.e. social-related processing. The sample comprises 78 healthy adults (age range 18–40), satisfying the healthy adult criterion. The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses (voxelwise p<0.05 FWE-corrected), figures, and a supplementary table of peak coordinates; maps are also available via NeuroVault/HBP links. These meet the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group results and acceptable reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6.

The study reports task-based fMRI using social stimuli (traffic awareness videos eliciting socio-cognitive processing), includes healthy adult participants (two groups of right-handed male drivers, ages 19–30), and presents group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (CV vs NV) with whole-brain analyses reported for each group and in the text/figures. Thus it meets social-related fMRI task requirement, healthy adult sample, and the presence of whole-brain group-level activation maps/results (reported in figures and text).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (self, friend, celebrity trait judgments) in healthy adult participants (n=37, mean age 22.9), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation contrasts (self vs. celebrity; friend vs. celebrity) with voxelwise statistics (FDR-corrected) and tables of activations. Whole-brain regression and gPPI results are reported and clearly identified as coming from the healthy sample. Thus it satisfies the review’s fMRI task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

Full text content provided appears incomplete (only title, authors, journal metadata; no Introduction/Methods/Results/Discussion). Unable to verify key inclusion criteria: I3 (use of fMRI during a social-related task) cannot be confirmed from provided text; I4 (healthy adult group 18–65 reported separately) cannot be confirmed; I5 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map for healthy/control group) cannot be confirmed; I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/supplement) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria can be confidently identified from the incomplete content. Because the full text is incomplete and essential methodological/results information are missing, the study cannot be judged eligible for inclusion at this stage.

Exclusion IDs met: E2, E3. Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4. Inclusion IDs not met: I5. 

Rationale: The study used task fMRI with a social-affective (empathic fear) cinematic stimulus and reports results for a healthy adult control group (satisfying I3 and I4). However, the manuscript does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group. Analyses focus on network-cohesion indices derived from meta-analytic ROIs and connectivity/time-series comparisons (NCI) rather than unmasked whole-brain activation maps. Thus it meets exclusion criteria E2 (ROI/connectivity-focused without whole-brain results) and E3 (connectivity-only analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The paper reports an fMRI study of social decision-making (modified iterated prisoner's dilemma) in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 23–38). It includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (conjunction and task contrasts such as COMP>COOP), cluster-level multiple-comparison correction, and reports results in figures/tables (coordinates and SPMs). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is present. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I3: It uses task-based fMRI with social-related stimuli (pictures of faces as target events) within an oddball target-detection paradigm, addressing social processing. I4: The sample comprises healthy adults (N=19; age range 19.3–47.5), with screening for psychiatric symptoms and separate reporting of this (healthy) group. I5/I6: The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (shape targets–novels, face targets–novels, and direct comparisons) analyzed with FSL (cluster-corrected Z and P thresholds), and presents figures and a table of MNI coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and the paper reports original empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables). Therefore include.

This is an fMRI study of social communication/interaction in healthy adults (ages 18–27; final N=29). The task manipulates perceived live versus recorded speech and examines neural responses; authors report group-level whole-brain task contrasts (Live > Social; Social > Standard) with cluster-correction and figures/tables of results. Although ROI/localizer analyses are also reported, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps for the healthy sample are clearly presented and described. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, healthy adult sample, empirical fMRI data). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related processing in healthy adults.

Although this fMRI study examines social/attachment-related processing using a baby-cry task (meets I3) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (meets I4), the paper reports results primarily via ROI-based small-volume corrected analyses and seed-based connectivity (gPPI). The manuscript does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (i.e., no whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task effect is reported). Therefore it violates the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E2.

This is an fMRI study investigating learning about others’ preference similarity—a social cognitive task (affiliation/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (n=25, mean age 25.1) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (conjunction analyses, cluster-corrected activations, MNI coordinates) for the healthy participant group (e.g., dmPFC, caudate, precuneus, AG, STS), satisfying reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, model-based fMRI analysis), Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical study). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the review.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=29, ages 18–24) investigating communicative speech production, a social communication task involving perception and understanding of others. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (communication vs description, task vs control) with statistical thresholds and tables/figures of activated cortical areas and peak coordinates. Results are reported for the healthy/control group and include whole-brain analyses rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only approaches. Thus it meets the review objective and satisfies the required reporting and sample criteria.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in which healthy adult participants (N=13, mean age 27.2) passively viewed realistic social interaction video clips (a social-related task). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (corrected P ≤ 0.05 across the whole brain) with figures and tables of activations (including coordinates and clusters), and contrasts versus rest and versus an ‘alone’ condition. These satisfy the review’s requirements for social task fMRI, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) apply.

Exclusion per I5 not met: The study reports task-based fMRI (false-belief localizer) and includes a healthy young adult group (age 18–33), so it meets I3 (fMRI during social task) and I4 (healthy adult subgroup 18–65). However, the paper does not provide a clearly identified, unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map explicitly from the healthy adult group (YA 18–33). The reported whole-brain maps/contrasts are either an ANOVA/main effect or contrasts collapsed across both age groups (including participants >65), and the theory-of-mind localizer nodes were defined using a contrast collapsed across age. Thus inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied, and per review rules the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (no accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect reported).

The study meets I3 (uses fMRI with a social inference task — the Why/How task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, age 18–45, reported separately). However, it does NOT provide a whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5 not met). The paper reports whole-brain analyses of Group×Stimulus interactions and ROI-based results, and primarily focuses on between-group contrasts and interactions; there is no unmasked, within-healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (only ROI and between-group/interaction maps are presented). Therefore exclusion criterion E4 (studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect) is met. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses fMRI during a social-evaluation task (perception/understanding of self/peer evaluation); (I4) the sample includes healthy adult participants (ages extend to 22.9 years, i.e., adults within 18–65); (I5) the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (whole-brain mixed-effects analyses and corrected cluster results, e.g., MPFC activation and PPI results reported for the full healthy sample); (I6) whole-brain results are described in the text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only, not only connectivity, and the study reports within-group whole-brain task effects in a healthy sample. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this fMRI study used a social task (Cyberball) and reports group-level whole-brain maps and coordinate tables/figures, it included both healthy adults (n=37) and a clinical subgroup with SAD (n=9) but did not report group-level whole-brain results separately for the healthy-only group. The meta-analysis requires that when clinical groups are included, results for the healthy group be reported separately. Here the primary one-sample t-tests and regression analyses are reported for the entire sample (combined healthy and SAD) rather than a clearly identified healthy/control group. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly triggered by the paper’s reporting format.

This is an fMRI study using social-cognition tasks (affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral face processing) meeting the review objective. The sample includes a healthy control group of adults (n=13) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain group-level activations and single-group results (reported at P<0.001 uncorrected; single-group results noted in Supplementary Tables S1–S4), satisfying the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, participants are adults, and this is empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study should be included.

Full text appears incomplete: only metadata/title/abstract-like page info provided, without methods, participants, results, or figures. Cannot verify inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met (cannot confirm): I3 (uncertain whether task-based fMRI during a social-related task is reported in the available text), I4 (sample details and whether healthy adults 18–65 are reported separately not available), I5 (no accessible whole-brain, group-level task activation map or coordinates in the provided content), I6 (no supplementary or coordinate tables are present in the provided content). No exclusion criteria were clearly met from available content. Because the full text is incomplete, study cannot be confidently assessed for inclusion in the review and is excluded pending access to the complete article.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract-like sections provided). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study uses fMRI during social-related tasks; tasks probing attentional and attributional biases/relevance to self). Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable from provided text: I4 (cannot confirm participants' ages — text only says 'normal subjects' without ages to ensure 18–65), I5 (no explicit report in the provided content of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or coordinates/figures clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group). No exclusion criteria are clearly met based on available content ([]). Because core article content (detailed methods, participant demographics, and full analytic reporting) is missing, I cannot confirm the required whole-brain healthy-group results; therefore the study is excluded pending provision of the complete full text.

Exclusion E3 met: the paper reports only task-based functional connectivity analyses (ROI-to-ROI and seed-to-voxel connectivity) and does not present any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps or within-group task activation contrasts for the healthy/control (TD) group. Inclusion I3 met: study uses task fMRI of a social-related action-intention judgment. Inclusion I4 met: a healthy adult control group (typically developing adults, 18–65) is included and reported separately. Inclusion I5 NOT met: no whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy group is reported. Therefore the study must be excluded per E3.

This article is a systematic review / meta-analysis (MKDA) of previously published fMRI studies rather than an original empirical fMRI study reporting new task-evoked whole-brain maps from healthy adult participants. Thus it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). While the topic (love and sexual desire) relates to social/affiliation constructs, the paper itself does not fulfill the required inclusion criteria: it does not use fMRI on its own during a social-related task (I3 not met), does not report an original healthy adult participant group (I4 not met), and does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map from an original healthy group (I5 not met). No inclusion criteria are fully satisfied by this paper as an empirical study.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 18–35) using an empathy-for-pain paradigm with experimentally induced (minimal) groups, which is a social cognitive task (perception/understanding of others). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses are reported (SPM8 repeated-measures ANOVA; main effects and interactions reported with FWE-corrected and uncorrected thresholds and referenced Tables of results), providing unmasked healthy-group task activation maps. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used a social-feedback (acceptance/rejection) task during task-based fMRI (satisfies I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (20 females, mean age 28.15) and reports controls separately alongside patients (satisfies I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group activation maps/analyses for the healthy control group (SPM8 whole-brain analyses with cluster correction; within-group activations for controls are described and shown), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group healthy whole-brain task effects are reported. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathy/perspective-taking (perception and understanding of others), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=23, ages 19–34). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects contrasts such as Pain > No Pain and target-specific contrasts) with reported statistical thresholds, tables/figures of activation clusters, and PPI connectivity results. Behavioral and dispositional measures for the healthy sample are reported separately. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study examines vocal emotional processing in healthy adults (I3 and I4 satisfied) but does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy group. Instead, results are reported as ROI-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical network metrics. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (connectivity/graph analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E2 (only ROI/parcellation-based analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain task results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related task: vocal emotion/social communication) and I4 (healthy adult sample 20–35). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study investigating social perception (affiliation vs. isolation) during a task with pleasantness ratings. It includes a healthy younger adult group (mean age 20.75) within the 18–65 range and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM2 results, thresholding, coordinate tables, conjunction analyses, and figures) for the healthy groups. Results for younger (healthy) and older groups are reported separately and whole-brain task-evoked effects (e.g., temporal pole, medial PFC, precuneus, hippocampus) are presented in tables/figures. The paper is empirical, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and provides the necessary group-level whole-brain activation maps/statistics in the main text/tables. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study used task-based fMRI of social cognition (affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral face processing) meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=22) reported separately and matched to patients. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task effects (ToM > Emotion > Neutral) with tables of cluster coordinates and statistics, and the manuscript and supplementary materials describe group-specific and within-group contrasts (supplementary analyses are referenced). Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures (main text and supplementary), satisfying the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task maps. The full article text including introduction, methods, results and discussion is provided. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria. Note: some group-specific contrasts are reported in supplementary materials referenced in the text; these are acceptable per I6.

The study uses fMRI with an emotional face (social) go/no-go task and reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps for the neurotypical control group (meets I3, I5, I6). However, the healthy/control sample includes participants aged 12–23 and is not restricted to adults 18–65; no separate healthy adult (18–65) subgroup is analyzed or reported. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I4. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) directly apply beyond the failure to meet I4.

This study used fMRI during a social-related task (affiliation and power movie clips) in healthy adult participants (n=17 males, mean age 23.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (affiliation > control; power > control) and regression analyses with activation clusters and MNI coordinates presented in Table 1 and Figure 2. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical) are applicable.

This is an empirical dual-fMRI hyperscanning study in healthy adults (N=44, mean age 22.37) using a social interaction task (pattern game) that manipulates cooperation/competition and concurrent/turn-based interaction—clearly a social-related task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results with non-parametric permutation correction and presents cluster coordinates and figures (Tables 1–3, Fig. 4), satisfying whole-brain reporting (coordinates/figures). All inclusion criteria are met (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample reported; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported; I6: whole-brain results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition using the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test (a social-related ToM task), conducted in healthy adult participants (18 right-handed males, mean age 26.4). The paper reports group-level task-evoked contrasts within the healthy/control group (ToM > gender in the placebo condition) and additionally reports exploratory whole-brain analyses (coordinate tables and figures) comparing LPS vs placebo, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task effects. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing (implicit social stimulus processing) in healthy adults. The sample comprises 28 healthy right-handed adults aged 30–50 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses (ANOVA across the 28 subjects), conjunction and direct contrasts, thresholded and reported with cluster sizes and MNI coordinates, and figures/tables of results. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) targeting social interaction and responses to unreciprocated cooperation, satisfying I3. Sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–22 (N≈304), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses and whole-brain results (e.g., main effect CD>CC in whole-brain analyses, referenced figures and supplemental whole-brain figures/tables), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants within age range, and it is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition using a social-comparison task (Close Other vs Non-Close Other) performed in healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age 18.7). The paper reports group-level, random-effects second-level voxelwise contrasts (SPM{t} maps) and provides peak coordinates and statistical values for task-evoked activations (reported in text and figures/tables). Whole-group healthy participant results are clearly presented (e.g., Target × Breadth and Valence contrasts), meeting the review objective of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults. Although multiple-comparison correction was implemented within a priori ROIs, the study presents voxelwise, group-level activation maps and coordinate tables for the healthy/control sample.

The study reports an fMRI task examining social interaction processing (affective and cooperative interactions), satisfying the review’s social-related construct (I3). Sample consists of 36 healthy adult participants (ages ~24–25), meeting the sample criterion (I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects group analysis; results thresholded and reported with cluster FDR p<.05; tables and figures of activations), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). The supplied full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI task study of social-related processing (empathy/theory-of-mind) in healthy adults (N=16 analyzed; mean age 27.8), using a social task (viewing emotional vs. neutral social scenes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (EMOT vs NEUT; TWO vs ONE) with Talairach coordinates, tables, figures and voxelwise statistical maps (FDR q<0.05) clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Results are not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, or patient-group-only contrasts. Thus it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for whole-brain healthy adult fMRI social processing studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=25 females, mean age 23.2). Participants performed a social (mentalizing) task about friends and kin during task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (friend > kin contrast and parametric linear analyses across network layers) with cluster-thresholding, tables of clusters/coordinates, and figures. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears to be a complete full text. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (task fMRI of social processing), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from healthy group), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Task is the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test, a social-cognitive task probing perception/understanding of others; (I4) Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=16, mean age 20.8) reported separately; (I5) The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts (emotion vs control) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and listed peak coordinates (Tables/Figures); (I6) Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-affective task (threat-of-shock while holding a friend, stranger, or alone) that directly probes social regulation of neural threat responding, satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=22, mean age 23.6), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses used to identify functional ROIs (cluster-wise tests with FSL, Z-threshold and cluster p-threshold) and provides ROI coordinates and statistical results (Table 1 and text), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROIs only, are not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and the article is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is a resting-state fMRI study that manipulated participants’ belief about being observed; analyses report changes in functional connectivity (network/node correlations) rather than any group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise activation maps. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=29, ages 18–22), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. However, the paper does not present whole-brain task activation results (no task-evoked voxelwise maps), and it reports only resting-state/connectivity analyses, so it meets exclusion E3. Therefore it cannot be included for a meta-analysis that requires whole-brain task-evoked activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-cognitive task (judging political statements) that probes perception/understanding of self and others and broader social cognition. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages 22–45) and the study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task analyses (SPM random-effects second-level analyses, whole-brain thresholds reported, ROI corrections noted) with result tables and figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so article is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16–17 analyzed per task; age range 21–46) that directly probes social-related processing (attribution/understanding of emotions in humans and non-human animals). The paper reports whole-brain group-level analyses (conjunctions, cluster-level FWE correction) and ROI and whole-brain results, with statistical maps and tabulated results described (meeting acceptable reporting formats). All required content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in acceptable formats). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group task effects, empirical data in healthy adults).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (approachability judgments from faces) that reports whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and coordinates for the healthy control group separately. The Methods and Results provide group-level, voxelwise contrasts for controls (e.g., approachability > gender) with cluster-corrected statistics and peak MNI coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Healthy adult control sample (n=24) is described and analyzed separately. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text describes an empirical fMRI study using a validated social ‘Theory of Mind’ visual task (moving triangles) meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample consists of 20 healthy adults aged 24–64 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (ToM > R; ToM > Baseline) with statistical thresholds, peak coordinates, and tables/figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). The full text content appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (empathic concern for characters in film clips) in healthy adults. The sample comprises 26 healthy adult participants (mean age 30.3), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and contrasts, Tables 1–2, and whole-brain figures) and parametric modulation results for the healthy group, which meet the whole-brain evidence criterion; results are presented in text, tables, and figures. The study additionally includes connectivity (DCM), but also reports univariate whole-brain activations, so it does not violate exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract provided). The abstract indicates use of fMRI hyperscanning during a social interaction (a deception game), so inclusion criterion I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) is satisfied. However, the provided content does not report participant details to confirm a healthy adult sample (I4) nor sufficient results/methods to confirm reporting of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (I5). No exclusion criteria are clearly met based on the available content. Because core article sections (methods, results) are missing, I cannot verify I4 and I5 — fulltext_incomplete is set and the study is excluded pending access to the complete full text.

This fMRI study investigates social cognition (evaluating whether one person’s actions are consistent with another’s intentions) using a task-based fMRI paradigm in healthy adult participants (final N=16, ages 18–29). The manuscript reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (voxelwise ANOVAs) and ROI analyses, and describes significant whole-brain effects (e.g., medial prefrontal, visual, and somatosensory regions) with statistical thresholds and coordinates. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for an fMRI social-related task in healthy adults and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked results clearly identified for the healthy sample. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants examining processing of mutual vs. averted social gaze (a social-communication/perception task). The sample comprises healthy young adults (reported separately), and the paper reports group-level voxelwise/whole-brain activation maps (t-statistic maps) for the task conditions in the healthy group (in addition to ROI analyses). Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study uses fMRI of social processing (racial ingroup/outgroup face perception) in presumably healthy adult participants, but the full text/abstract does not clearly report a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group. The paper emphasizes an ROI-based analysis of amygdala voxels and does not provide explicit whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinates that can be clearly identified as unmasked healthy-group whole-brain effects. Because inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not demonstrably met, this study must be excluded per exclusion criterion E2 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results).

The study reports task-based fMRI during an interactive social task (Cyberball) assessing social exclusion (meets I3). The sample consists of 21 healthy adult participants aged 20–37, within the 18–65 range (meets I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical results (within-Pla one-sample t tests and paired t tests; uncorrected whole-brain results shown in Tables S3 and S4, and task contrasts described in the text), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-groups-only, participants are within age range, empirical fMRI data are reported). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports an fMRI task probing emotion perception (perception/understanding of others; social communication) using dynamic facial and vocal stimuli — clearly a social-related task. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (ages 19–24 and mean 19.67), reported separately. The paper presents voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked group analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA, whole-brain contrasts, PFWE<0.05) with tables/figures of activations rather than ROI-only results. Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical restrictions).

This is an empirical fMRI study that used the False-Belief Localizer (a social theory-of-mind task) during task fMRI (meets I3). It reports data from healthy adult control groups (Caltech: n=18, ages 21–46; MIT: n=462, ages 18–69), with healthy-group results reported separately (meets I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrast maps and whole-brain analyses for the healthy reference groups (e.g., MIT whole-brain results and Fig. 2), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Consequently, the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study investigates emotion recognition (a social-related task) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (meets I3 and I4). However, the full text does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group; results are reported primarily as between-group contrasts, interactions, ROI analyses, and post-hoc group comparisons. Therefore it meets exclusion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of joint social interaction (leading/following/mutual) with haptic contact, directly addressing social-processing constructs (social communication, perception of others, mentalizing, social reward). Sample comprises healthy adult dancers (mean age 40.4, within 18–65) with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (contrasts, FDR-corrected maps, and tables of Talairach coordinates), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting (figures/tables and text). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study directly examines processing of CT-targeted affective touch—a social-affiliation/affective touch paradigm—using task-based fMRI in healthy adults (ages 19–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation contrasts (arm>baseline, palm>baseline, arm>palm) with correction procedures and cluster thresholds and presents tables/figures of these results. A PPI connectivity analysis is also reported but does not replace the whole-brain task maps. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind) using the REMICS task (social vs physical scenarios) in a sample of healthy adults (N=19, ages 20–53).
