The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., SocAdj>PhyConf, Soc>Phy, Adj>Conf) with peak coordinates and tables of significant clusters (voxelwise threshold p<.001, cluster correction), clearly attributed to the healthy/control group. Thus it meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reported results.

The study uses fMRI to examine neural responses during music appreciation and explicitly interprets activations in default mode/ToM and cognitive-empathy regions as reflecting social-cognitive engagement for artistic music (i.e., perception/understanding of others/social cognition). It reports healthy adult participants (18–24 years) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FDR correction, with coordinates provided. Thus it meets the review objective of social-related processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task activation maps. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (social exclusion, punishment/forgiveness) using Cyberball and a modified Dictator Game (I3). Sample comprises healthy adults (n=26, mean age 20.7) with exclusions applied appropriately (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Exclusion no ball > Inclusion ball; Excluders > Includers; Excluders equality > Includers equality) with peak coordinates, tables, and figures from the healthy participant group (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participant ages are within 18–65, and this is an empirical study with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates event simulation including social situations (41% of stimuli depicted social interactions) and explicitly discusses social-cognitive processes (e.g., theory of mind). Participants are healthy adults (N=20, mean age 20.65), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Imp–Con, Exp–Imp, Ftr–Exp) analyzed with SPM8 using random-effects second-level one-sample t-tests and reports cluster-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates; tables/figures of activation are described. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is eligible for inclusion in the review.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study using social-related tasks (emotion processing and theory-of-mind) (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=14, ages within 18–65) with results reported separately (meets I4). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects task contrasts and statistical maps for the healthy/control group are described and presented (figures and supplementary tables) using an appropriate voxelwise threshold (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is not ROI-only, not exclusively connectivity or resting-state, reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects (not only between-group contrasts), includes adults in the target age range, and is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an empathy task (social cognition) with both schizophrenia patients and a matched healthy control group (N=14). The paper reports within-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) one-sample t-test results for the healthy/control group, including cluster tables and figures, with SPM8 and corrected thresholds (AlphaSim/SVC). Healthy participants are adults within the 18–65 range. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures/tables, discussion).

This study uses fMRI during a social-related task (biological motion perception) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately. However, the imaging results are reported primarily as ROI-based analyses (STSp and MT) localized within individuals; the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group. A whole-brain search is described but focused on schizophrenia patients, and no unmasked healthy-group whole-brain statistical map or coordinate table of a healthy-group whole-brain contrast is provided. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence for the healthy group) is not met. Exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of prosocial (social) learning in healthy adults. It meets I3: uses task-based fMRI targeting social/prosocial processing; I4: sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=31, ages 19–32) with results reported for the healthy group; I5: reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and peak coordinates (with voxelwise/FWE/SVC results and tables/figures); I6: whole-brain results are clearly described in the text, tables, and figures (including supplemental tables). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic social gestures) in a sample of healthy participants, reporting group-level whole-brain task activation results (cluster-corrected maps and coordinates). The sample consists of young healthy adults (mean age 21.4; range 16.9–25.7) — while the lower bound includes one participant under 18, the study reports a single healthy group with adults in the 18–65 range and provides group-level whole-brain results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are not required. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=195, age 19–38) using a social interactive task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) that probes mentalizing/social cognition. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (ment > cont) analyzed with SPM8 and voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; results (including coordinates and ROI follow-ups) are presented for the healthy sample. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=17, mean age 26) that used a social-related task (observation of social vs. individual actions with gaze manipulation). The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses, voxelwise contrasts (main effects and interaction) with SPM maps and coordinate tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The paper therefore meets the review’s criteria for fMRI social-processing tasks in healthy adults and reports whole-brain task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical paper) are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16, age 18–26) that explicitly investigates emotion perception/evaluation from vocalizations and music and relates these processes to medial prefrontal regions involved in social cognition (e.g., theory of mind/empathy). The study uses task-based fMRI with whole-brain group-level analyses (contrasts, conjunctions, cluster correction) and reports results in text, figures, and tables (including coordinates). The social-related construct (perception and understanding of others’ emotions/social cognition) is clearly targeted by the emotion-tracking task. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based BOLD fMRI collected while healthy adult participants (age 18–22) performed a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (thresholded Z maps and cluster-corrected results reported across sexes and genotypes), with results clearly coming from the healthy sample (OT vs placebo groups). Whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and discussed in the text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is an empirical fMRI study).

The paper is a short conference abstract that describes dyadic fMRI and network synchronizations but does not report essential information required by the review. There is no information on participant sample characteristics (age range, number of healthy adults), and no presentation of group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for a healthy adult group. The abstract appears focused on methodological development and connectivity/synchronization analyses rather than reporting unmasked whole-brain task activation results. Therefore it does not meet the review's requirements for whole-brain healthy-group task activation reporting.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (live social interaction and joint attention tasks) in healthy adults (participants aged 18–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Live > Recorded; Joint Attention > Solo Attention) with corrected statistics and coordinate tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=29; ages 20–35) performing explicit and implicit facial emotion/age discrimination tasks, which are social-cognitive (perception/understanding of others). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and SPM random-effects results are reported (FWE-corrected maps and contrasts), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation. Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and supplemented by ROI analyses. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition (ToM and empathy) in a sample of healthy college students (ages 17–21, mean 19.3). The authors report group-level whole-brain SPM activation maps (RFT-corrected) and pooled-condition contrasts, provide coordinates (Data S1 Table S3), and explicitly use these whole-brain maps in analyses. Thus the study meets the review’s requirements for (1) an fMRI social-related task (I3), (2) a healthy adult sample (majority in 18–65 range; I4), and (3) reporting group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not resting-state only, and includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task using social vs. non-social pictures) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group with results reported). However it does NOT provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (intra-group healthy results are reported via ROI analyses; whole-brain results are reported only for between-group contrasts as exploratory uncorrected maps). Therefore it fails I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task map) and I6 (no qualifying whole-brain healthy results in tables/figures for the healthy group). This matches exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interaction whole-brain results without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion sections, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Participants are adolescents (ages 12–18) rather than healthy adults aged 18–65, so the study does not meet the sample age inclusion criterion (I4). The paper does report an fMRI social task (implicit facial emotion processing) (I3), and reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps for the control group (I5) with results described in the text/figures (I6). However because all participants are outside the specified adult age range and no separate healthy adult subgroup (18–65) is reported, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Full text appears complete.

The study uses task-based fMRI of gaze processing (a social-related task) and reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps for the typically developing (healthy/control) group (Table 2; coordinates), satisfying I3, I5, and I6. However, the healthy/control group includes adolescents as well as adults (ages 16.1–42.4) and results are reported for the mixed-age TD group rather than for a healthy adult (18–65) subgroup specifically; therefore I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65 reported separately) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Because not all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I4 missing), the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study applying a social-cognitive task (affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral face processing) — satisfying I3. The sample includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (n=18) matched for age and education — satisfying I4. The paper reports within-group (healthy controls) task-evoked activation results with whole-brain analyses and voxelwise statistics (thresholds reported, coordinates and significant activations in bilateral STS, inferior prefrontal gyrus, fusiform, amygdala), satisfying I5. Results are reported as coordinates and described in the text/tables (and supplementary material), satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported, participants are adults, and this is an original empirical fMRI study). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines neural responses during a social-cognitive task (conceptualizing actions at different levels of abstraction, engaging theory-of-mind/mentalizing processes). Participants were healthy adults (N=17 after exclusions; ages 21–46). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (one-sample t-tests, cluster-level FWE correction, whole-brain tables/figures and supplementary tables) clearly from the healthy group. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social communicative/collaborative memory task (directors and matchers), investigating social cognition (mentalizing/theory of mind) and communication. The sample is healthy adults aged 18–33 and group results are reported for the healthy participants. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Collaborative > Individual, Individual > Arbitrary, Arbitrary > Individual) with cluster-corrected maps and tables of results; whole-brain ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain effects are primary. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis’ requirements for fMRI of social processing in healthy adults with whole-brain task activation maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults. It uses task-based fMRI during socially relevant tasks (round-robin face-viewing and person-judgment tasks) that probe perception/understanding of others (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (n=26, mean age 28.7) meeting the 18–65 criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects parametric whole-brain regression; Fig. S1 and Table S4) clearly from the healthy sample, satisfying I5 and I6. The manuscript therefore meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply (e.g., it is not ROI-only or connectivity-only). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (audiovisual integration of nonverbal emotional signals), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=24, mean age 26.6). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise task contrasts (conjunction (AV > A) AND (AV > V)), voxelwise correlation analyses, coordinate tables and figures (i.e., whole-brain/voxelwise results clearly attributed to the healthy group). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures described in text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related threat-reactivity task (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (mean age ~55, range 42–68) satisfying the sample criterion (I4). However, the paper reports only region-of-interest (amygdala) analyses and correlation results; it does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation maps or coordinate tables/figures for the healthy/control group. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examines face emotion discrimination, a social-cognition task (social perception/understanding of others). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (two community groups screened with SCID; ages consistent with adult university/community sample). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses (one-sample t-tests of EE vs baseline and EE vs EI across all participants, flexible factorial group analyses) with tables of clusters/coordinates and thresholding details. Results for the healthy groups are reported separately (one-sample maps and group comparisons). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly examines social reward processing (social incentive delay task) in healthy adult participants (N=63; ages 20.4–36.6). The paper reports within-group task-evoked neural activations including whole-brain results and small-volume FWE-corrected ROI results; whole-brain activations and coordinate tables are described (e.g., Tables 2–4, whole-brain FWE-corrected results). Results for the healthy/control group are reported clearly and separately. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports a voxel-based morphometry (structural MRI) study of grey matter volume and its correlation with proneness to moral sentiments in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (the study does not use functional MRI during a social-related task within this paper — the task was behavioral and structural MRI was acquired), I5 (the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked fMRI statistical maps from the healthy/control group; only a secondary analysis uses previously reported SSC-BOLD values from an earlier fMRI study in a subgroup, but this paper does not present unmasked whole-brain fMRI activation maps). Therefore it does not provide the required whole-brain task-based fMRI results for inclusion. No exclusion criteria from the list directly apply beyond failing required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social/affiliation processing: participants completed an IAT contrasting "monogamy" vs "adultery" and a go/no-go task with attractive female faces (social/attachment stimuli). Sample: healthy adult males (age range 20–32), meeting the 18–65 criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts (IAT incongruent vs congruent) with voxelwise thresholding and cluster-level FWE correction and provides tables of peak coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Although the go/no-go VLPFC analysis used an a priori anatomical constraint, the presence of whole-brain IAT results fulfills the whole-brain evidence criterion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state/seed-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical article) apply. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

Exclusion rationale: The study uses fMRI during a social task (implicit fearful face processing) and includes a healthy adult control group, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group. The analyses are ROI-based/parcellation multivariate connectivity (3-MDS) and between-group connectivity comparisons; activation mapping by mass-univariate analysis is stated as previously reported elsewhere, but this full text does not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map (voxelwise). Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E2 (ROI-only/no whole-brain results), E3 (connectivity-only without healthy-group whole-brain task map), and E4 (reports primarily between-group connectivity contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Frith–Happé animation ToM task) in adults and reports results for a neurotypical healthy control group. The healthy control group (n=23) is within the 18–65 age range (19–56 reported) and is analyzed/reported separately from the ASD group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain one-sample t-tests and whole-brain analyses for the NT/control group (results and supplementary whole-brain results are described and displayed), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (self-related judgments) in healthy adults. It uses task-based fMRI during self-judgment (a social-related construct: Perception/Understanding of Self), includes a healthy adult sample (n=24; ages within 18–65), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinate tables (and figures) of task-evoked activations. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (causal attribution/mentalizing) in healthy adults. The sample consists of 20 healthy adults aged 18–41 (meets age/sample criterion). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task analyses (ANOVA, contrasts vs baseline, conjunctions) with thresholding and FWE-corrected results and figures/tables, and describes these whole-brain results in the text (meets whole-brain reporting criterion). Clinical scales are ancillary and healthy-group results are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of vocal versus non-vocal sound processing, which the authors frame as socially relevant (voice processing/social communication). Participants are healthy adults within the 18–65 range (Experiment 1: n=13, ages 21–41; Experiment 2: n=18, ages 18–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps (vocal > non-vocal contrasts) with statistical thresholds described and displayed in figures. Thus it satisfies the social-related fMRI task requirement, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task results. Resting-state analyses are supplementary and do not prevent inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating interpersonal synchrony and affiliative responses using a task (‘bexting’) that engages social cognition and affiliation. Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–25) and the fMRI analyses report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (ANOVA and voxelwise correlations) with cluster-level correction; results are described in the text and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Study used task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (modified Cyberball) in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 24.1). The paper reports both ROI-based MVPA and an exploratory whole-brain searchlight analysis with group-level, whole-brain corrected results (significant STS coordinates reported), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked group-level maps. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5; I6 is also satisfied because whole-brain results are reported as MNI coordinates and described in text.

This is an fMRI study using a social task (modified Cyberball) probing social-evaluative exclusion — directly relevant to social processing. The sample comprises healthy adults (20 men, 20 women; mean age 27.8), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., EX>IN, PG EX>FG IN) with voxelwise FWE correction and provides tables of peak coordinates and cluster sizes. Whole-brain results are clearly presented in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult whole-brain task activation maps).

This is an empirical fMRI study of Theory of Mind (a social cognition task) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=20, ages 22–56). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation results for the healthy group (within-group ToM vs. random-motion contrast), with corrected voxelwise findings presented in tables and figures. All applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: fMRI social-related task; I4: healthy adult participants with separate reporting; I5: whole-brain group-level task maps reported; I6: results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses fMRI during an emotional sentence attribution task tied to social cognition (meets I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (meets I4). However, the paper does not present an unambiguous, whole-brain, group-level task activation map that is explicitly and separately reported for the healthy/control group (I5 not met). The reported results are a main effect of task (across groups), between-group contrasts (CON > PAT), and a task×group interaction identifying regions where controls > patients for EMO–GRAM; there is no clearly reported unmasked, within-controls whole-brain EMO>GRAM map or table of healthy-group coordinates identified as a standalone healthy-group task effect. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures described).

The study reports an event-related fMRI investigation of understanding others' mental states (false-belief/theory-of-mind task), which is a social-related task. Participants were healthy adults (n=34; ages 20–28) with no psychiatric/neurological history. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation contrasts (ROMS vs. CTRL) with statistical maps, coordinate tables, and ROI analyses supplementing whole-brain results. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults with whole-brain group results). No exclusion criteria are met.

The paper reports task-based fMRI during moral reasoning (a social-cognition task), includes a healthy adult control group (N=28, ages 18–55) with results reported separately, and provides group-level, whole-brain one-sample analyses for the healthy control group (Moral vs BL) with FWE-corrected maps/tables/figures. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of social cognition (eye-gaze/intention processing), satisfying the social-related task requirement. It includes a neurologically normal healthy adult comparison group (n=9; mean age ~23.4, range within 18–65) with results reported separately. The manuscript provides group-level, whole-brain random-effects statistical maps and reports stereotaxic coordinates (Table 1) and figures for the healthy/control group (i.e., unmasked within-group task effects), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for the healthy group are clearly described in text, figures, and tables. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (20 participants, ages ~35) that used a social-related task (viewing faces of political candidates) addressing perception/understanding of others. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical analyses (FLAME), thresholding and cluster-corrected maps, tables of coordinates, and figures showing task effects and group contrasts. Full article text (methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses fMRI in a social-related task (biological motion perception) and includes a healthy adult sample, but it does not report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group within this paper. fMRI results and whole-brain activation maps are presented for the single patient (SL) only; comparisons to ‘healthy participants’ are made by reference to prior work rather than by reporting an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group map in the present article. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported). No exclusion criteria from the list are directly met. Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of charitable donation decisions (social/moral decision-making), involving healthy adult participants (n=19; mean age 28.2) and a task that probes social-related constructs (altruism, attachment/aversion to societal causes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and voxelwise contrasts (e.g., mesolimbic, orbitofrontal, anterior PFC activations) with reported thresholds and cluster criteria; coordinates and tables are referenced in the text/supporting information. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (task, subjects, image acquisition/analysis), Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (race perception/trustworthiness), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 18–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Black>White) and second-level covariate analyses with tables and peak coordinates, and describes PPI connectivity alongside whole-brain results. Thus it meets criteria for a social-related fMRI task, appropriate healthy adult sample, and provides whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (reported with coordinates).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (recall of self- and other-referential relationship episodes) in healthy adults (final sample n=35). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts (self-relevant>control, other>control) with cluster inference (FDR-corrected) and tables/figures of significant clusters. Results are clearly reported for the healthy/control group. Reporting includes voxelwise whole-brain analyses and coordinate tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for whole-brain task fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study that uses social-related tasks (empathic and forgivability judgements), satisfying the review topic. The sample comprises ten volunteers described as study participants (healthy adults), meeting the sample requirement for a healthy adult group. The abstract reports group-level brain activations (e.g., left superior frontal gyrus, orbitofrontal gyrus, precuneus, etc.), indicating whole-brain task-evoked results are reported for the healthy group. Results are described in text/tables (activation loci), so whole-brain evidence is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (passive viewing of faces vs objects) and includes a healthy adult sample (21 adults age 18–37). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (faces>objects) with voxelwise results and tables of coordinates (Table 3) describing whole-brain effects and regression of activation against age; FFA group metrics are reported separately for adults in Table 2. Whole-brain results are reported for the healthy sample and provided in figures/tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, task-evoked maps from the healthy group. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s inclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (the study reports resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses without any task-evoked healthy-group whole-brain activation maps) and E5 (participants are children/adolescents, age range 6.5–18.7, with no healthy adult subgroup aged 18–65). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a task fMRI study of social-related processing — it uses resting-state fMRI), I4 (no healthy adult sample 18–65; sample consists of male children/adolescents and clinical ASD group), I5/I6 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for a healthy adult group). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (joint attention/theory-of-mind) using a task in which participants viewed an avatar’s gaze to occluded body/place images, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adults age 20–31 with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (body>place and place>body contrasts), figures of whole-brain maps, and a table of activation coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only groups) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

The study uses task-based fMRI to examine perception and anticipation of an opponent’s body actions, which maps onto the ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’ construct (I3). Participants are healthy adult players (recreational to international), meeting the sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and presents contrasts (e.g., shots–mctrl), cluster peaks in tables/figures, and ROI analyses based on independent whole-brain results, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only reporting, and subjects are adults). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI experiment probing social-related processing: participants judged meaning (social/semantic) versus physical properties of LEGO models, and contrasts probe self/other and collective/individual effects (social cognition constructs). Sample consists of healthy adults (n=25, mean age 24). Analyses report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results using SPM8 with random-effects second-level tests; results are presented with peak coordinates, tables and figures and corrected thresholds. Thus the paper provides healthy-group, whole-brain task-evoked activations relevant to social processing and satisfies the inclusion criteria below.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults. The task probes social cognition (legal responsibility and punishment judgments — perception and understanding of others), satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=20 analyzed; age range 18–45), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts (whole-brain main effects and whole-brain contrasts with Talairach coordinates and t-values; tables/regions described), satisfying I5 and acceptable reporting per I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results (ROI and whole-brain analyses), and discussion, allowing assessment of criteria; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social-perception task (dynamic interacting shapes) in a healthy adult sample (n=28 women, ages within 18–65). The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and thresholding procedures (permutation testing, TFCE) and describes baseline and drug-condition whole-brain contrasts and correlations. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (face-based trustworthiness judgments with feedback), includes a healthy younger adult group (ages 20–33) meeting the 18–65 requirement, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level ANOVA and whole-brain results, with tables/figures reporting activations). Whole-brain results are clearly described and reported (ANOVA, contrasts, tables/figures), satisfying reporting requirements. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

Provided ‘full text’ is a cookie/privacy preference page only; core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is not present. Unable to verify key inclusion criteria: I3 (use of fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (presence and reporting of a healthy adult group 18–65), and I5/I6 (reporting of group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps). No exclusion criteria can be positively identified from the truncated content. Exclude pending retrieval of the full article; recommend obtaining the full text to reassess eligibility.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an emotional face discrimination task (social processing of others’ expressions), in a sample of 38 healthy adults (mean age 27.5), satisfying the sample criterion. It provides a second-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise group contrast (FACES>OBJECTS) with SPM results, cluster statistics, figures (SPM t-maps), and VOI analyses described in the text and supplementary material. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map), and I6 (results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. Inclusion criteria applied: I3,I4,I5,I6. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (joint attention) and reports results for a healthy control group, fulfilling I3 and I4. However, the reported fMRI results are analyzed primarily using small-volume (ROI) corrections focused on five a priori ROIs; the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (only ROI/SVC results and ROI peaks are reported). Therefore it fails to meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group. It meets inclusion criteria I3 (task-based fMRI of social perception) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). However, task-related analyses are ROI-based rather than whole-brain, so it violates exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (reports group/interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition: participants (N=20, healthy adults aged 18–27) performed a task eliciting thoughts about others’ mental states (mentalizing), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain analyses (searchlight MVPA, network-level analyses, one-sample random-effects t tests, whole-brain univariate maps, cluster correction via Monte Carlo/3dClustSim) and presents tables/figures and supplementary tables of results, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 — the paper reports between-group contrasts (controls > schizophrenia) and pooled/main effects but does not clearly present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map identified as coming from the healthy/control group in the provided full text. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 — uses fMRI during a social-related task (irony comprehension/social communication); I4 — includes a healthy adult control group reported separately alongside patients. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — the manuscript as provided does not clearly report at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map explicitly labelled as the healthy/control group (results for the control group are only referenced as previously published, and within-paper results emphasize between-group contrasts). I6 not applicable because no clear healthy-group whole-brain map is included in text/tables/supplementary material presented here. Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false (core article content present). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to provide the required healthy-group whole-brain activation map, triggering E4.

The study uses HCP task fMRI including a social cognition task and reports analyses on healthy adult participants (n=493; training/validation/testing split drawn from healthy HCP subjects), satisfying the sample requirement. The paper reports group-level task-evoked activation patterns derived via GLM (e.g., mean WM evoked activation patterns in Fig. 9b and GLM-derived activation similarity analyses) and sensitivity analyses that identify whole-brain task-related regions for social cognition (e.g., superior temporal sulcus, temporo-parietal junction, prefrontal cortex). These are presented as group-level voxelwise activation maps/figures derived from the healthy cohort, meeting the whole-brain reporting requirement. Therefore the manuscript meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (maps/figures reported). Full text appears to contain introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete).

Inclusion criteria met: I3 and I4 (task-based fMRI of an interactive social Domino game; includes a healthy adult TD group, ages 18–34). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map (e.g., an unmasked show>no-show voxelwise contrast) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Analyses are reported at the ICA component spatial-map level and component beta-weights with group comparisons/interactions rather than a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies (reports mainly group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

The study reports fMRI data collected during a live verbal social interaction task (speech/listening/imagination) involving healthy adult participants (22 women, mean age ~27). Group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise second-level analyses (one-tailed t-tests) are reported for talking, listening and imagining, with cluster-thresholding and results presented in text/figures/supplementary tables. The task is clearly social communication-related. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for task relevance, healthy adult sample, and provision of whole-brain task-evoked maps.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (social reflection: Self and Other judgments vs affect labeling), satisfying I3. The sample consists of 22 healthy adult participants (mean age 37.4, range within 18–65) meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (cortical surface–based) task-evoked activation for the SR>AL contrast, with cluster-corrected results, figures (e.g., Fig.1B) and tables (Table 2) documenting voxel/vertex-wise effects from the healthy sample, meeting I5 and I6. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Thus the study qualifies for inclusion.

This fMRI study tested facial color processing (a form of social communication/perception of others) using task-evoked BOLD responses to natural vs. bluish faces in healthy adults (N=25, mean age 25.2). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (natural-colored face vs. natural-colored scrambled image) and presents group-level activations (figures and table) used to define ROIs. Thus it meets: I3 (social-related task: facial color/social perception), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task contrast reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making (ultimatum game) in healthy adult participants (10 male volunteers, ages 23–28). The paper reports whole-brain offline analyses across subjects (leave-one-subject-out cross-subject SVM) and lists discriminating volumes with MNI coordinates and thresholding (Tables/figures), satisfying the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task-evoked map. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and clearly reports results for the healthy control group. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain evidence reported), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly described).

This study used event-related fMRI while healthy adult participants (n=16 scanned, 14 included in analysis; ages 18–30) performed a social-evaluative task (trustworthiness judgments vs age judgments). The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain analyses (SPMs), with coordinates and tables of activations (including small-volume corrected results and whole-brain contrasts), and describes task-evoked effects for the healthy control group. Thus it provides whole-brain task activation maps from healthy adults during a social-related task and meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalising/theory of mind) in healthy adults. It reports task-based fMRI with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level random-effects ANOVAs), thresholded to whole-brain-corrected significance and summarized in Table 1 and figures (contrasts such as mentalising>factual and parametric modulation). Participants are healthy adults within 18–65 (Experiment 2 mean age 22; Experiment 1 range 18–60). Whole-brain results are clearly reported in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that implemented an interactive, social gaze-based task (joint and non-joint attention) during whole-brain fMRI acquisition in healthy adult participants (n=24; age range 20–34), satisfying the sample requirement. Group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., self > other; JA > NJA) are reported with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics from second-level analyses (reported in text/figures), meeting the whole-brain results criterion. Although many inferences used small-volume correction for a priori ROIs, group-level voxelwise contrasts for the healthy sample are explicitly reported. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study examining integration of speaker characteristics (a social-communication/self-other inference process) during auditory sentence comprehension. It includes a separate healthy control group of adults (age 18–39) reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and within-group contrasts for the control group (with coordinates, figures and tables), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain task effects, adult sample within range, empirical data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using an ecologically valid social interaction task (adapted Taylor Aggression Paradigm) presenting opponents' facial expressions; sample comprises healthy adult males (32 included in analyses, mean age 23.3); the paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (angry > neutral) with cluster-wise FWE correction and presents tables/figures of whole-brain results. Thus it satisfies fMRI social processing, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the EmpaToM task that probes social cognition (empathy and Theory of Mind) during task performance. The sample includes 178 healthy adult participants (mean age 40.9, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (emotional vs neutral videos for empathy; ToM vs non-ToM questions/videos for mentalizing) entered into random-effects one-sample t-tests and presents activation results in figures/tables. Resting-state and DCM analyses are supplemental but do not replace the reported task-evoked whole-brain maps. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (third-party punishment/attribution of intentions) relevant to perception and understanding of others (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=26; mean age 26±5.7) within the 18–65 range (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical analyses (GLM, random effects multisubject ANOVA) with thresholding (q[FDR]<0.05) and reports Talairach coordinates and figures for activations (R TPJ, R AI), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing using the DISC social-attribution task in a sample of healthy adults (N=22, ages 18–25). The study reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., FRIENDS > WATCH and FRIENDS > SIZE) with appropriate voxelwise/statistical thresholding and correction (cluster thresholding and permutation testing with TFCE/FWE), clearly describing results from the healthy/control group. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is not available in the provided materials (only abstract/metadata). From the abstract, the study uses fMRI with a social-attribution task in healthy young adults (satisfies I3 and I4). However, I cannot verify whether the paper reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy/control group (I5), because full methods/results are not accessible. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract alone. Because the full text is incomplete and I5 cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded pending access to full article.

This is an empirical fMRI study of face processing (a social-related task: perception/understanding of others) that includes a healthy adult control group (CA group; mean age 31 years) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and displays group activation maps (e.g., Figure 3: mean z-score images for CA controls, P<0.05 corrected) and describes voxelwise ANOVA and correction procedures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 21–40) using a social cognition task (Implicit Association Test with politicians’ faces and names) probing social-related processing (attitudes toward others). The paper reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects, FDR correction and voxelwise tables/figures), clearly from the healthy/control group, with reported contrasts and coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (dynamic and static facial-expression perception), includes a healthy adult control group (N=13, ages within 18–65) whose results are reported separately, and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps for the control group (simple main effect of dynamic vs. static faces with whole-brain correction). Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6. The full text provided contains background, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-perception task (passive viewing of biological vs scrambled point-light displays), includes a healthy adult group (n=48, ages 20–35), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., biological>scrambled; Sex×Condition ANOVA) with tables/figures and cluster-correction details. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

Although this study uses fMRI with a social face-processing task (fearful faces) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=19, age ~32), it does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map from the healthy/control group alone. The paper mainly reports group results across all participants and between-group contrasts (controls vs TLE) and ROI-based percent signal change for controls. Because there is no clearly identified whole-brain, within-group healthy-control task map (unmasked) presented, it fails exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Therefore it must be excluded.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a social gaze (face/gaze-shift) stimulus during a task that probes social-related processing and action control. Sample: 23 healthy adults aged 21–37 (within 18–65). Analysis: voxelwise, whole-brain second-level random-effects SPM analyses are reported (main effects, interactions, cluster-level corrected maps and coordinates reported in text/tables/figures). The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria for whole-brain task-evoked activations in healthy adults during a social task. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a social-attribution (Theory of Mind) task (People vs Bumper) and reports results for a healthy adult control group. The paper includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (People - Bumper) and presents group maps and ROI tables for the control (CON) group separately from the recovered-anorexia (RAN) group, satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task effect. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, healthy adults within 18–65, and original empirical data). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self-reference vs reference to others) in healthy adults (n=110, ages 19–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses with voxelwise contrasts (e.g., SR>OR, SR+OR>baseline) and FWE-corrected statistical maps and tables, and clearly identifies results from the healthy sample. Although the study also includes effective connectivity analyses (DCM), it additionally provides whole-brain task activation maps. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study directly examines self-referential (social) processing and includes a healthy adult control group (n=15, ages 31–58). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and contrasts for the healthy control group (within-group referential task vs baseline and task contrasts are described and shown), with statistical thresholds and cluster correction. The task operationalizes perception/understanding of self (a social-related construct). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria.

The full text reports an fMRI experiment using social/empathy-induction traffic-awareness videos (social-related task). Sample: 20 healthy adult males (ages 20–28), meeting the 18–65 healthy adult requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (CV>NV) with FWE correction (p<0.05) and peak coordinates/tables/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This study uses fMRI with a social-related Theory-of-Mind task (I3) and includes a healthy control group of adults within the 18–65 range (I4). However, the paper reports analyses constrained to pre-specified ROI masks and presents primarily between-group contrasts (ALS>HC) without reporting an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails to meet the whole-brain healthy-group evidence requirement (I5). Exclusion criteria E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (reports mainly between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study investigates impression formation (perception and understanding of others), uses a task-based fMRI paradigm in healthy adult participants (20 males, ages 19–31), and reports both ROI and an exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analysis (whole-brain voxelwise ANOVA with results shown in table/figures). Thus it meets the review objective and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy sample.

This is an fMRI study of laughter perception (social communication) in healthy adults (n=18, mean age 26). Tasks explicitly probe social/emotional processing (explicit emotional classification; implicit bout counting) and thus address social-related constructs (social communication; perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain contrasts and conjunctions reported, tables of activations, ROI and whole-brain results), clearly identified as coming from the healthy participant group. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (thinking about interpersonal interaction verbs) with both high-functioning autism and age/IQ-matched healthy adult control participants. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain within-group GLM contrasts and SPM results for the control (healthy) group (e.g., within-group social-interactions vs fixation maps, figures and tables described), and also provides multivariate/factor analyses performed separately for each group. Healthy adult controls (young adults) are analysed and reported separately. The study is not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and participants fall within the 18–65 range. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social cooperation using a one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma (social task) with whole-brain task-based analyses reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: PD game/cooperation), I4 (healthy adult sample; final analyzed N=18, mean age 21.04, within 18–65), I5 (group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses reported with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and tables of coordinates), I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate tables/contrast descriptions). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not an only between-group contrast, participants within age range, and this is empirical data. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental XLSX references do not prevent treating the core article as complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (action understanding) in healthy adults (N=19, ages 18–32). The task is social-related (why/how/what observation goals) and uses task-evoked, group-level voxelwise analyses. Although main analyses were restricted to an a priori mask of mirror neuron and mentalizing systems, the manuscript explicitly notes that details about the mask and whole-brain results are provided in the Supplemental Methods, and group-level random-effects analyses were conducted and reported (cluster coordinates/tables and figures). Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I5), and acceptability of coordinate/figure reporting (I6).

The study uses task-based fMRI to examine perception of biological motion (point-light walkers), which falls under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=13, mean age 28.2), meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (canonical vs. scrambled biological motion) with corrected voxelwise results and provides MNI coordinates and cluster tables/figures. Thus it satisfies the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines facial emotion recognition (a social-communication/perception task) in healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain results, but the reported whole-brain maps are presented as between-group (LDA > HDA and HDA > LDA) contrasts between two healthy subgroups. The paper does not present an unmasked, within-group or main-effect whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from a healthy/control group independent of between-group contrasts. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample, ages within 18–65), and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clearly reported group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map for the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (observation of risk-taking vs safe actions) that probes social cognition/emotional processing. Sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18.1–22.8 (within 18–65) with screening for neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (risk-taking vs safe) analyzed with SPM and presents peak coordinates and cluster results (MNI/Talairach), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (passive viewing of positive social stimuli: social interactions, human faces, erotic scenes) meeting the review objective. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=14, mean age 28.2) reported separately from the clinical (depressed) group. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise (repeated-measures ANOVAs), and results are reported as cluster tables and figures with coordinates and cluster volumes (Tables 3–5, Figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked results. The full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-fMRI study of social cognition (empathy) using dynamic multimodal social stimuli (satisfies I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=24, mean age ~35) with results reported separately (satisfies I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects GLM, cluster-corrected thresholds) and within-group T-contrasts for each participant group, with whole-brain results presented in figures/tables (satisfies I5 and I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental materials are referenced but not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an fMRI study of affective theory-of-mind (social cognition) in healthy adults (n=21 analyzed, mean age ~23.7), using a task involving emotional facial expressions during ToM judgments. The paper reports group-level, within-subject whole-brain task contrasts (EFE > no EFE and whole-brain tables/figures and ROI analyses) clearly identified from the healthy/control sample. Whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures and described in the text. Thus it satisfies the fMRI social-task requirement, healthy adult sample, and provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (tables/figures) meeting inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range age) apply.

This study used task fMRI of a social cognition paradigm (Reading the Mind in the Eyes) so I3 is satisfied, and it includes a healthy control group of young adults assessed with SCID/CIDI so I4 is satisfied. However, the paper reports mainly between-group (high-risk vs low-risk) voxelwise comparisons and does not present or describe an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map (or main effect) for the healthy/control group alone. Therefore it fails to meet I5 and must be excluded per E4 (studies that report only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This is an fMRI experiment with healthy adult participants (mean age 24.6) using a social task (observed eye contact and gaze-following). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with statistical thresholds and coordinate tables/figures (e.g., EC > AG, Cong > Incong, interaction contrasts), clearly from the healthy sample. Thus it satisfies the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI activation in healthy adults and meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are violated.

This fMRI study used a social-related task (explicit labeling of others’ brief emotional facial expressions), scanned healthy adult participants (N=50, ages 18–29), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group-level contrasts and regression results (with cluster-level FWE correction) clearly identified for the healthy sample. Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an interactive social (mentalizing) paradigm (Prisoner’s Dilemma) addressing attachment/social cognition. Sample: 164 healthy adult participants (age range 19–35) with results reported for the healthy group. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (contrast task > control) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; activation peaks/coordinates and clusters are provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening.

This fMRI study uses a social facial-emotion task (I3) and includes a separate healthy adult control group (I4). However, the paper reports only between-group (VCFS vs controls) whole-brain contrasts (Table 1 and text) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map or statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (and thus I6 is not satisfied for a healthy-group map). Consequently the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

While the study uses task-based fMRI of a social interaction (multi-round trust game) and includes a separate healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met), it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain within-group (healthy/control) task activation map. The only whole-brain voxelwise results presented are exploratory between-group contrasts (control > patients) rather than an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the paper must be excluded for failing to meet I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task map). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study that directly manipulated social information (trustworthiness judgments) versus nonsocial information during an n-back task. Participants were healthy adults (mean age 22; final imaging N=14), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster correction and tables of peak coordinates (Tables 2–4), clearly identifying healthy-group task effects. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for fMRI social-task data, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task activation reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, non-healthy-only groups, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are violated.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (real-time mutual eye contact) in healthy adults. The task is explicitly social (mutual gaze/eye-blink entrainment) and uses functional MRI (hyperscanning fMRI) with task conditions (LIVE vs REPLAY). The sample is healthy adults (final analyzed N=30 participants; mean age ~21.7 years), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (LIVE > REPLAY) with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates, and describes whole-brain interbrain synchronization and GLM results in the text/tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

Meets inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI with dynamic happy and fearful facial expressions (a social/emotion recognition task); (I4) includes healthy adult participants (control group and non-psychotic familial-risk participants in early twenties, within 18–65); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the groups (figures and text describe within-group activation/deactivation maps thresholded Z>2.3, cluster p<0.05); (I6) whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, whole-brain maps for healthy groups are provided, task-based activations (not only connectivity) are reported. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates social communication (speech act comprehension: Naming vs. Requesting) in healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 18–41). It reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., “Request > Naming”) with FDR-corrected results and provides coordinates/tables and figures, clearly identifying effects from the healthy/control sample. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This fMRI study of social processing (watching a TV episode) includes a healthy adult control group and reports whole-brain analyses, so it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported). However, the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. The authors report (a) a whole-brain map collapsed across all subjects and (b) between-group contrasts (NT > ASD) and ROI-based analyses, but I find no unmasked, whole-brain NT (healthy-only) task activation map or contrast described as coming solely from the healthy group. Therefore I5 is not met. This triggers exclusion criterion E4 (studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of emotion regulation using angry faces (a social stimulus) with healthy adult participants (N=60, age range 18–57). The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Observe-angry > Observe-neutral; Decrease vs Observe-angry) with coordinates, tables, and figures describing healthy-group effects. Resting-state analyses are additional but the study includes task-evoked whole-brain results for the healthy sample. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only, sample within 18–65, and empirical). Hence it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 21–32) that investigates personal prayer vs controls as a social-cognitive task. The contrasts probe theory-of-mind/social cognition (e.g., Personal Praying > Wishes to Santa; Personal Praying > Lord’s Prayer). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (tables of coordinates, thresholded at p<0.05 FDR, with MNI/Talairach coordinates and figures). The paper therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements for an fMRI social-related task in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group activation maps/coordinates.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults using two social-cognitive tasks (emotional perspective-taking and emotion attribution) that probe social perception/understanding. The sample is healthy adults (n≈120; ages 18–35). The authors report group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (emotion perspective-taking > shape matching; emotion attribution > gender matching) and whole-brain regression analyses with coordinates and cluster statistics (FWE and voxelwise thresholds), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task-evoked maps.
