No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supporting methods).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age ~31) that uses the Ultimatum Game, a social economic exchange task probing social decision-making and cooperation. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects ANOVA, conjunction analyses, whole-brain parametric regressions) with coordinates and corrected statistics, clearly from the healthy participant groups. Methods and results provide whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate tables. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

Full text is incomplete (only a cookie/website notice provided), so core article content (methods, participants, results) cannot be verified. Therefore I cannot confirm any inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be confirmed: I3 (uncertain whether an fMRI social-related task is reported in healthy adults), I4 (uncertain whether a healthy adult group 18–65 is included and reported separately), I5 (no accessible whole-brain group-level task maps for healthy group), I6 (no supplementary/tables/figures available to verify whole-brain results). Exclusion criteria met: none can be confidently applied given missing full text. Because the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded from the review pending access to the full article.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (attribute framing/self and reflected perspectives) in healthy adults (ages 19–41). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., positive vs negative frames, frame-consistent vs inconsistent) with coordinate tables/figures and thresholding procedures. Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Cannot confirm that the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy adult sample (I5 not verifiable). The study likely meets I3 (fMRI during social-related/self-regulation goal processing) and I4 (healthy adult participants), but without full methods/results we cannot verify whole-brain results or exclude ROI-only reporting. Therefore excluded due to incomplete full text and inability to confirm inclusion criterion I5.

This fMRI study meets inclusion criteria I3 (task is a social-related dyadic conversation involving perception/understanding of others) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, n=14, ages within 18–65). However, the paper does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. The reported whole-brain results are for combined groups and for between-group contrasts/interactions; ROI extractions and parameter estimates for the control group are provided, but no standalone healthy-group whole-brain statistical map (one-sample/group-level map) is clearly presented. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) is met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=12, mean age 26) that investigates perception and understanding of others’ actions/effort (social-related processing: force perception during action observation). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (SPM whole-brain and SUIT cerebellar analyses) with thresholds, cluster coordinates, figures, and conjunction analyses clearly attributed to the healthy group. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task: perception/understanding of others), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are not required for eligibility.

This paper uses fMRI to study processing of faces (neutral and fearful), a social perceptual task (meets I3). The sample consists of six healthy observers (meets I4). However, the reported analyses are ROI-based (subject-specific ROIs and ROI time courses and correlations) and the manuscript does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or contrast for the healthy group in the main text (no unmasked whole-brain statistical map or coordinate-based group map is reported for the main task). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis objective. It uses task-based fMRI during social-related processing (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluation of the self), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults (final N=31, ages 19–24), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (contrasts and a whole-brain multiple regression with cluster-level FWE correction), with coordinates/tables/figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Tables/Figures, and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65).

This study uses task-based fMRI of social reward (meets I3) and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures (meets I6). Participants are aged 18–21 (within adult range), but the sample is a mixed clinical/healthy sample and all reported whole-brain results and regressions are from the combined sample rather than from a clearly identified healthy/control group. The paper does not provide an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map explicitly identified as coming from a healthy adult control group. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (no accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (naturalistic movie viewing that elicits social cognition and social interaction processing), includes a healthy adult sample (n=34, mean age 22.2), and reports whole-brain voxelwise reverse-correlation results with corrected statistics and visualization (whole-brain χ2 tests, Bonferroni correction; Figure 3). Group-level healthy-participant effects are clearly described. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group only, ages within 18–65, empirical data present). Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be included.

The study is an fMRI experiment involving social communication tasks (viewing, imitating, and producing facial expressions and social hand gestures), indicating social-related processing (I3). The text describes participants (healthy adult participants rather than clinical groups), meeting the sample requirement (I4). The paper reports neural activation locations and condition differences (e.g., IPL and frontal operculum activations and significant differences in locations), indicating group-level whole-brain task-evoked results are reported (I5). Results are clearly described in the text, consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, resting-state only, non-empirical) are evident from the provided information.

This is an fMRI hyperscanning study of joint attention—a social interaction task—using task-based fMRI in healthy adult samples (discovery n=26, replication n=50; ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain spatial component maps derived from group ICA and tests component task associations (INT vs NoINT) with group statistics (ANOVA/F statistics) and presents spatial maps/figures (and supplementary tables) identifying components (e.g., rTPJ) associated with interaction. Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps (reported in figures/SI) for the healthy participants and links neural measures to behavioral social-network measures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not exclusively resting-state or connectivity-only without whole-brain task maps, includes healthy adult within-range group, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study of social/empathy processing (viewing human and animal suffering), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=60; ages 18–60) with within-group and between-group task contrasts. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample/paired t-tests, ANOVA interaction), corrected results (FWE) and cluster coordinates, as well as conjunction and masking procedures; results are presented with MNI coordinates and statistical thresholds. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, fMRI acquisition, analysis), Results, and Discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-state-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, task-based EEG-fMRI study of minimal-group social processing (group categorization) in healthy adults (N=20 analyzed; mean age 23.4). The experiment uses functional MRI concurrent with EEG during a social task addressing affiliation and perception of others. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI analyses (thresholding described; cluster-level FWE correction; activations and MNI coordinates presented in Table 1 and figures) linking BOLD activity (mPFC, STS/TPJ) to EEG components. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of verbal irony implicating Theory of Mind and social communication (social cognition). Sample: twenty healthy adult participants (mean age 22) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (Ironic > Literal) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FDR correction and provides coordinates and ROI analyses. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported as coordinates and described in text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s inclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (the study uses resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses and does not report any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps for a healthy adult group) and E5 (participants are adolescents aged 11–18, outside the 18–65 adult range; no separate healthy adult subgroup is reported). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use task-based fMRI; it uses resting-state fcMRI), I4 (no healthy adult sample 18–65; the control group are adolescents), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from a healthy/control adult group), I6 (not applicable because no task whole-brain results are reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (repeated public good game probing social tie formation/other-regarding preferences). Scanned sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=25 analyzed; mean age ~22.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FSL GLM, cluster-wise FWE correction) with MNI coordinates and tables/figures. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered.

This is an empirical dual-fMRI (hyperscanning) study using a social interactive task (cooperation/competition) in healthy adult participants (n=38, mean age 22.4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses: spatial maps derived from group ICA (gICA) and associated task-related time-course comparisons (multiple regression and paired t-tests), plus group-level inter-subject correlation (ISC) results and thresholded component maps (figures/Tables/Supplement). These constitute whole-brain, task-evoked group results for the healthy sample. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

This is a double-blind, placebo-controlled fMRI study in 55 healthy adult males (mean age ~24.9) that used an explicit social-related task (extended Hariri face/scene matching including erotic/attachment and fearful social scenes), satisfying the social-processing construct. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (whole-brain FWE-corrected maps and contrasts are described and shown in figures/tables, with ROI analyses supplementary), clearly coming from the healthy participant group. Reporting includes whole-brain results in the main text and figures (and supplementary material), meeting the acceptable reporting criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion requirements for the review: (1) It uses task-based fMRI during an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma, a social decision-making task (I3). (2) The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=20 males, ages 21–37) with results reported for the healthy group (I4). (3) The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (one-sample t tests, flexible factorial analyses, MDMA vs placebo contrasts) with cluster-level FWE correction and tabulated activations (I5). (4) Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in the text (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROIs only, are not solely connectivity/resting-state, and are not only between-group or non-healthy samples. The supplied full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a social motor response (social inclusion/exclusion) task and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in healthy adult participants. The sample consists of 18 healthy adults (mean age 42 ± 12), satisfying the adult healthy sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain random-effects analyses with FDR whole-brain correction and displays tables/figures of activations (e.g., dorsal anterior cingulate, frontal operculum, ventral striatum), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided content is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range sample) are met.

This is an fMRI study of empathy for pain (social processing: perception/understanding of others) using a task that contrasts pain vs no-pain stimuli. The sample includes healthy adult participants, including a younger group aged 20–30 (within the 18–65 range). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., pain>no pain and pain>baseline) with voxelwise results (FWE-corrected maps, tables of coordinates, and NeuroVault statistical maps). The study is not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, or patient-only analyses. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults investigating social-related processing.

This is an fMRI study that implemented a social-related task (evaluative judgments of guilt and embarrassment; Theory of Mind/social cognition), recruited a healthy adult sample (N=19, ages within 18–65), and reported group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (random-effects contrasts G−N, E−N, G−E, E−G) with coordinate tables and figures. Whole-brain statistical thresholds and extent criteria are described, and regression analyses with group-level maps are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults. It used task-based fMRI during a social/competitive matching-pennies paradigm involving human and non-human agents (social-related processing/mentalizing). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=16, ages 18–25). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise GLM group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise thresholding (p<.001) and cluster-level FWE correction across the whole brain; results are presented in figures and tables with coordinates. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (task-based fMRI of social processing, healthy adult sample, whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, and appropriately reported maps/tables). No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion(s) met: E2. Inclusion(s) met: I3, I4. Inclusion(s) not met: I5. The paper reports an fMRI visual perspective-taking task (social cognition) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3, I4). However, the Methods state that second-level activation analyses were restricted to predefined prefrontal ROIs and results are reported within these ROIs; no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map or healthy-group whole-brain contrast/coordinate table is reported for the healthy/control group. Although exploratory whole-brain functional connectivity was performed, this does not satisfy the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded for failing I5 and meeting exclusion criterion E2.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It used task-based fMRI to probe social/affiliative processing (mothers viewing own vs. unfamiliar child and dog images) (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult women aged 22–45 with exclusions for psychiatric or major medical conditions, satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., own child vs. fixation, own dog vs. fixation, own child vs. own dog, own vs. unfamiliar) with cluster coordinates, t-values, and activation maps described in the text and figures, providing whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results for the healthy group (I5,I6). Although analyses used ROI masks and small-volume correction for a priori regions, whole-brain voxelwise GLM contrasts and coordinates are reported rather than only ROI-summary statistics, so the study is not limited by exclusion E2. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of co-speech gesture processing during naturalistic narrative comprehension, which falls under social communication/social-related processing. The sample comprises 20 healthy adult participants (ages 22–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., low_ID > high_ID; speech > gestures+speech; gestures+speech > speech; interaction effects) with coordinates, cluster extents, tables and figures, and multiple whole-brain statistical thresholds. It is empirical, not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, and reports healthy-group task effects. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used fMRI during a social-relevant task (face encoding/recognition) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the analyses are region-of-interest (right FFA) focused: individual localizer contrasts were used to define ROIs and subsequent encoding/recognition results are reported from the ROI. The paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (only single-subject localizer contrasts and ROI results). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain healthy-group results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E2.

This is an event-related fMRI study of empathy for others' pain (a social-related task: perception/understanding of others) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=13, mean age 33) reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and provides figures and tables of voxelwise activations and coordinates for the control group (within-group contrasts and main effects), not limited to ROIs. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This study meets I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related mentalizing task) and I4 (reports a healthy adult control group, n=33, ages 18–42). However, it does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. The only whole-brain analysis described is a between-group contrast (Controls > ASC). Therefore it falls under exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrast without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain map). Exclusion criteria met: E4.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an explicit social judgment (approachability) task (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group and reports their data separately alongside clinical groups (meets I4). The methods describe second-level within-group contrasts (social vs baseline/gender) for each group, and the manuscript and supplementary material report within-group whole-brain task activation results (meets I5 and I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

The paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (three experiments, N=25, N=65, N=178; Experiment 2 mean age 40.9) using a social cognition paradigm (EmpaToM) probing empathy and Theory of Mind, addressing social-related processing. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., empathy contrast, ToM contrast) with tables of activation peaks and figures; second-level one-sample t-tests and FWE-corrected thresholds are described. Behavioral and imaging results for the healthy/control samples are reported separately. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-based fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain task activation maps and coordinate tables.

This is an fMRI study of social processing: eye contact modulation of spontaneous mimicry (social perception/communication). Participants: 20 healthy adults (mean age 23), so sample meets the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., Congruent > Catch, Incongruent > Congruent, Direct > Averted, interaction), thresholded and cluster-level FWE-corrected, with results presented in Table 1 and Figures (coordinates reported). This is not an ROI-only or connectivity-only paper (although DCM is included, whole-brain task activations are reported). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task study explicitly investigating self-face recognition (a social-cognitive construct: Perception and Understanding of Self), using an event-related BOLD paradigm. Participants are healthy adults (12 right-handed males, mean age 19.36), meeting the 18–65 age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., unknown vs. scrambled, familiar vs. unknown, self vs. familiar) analyzed in SPM with thresholding and cluster reporting; results are presented in figures and tables of coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, age within range, empirical data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of prosocial decisions (family assistance), a clear social-related task (mentalizing, affiliation/attachment). Sample consists of 25 healthy young adults (Mage=20.2), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (Costly-Donation vs Noncostly-Reward) with tables of coordinates and corrected inference, and whole-brain regression and PPI analyses; results are reported for the healthy sample. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses task fMRI of dynamic face processing (social-related) and includes a healthy adult control group, but the reported whole-brain results are limited to between-group contrasts (patients vs controls). No unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map (controls’ within-group task effect) is reported in the text/tables; tables/figures show clusters for patient vs control differences. Therefore it fails the requirement for an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect (I5). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (imagined triadic interactions vs self/other/control), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=19, ages 18–35). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., triad > iron; triad > (self & other)) with whole-brain FWE-corrected thresholds and reports peak coordinates/tables and figures. Results for the healthy control group are clearly reported and not limited to ROI- or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for task relevance, sample, and whole-brain reporting.

The study is an fMRI investigation of empathy and perspective-taking (social cognition), meeting the review’s topic. Participants are healthy adults aged 21–31 (N=18), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Self vs Other, View-Pain vs View-No-Pain) with cluster- and peak-level FWE correction and tables/coordinates, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly presented (including conjunction analyses, time-course analyses, and ROI-corrected contrasts), and whole-brain findings are described in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met.

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of social interaction and reactive aggression using an interactive Taylor paradigm (social perception/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adult males (N=16, mean age 28.6), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. Analyses used SPM2 with random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise statistics reported (thresholds, conjunctions, coordinates, activation maps and tables) for group-level task effects (retaliation, watching opponent, anticipation), and ROI splits by psychopathy are secondary; whole-brain healthy-group results are clearly presented. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria for task-based social fMRI, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level reporting (coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This fMRI study used natural movie stimuli containing social communication (people talking/gesturing) and explicitly modeled responses to social-communication categories. Participants were healthy adults (n=6, ages within 18–65). The paper reports voxelwise encoding/modeling across cortex and projects category-selectivity (including social communication) onto cortical flatmaps and reports group-level analyses (e.g., group PCs, group cluster centers, and flatmap visualizations aggregated across subjects), which constitute whole-brain, group-level task-evoked voxelwise statistical maps for the healthy sample. Reporting appears in figures and text (and across subjects) rather than being limited to an ROI-only analysis. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (social communication construct analyzed), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps for the healthy group), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria are met. The full text provided appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a social/emotion-related task (facial affect matching) during fMRI, satisfying I3. The sample includes a clearly reported healthy adult comparison group (n=12, ages within 18–65), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses for the healthy group (within-group Emotion Match > Shape Match contrasts, tables of coordinates and figures), satisfying I5 and the reporting format requirement I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social processing in adults and includes a healthy/control (NT) group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The only whole-brain (searchlight) results are reported across all participants combined, and the paper's detailed healthy-group results are ROI-based (not whole-brain). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. This violates exclusion criterion E4 (no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Hence EXCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (self- and other-reflection; perceptions of self and close other), includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (21 HCs), and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy controls (contrasts self>semantic and other>semantic) with voxelwise/FWE-corrected results and figures/tables. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing using a pseudo-interactive joke task (action-outcome contingency), directly probing self/other social processing and reward. Sample: 38 healthy adult participants (ages 19–29) with analyses reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., SELF vs OTHER; action-outcome interaction) with cluster-level FWE correction, tables of coordinates, and figures—meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly probes social-related processing (images of social group interactions vs individuals) while participants imagined themselves in the situations. A healthy control group (n=29; adults ≈32 years) is reported separately and reported within-group (control) whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., group-positive vs group-neutral; group-negative vs group-neutral) with voxelwise coordinates and statistical thresholds, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results (control group main effects and contrasts), figures, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI social-processing study in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps/coordinates for the healthy/control group.

This is an empirical fMRI study (20 participants) that investigates integration of faces and voices — a social perceptual/communication task relevant to social processing. The abstract reports group-level voxelwise activation results using multiple statistical criteria (identifying regions such as hippocampus, occipital and temporal cortices) and PPI connectivity analyses. Thus the paper reports whole-brain task-evoked effects for a healthy participant group. No evidence that results are ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical. Based on the provided full-text information, all inclusion criteria for healthy adult fMRI task activation mapping appear satisfied.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social-related face-processing task and included a healthy adult control group, but it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The paper reports a whole-group (AS + NT) faces>houses whole-brain map (Table 1) and reports group-comparison contrasts (NT>AS) and ROI analyses of the amygdala for the control group, but no standalone, voxelwise whole-brain faces>houses (or equivalent) statistical map for the healthy/control group is presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4.

This fMRI study directly investigates perception of social cooperation (a social-related task) using task-based fMRI (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=19) reported separately from the patient group (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts for the healthy control group (e.g., C+ > C–, FDR-corrected, reported coordinates and figures) meeting whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper issues). Therefore the study should be included in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (perception/understanding of others) using a task contrasting social interactions (SI) versus non-social interactions (NSI) depicted with point-light displays, satisfying I3. The sample comprises 14 healthy adults (mean age 29.4), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses for the SI-NSI contrast with FDR-corrected results and lists peak voxels/clusters (Table 1; figures), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social gaze-following (a social-related task examining responses to in-group vs. out-group political faces), conducted in healthy adult participants (ages 18–36). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent) with cluster-level correction and provides tables and figures describing activated clusters across the brain (dorsal and ventral fronto-parietal networks, FEF, parietal, occipital regions). Results are reported for the healthy/control sample (no clinical groups). Thus it satisfies the review inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This empirical fMRI study acquired whole-brain functional data while healthy adult participants (N=23; ages 19–32) read a literary narrative and provided trial-by-trial suspense ratings. The task elicited activation in theory-of-mind/mentalizing areas (medial frontal cortex, temporo-parietal junction) and predictive-inference regions, i.e., constructs clearly relevant to ‘perception and understanding of others’ (social-related processing). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (SPM; cluster-level FWE correction), and activation tables/coordinates are provided; region-of-interest analyses were supplementary. Thus the paper meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps reported), and I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition (second-order Theory of Mind) task during BOLD fMRI (meets I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=25, ages 18–60) with results reported separately alongside the bipolar group (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task analyses (whole-brain contrasts and tables/figures of activations) and describes within-group activation patterns for controls (meets I5). Whole-brain results are presented in text, tables, and figures (acceptable per I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is an fMRI study of social attribution (self-responsibility and self-serving bias) using task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adult participants (12 neurologically healthy males, ages 20–51). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99; fixed-effects and follow-up random-effects ROI testing) with results presented as voxelwise statistical maps and coordinate tables. The task is clearly social-related (attribution of positive/negative social events). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this fMRI study used a healthy adult sample (N=46, ages 18–45) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (HA− > NTR) and coordinates, the experimental paradigm targets general emotional (negative) picture processing (IAPS) rather than an explicit social-related task (e.g., affiliation/attachment, social communication, mentalizing, or explicit perception/understanding of others). The manuscript focuses on emotion reactivity and fronto-limbic connectivity; while dmPFC has roles in social cognition, the task did not explicitly probe social processes. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (social-related task), and must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study uses fMRI of face processing (social-related task) and includes control subjects, but the full article is not available to verify whether at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group is reported. Because I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map) cannot be confirmed, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the abstract alone. Fulltext_incomplete is flagged to indicate inability to fully assess reporting of whole-brain results.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (mutual direct vs averted gaze in dynamic virtual characters) addressing social cognition/understanding of others, and includes a separate healthy adult control group. The manuscript provides whole-brain, group-level task activation results for the healthy/control group (within-group and whole-brain contrasts reported in text, tables, and figures), not only ROI analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, imaging, analysis), Results (behavioral and whole-brain and ROI imaging results for controls), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Meets inclusion criteria: (I3) Uses task-based fMRI probing social processing (Dynamic Social Gesture task contrasting social vs nonsocial gestures, actor-orientation, face-visibility); (I4) Reports a sample of healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age 21.41, range includes adults within 18–65); (I5) Presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (TFCE with permutation testing, reported in figures/tables and text); (I6) Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and supplementary tables. No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are reported. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (face perception with emotional and neutral faces) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=7, mean age 30 years) reported separately from the clinical Social Phobia group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task vs. rest contrasts and within-group deactivation maps for both groups, using whole-brain multiple-comparison correction (AlphaSim) and reporting clusters in DMN regions for the healthy group; these constitute qualifying whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked results. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, includes healthy adults, and is empirical).

The study uses task-based fMRI to probe evaluative judgments/self-referential processing (social cognition/theory of mind), includes a healthy adult control group (n=7, mean age 26.4 within 18–65) analyzed separately, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and coordinates for the control group (figures and tables). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (Narrative Experiment: N=41, ages 18–37; separate localizer group N=14). The task is social-related (empathy/Theory of Mind narratives and pain/localizer tasks). The paper includes group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (SnPM, corrected p<0.05), contrasts for pain vs control and condition-specific contrasts, and reports peak coordinates (Table 3) and whole-brain figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text (not truncated). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text is complete for screening purposes.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n≈36, ages ~21) using a social cognition task (viewing others in pain — perception/understanding of others/empathy). The manuscript includes whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses (pre-priming whole-brain FDR-corrected maps; post-priming whole-brain results reported) and provides coordinates/tables and ROI analyses. All inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results are described and reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (gaze-based joint attention) in healthy adults. Methods report fMRI data acquisition and a GLM group analysis (n=21), and Results describe whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activations (e.g., MPFC, PCC, anterior temporal poles; voxel-level correction noted). Sample consists of healthy adult volunteers and group-level whole-brain maps are reported in text/figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates implicit facial emotion processing (a social perception task) and includes a healthy control (HC) group. The full text reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps for the HC group (one-sample t-tests, SPM8, cluster-wise thresholds) and provides group-level results and coordinates. The HC group is described as age-matched healthy adults and reported separately from clinical/high-risk participants. The manuscript includes methods, results, and discussion (full article content present). Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for a social-related fMRI task, presence of a healthy adult group with separately reported whole-brain task maps, and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (interpersonal resource conflict) using an event-related whole-brain fMRI design. Sample: healthy adult participants (final N=17, mean age 23.5), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Human Conflict > No Conflict, Computer Conflict > No Conflict), thresholded statistical maps, conjunctions, and tables/figures with coordinates and cluster information. Results are not ROI-only, nor limited to connectivity or between-group contrasts. Full text contains introduction, methods (participants, stimuli, MRI acquisition/analysis), results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (viewing dynamic facial emotional expressions) in healthy adult participants (fMRI N=40, mean age 30.5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (dynamic > static) with FDR-corrected maps and tables of coordinates and describes the second-level one-sample t-test results, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures descriptions) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults 18–65).

The study reports fMRI activation to dynamic social interaction videos in a sample of 20 young adult volunteers (healthy adults). The task is explicitly social (positive and negative social encounters), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The abstract states whole-brain and hemispheric activation with significant right>left effects (p<0.0001) in multiple regions (amygdaloid complex, IFG, fusiform, temporal gyri), indicating group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results from the healthy sample. There is no indication that results are ROI-only, connectivity-only, or limited to non-adult ages. Full text access is limited, but the abstract provides clear evidence that inclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study measures neural responses while healthy adult participants (ages 18–27) listened to literary story excerpts and explicitly models mentalizing and action content. The task targets social cognition (mentalizing/theory-of-mind) which maps to the review’s social-related processing constructs. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (Mentalizing vs Action and vice versa) with appropriate multiple-comparisons correction and displays whole-brain results in the Results/figures. The sample is healthy adults and results are reported for that group. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment against criteria.

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related task (decoding vocal emotions/prosody), meeting the review’s definition of social communication/perception (I3). The sample comprised 22 healthy adult participants (mean age 26.3 ± 7.7), satisfying the healthy adult age range (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conventional SPM GLM and voice-localizer contrasts identifying bilateral STG and Heschl’s gyrus) and presents activation maps/figures, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only (E2), not limited to connectivity or resting-state (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), and participants are within the eligible age range (E5). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study tested emotion modulation of trained visuomotor (mirror) responses in a sample of healthy adults (n=19, mean age 27.7) using a task involving action/shape observation preceded by emotional IAPS images. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (untrained>trained; whole-brain cluster-level FWE-corrected results in SMA and IFG) and provides coordinates and figures. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task—the MNS/emotion/social cognition domain), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results presented as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not limited to ROI-only analyses, not connectivity/resting-only, not restricted to out-of-range ages, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age 23.6) that tests neural responses during social conditions (threat-to-self, threat-to-friend, threat-to-stranger) addressing empathy/understanding of others. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (threat minus safe) and conjunction and covariate analyses, with cluster thresholds and coordinates presented in figures/tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI task examining social sharing/affiliation (participants view emotional pictures either together with a friend or alone), meets the social-related construct (affiliation), and tests healthy adult participants (ages 20–33). The paper presents group-level task-evoked whole-brain analyses and reports whole-brain activations (e.g., DLPFC, precuneus) with appropriate correction as well as ROI results; these healthy-group whole-brain effects are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/influence in healthy adult participants (mean age ~20.6). The task involved social processing (message encoding/intention to recommend) and used task-based whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported at the group level (whole-brain results with MNI coordinates and thresholding are provided). Thus it meets the review’s neuroimaging and sample requirements and reports whole-brain activation maps rather than ROI- or connectivity-only results.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of perception of socially relevant facial expressions (social communication), i.e., a social-related task (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=17, right-handed males, mean age 25.9) meeting the 18–65 criterion (I4). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FIR model in SPM5) are reported with statistical parametric maps and MNI coordinates (random-effects inference; p=.001 uncorrected, extent threshold), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I5,I6). The study is empirical and not ROI- or connectivity-only, and reports healthy-group task activations directly, so it meets inclusion criteria.

The study reports an fMRI experiment involving social-related processing (social reputation), meeting the review topic. The sample consists of 28 healthy young adult participants (14 male, 14 female; ages 20–24), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper presents whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation analyses (thresholds, cluster-level FWE correction, peak voxels in MNI coordinates, and a results table), clearly identified as group-level results from the healthy/control sample. Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and a table of activations. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social touch (a social-related task) in healthy adult participants. Sample: 40 healthy heterosexual males (mean age 25.8), meeting the adult age range. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activations with MNI coordinates, statistical values, and PFWE-corrected clusters (text, figures, and supplementary tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and it is an empirical paper). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social perception: participants viewed approaching characters making happy or angry expressions (social-related task assessing affiliation/dominance). Sample includes ten healthy young adult participants (healthy adults). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrasts (Angry>Happy and Happy>Angry) with statistical thresholding, cluster coordinates, voxel counts, and figures—satisfying whole-brain task-evoked map reporting. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly presented. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within adult range, and this is empirical fMRI data). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: The study employed task-based fMRI during a social decision-making (modified prisoner’s dilemma) task (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=20, ages 23–45) reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for the healthy group (e.g., HC (COMP > CONT), HC (COOP > CONT), conjunctions and within-group Task > Control results) with tables/coordinates and cluster-level correction (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state only, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are explicitly reported. Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social-affective processing (mimicry, affiliation/appeasement) in healthy adults using a task manipulating emotion and group membership, satisfying the review topic. Sample: healthy adult participants (N=41 for fMRI analyses; ages reported, within 18–65). Whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts are reported (e.g., Incongruent>Congruent and masked contrasts for Happy vs Angry, Out-group vs In-group) with cluster-level correction and tables of peak coordinates (Tables 2–4) and detailed methods for SPM analysis. Results are reported for the healthy/control group (no exclusive patient group). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, or non-empirical limitations).

This is an fMRI study of empathic decision-making (social processing: empathy/mentalizing) in healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Sample: 32 healthy adult males (mean age 22.8), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (GLM whole-brain results reported at cluster-corrected P<0.05 with tables of activations and conjunctions) and describes whole-brain PPI analyses; whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts are clearly reported for the healthy group. Therefore it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study that explicitly investigates social communication (perception and evaluation of different laughter types) using task-based fMRI with healthy adult participants (N=18, mean age 26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses (contrasts CSL>TIC, TIC>CSL, CAT>COU, etc.), with statistical thresholds, cluster corrections, and coordinate results/tables/figures. Whole-brain activation maps and contrasts for the healthy participant group are clearly described and reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (kinship-based affiliative vs nonaffiliative scenarios) with healthy adult participants (final N=27; ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FWE-corrected results, whole-brain and ROI-corrected contrasts) with tables/figures and coordinates. The full text includes methods, behavioral and imaging results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and the article is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This study reports an fMRI experiment involving observation of virtual social interactions (social-related task), with a healthy adult sample (group of 15 participants) and group-level whole-brain activation maps. The paper describes whole-brain preprocessing and SPM-based analysis and presents unthresholded/thresholded activation maps and timecourses for social interaction vs. control contrasts showing activity in STS, mPFC, and amygdala. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes methods, scanning parameters, data analysis, and representative results; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper reports task-based fMRI during observation of socio-affective touch (a clearly social-related task) and includes a healthy adult control group (21 neurotypical adults, age-matched). The manuscript provides group-level whole-brain task results for the healthy/control group (mean group effects and brain areas activated for social vs. non-social touch), with MNI coordinates and figures reported in the main text and Additional file 1 (Figure S2 and Table S2), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and participants are within 18–65).

This study employed task-based fMRI probing social-related processing (familiar/partner faces) relevant to affiliation/attachment and perception/understanding of others. It includes a healthy control group (n=13, mean age 64.5) reported separately from the patient, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for the control group (partner > unfamiliar; FWE-corrected results and coordinates are reported). Results are described in figures/tables and whole-brain analyses are clearly attributed to the healthy/control group. The only minor uncertainty is that exact age ranges for controls are not listed (mean 64.5 ±5.7 suggests some participants may approach or slightly exceed 65), hence a confidence <1.0. Overall, the paper meets the review’s requirements for inclusion.

Exclusion E4: No healthy adult control group whole-brain task map is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task—PANSIT-MC with mother–child affect clips) and I6 (reports whole-brain results in tables/figures/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no healthy adult participant group reported separately — sample consists solely of depressed mothers of psychiatrically ill children), I5 (no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map reported for a healthy/control group). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study cannot be included because it does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain activation maps required by the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (direction-sensitive coding of observed head turns), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 22–38). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (gray-matter–masked) voxelwise analyses and corrected voxel coordinates and maps (FWE-corrected results and exploratory whole-brain analyses), clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates and figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (perception of others’ emotional facial expressions, including affiliation-relevant emotions like happiness and disgust), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=40, mean age 29.5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses (family-wise error-corrected cluster threshold, voxelwise P<0.001) with coordinates and ROI results clearly described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (results reported with coordinates/thresholds). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of perception of emotional facial expressions (social communication / perception of others), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample includes 23 healthy adult human volunteers aged 24–34 (meets sample criterion). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (random-effects group analysis, voxel- and cluster-level thresholds, figures of group significance maps) and provides stereotactic coordinates (supplementary table), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures, and tables) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age-out-of-range-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

The study uses task-based fMRI during a social perception task (gender judgments to faces with direct vs averted gaze) addressing perception/understanding of others, with healthy adult participants drawn from the general male population. The fMRI results report group-level task-evoked activation differences (reduced activation in amygdala, fusiform gyrus, anterior superior temporal cortices for low vs normal fear scorers) and functional connectivity findings; these are presented as voxelwise activation contrasts between healthy groups, consistent with whole-brain task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, age out of range, or non-empirical) are evident from the provided full text. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation reported), and I6 (results acceptable as figures/tables).

This study meets inclusion criteria for the review. I3: The task examines voice processing (social perception/communication), a social-related construct. I4: A healthy adult control group (8 male adults, ages ~27) is included and reported separately. I5: The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the control group (voice > non-voice; random-effects analysis, P < 0.001 corrected), clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. I6: Whole-brain results are described in the text and shown in figures/tables (with supplementary material referenced). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (team membership, perception of others) in healthy adult participants using task-based fMRI. The methods and results report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., single-video vs baseline; own-team vs other-team; paired judgments vs press task) with cluster-level FWE correction and MNI coordinates. Sample comprises healthy, right-handed adult volunteers (age range reported 17–43; majority are adults and analyses are reported at the healthy-group level). Reporting includes whole-brain statistical maps/tables and coordinates. The study is empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and provides clearly described within-group task activation results appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study uses fMRI during a social perception task (dataset from a social perception paradigm) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, the primary reported results are seed-based intrinsic/background functional connectivity analyses and between-group connectivity contrasts; the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group (no unmasked whole-brain task activation map for HC is reported in the main text). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only seed-based/connectivity/resting-type analyses without also reporting a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked statistical map) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study used task-based fMRI probing social interaction (a social interaction simulation manipulating relationship type and valence), included a healthy adult sample (28 right-handed participants, age range 19–27), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5 random-effects; FWE- and cluster-corrected results, figures and Table 1 listing significant clusters). Healthy-group effects (main effects and interactions) are clearly described and reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, clinical-only samples) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception/understanding of others) using point-light dyadic displays and an orthogonal task, meeting the review's construct. Sample: healthy adult participants (ten right-handed males, ages 22–32) are reported separately — satisfies the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts ((atypical upright + atypical inverted) − (typical upright + typical inverted)) with cluster-size correction and tables/figures of activated loci, meeting whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and thus appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment using Heider-&-Simmel-style animations to probe agency attribution and mentalizing, which is a social-related task (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (12 in fMRI; mean age 25.2), meeting the age/sample requirement (I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (high>low and low>high), analyzed with SPM2 and reported activations across many brain regions at a voxelwise threshold (p<0.001), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be included in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (self-, mother- and celebrity-judgments) probing self- and other-processing. The sample consists of healthy adult Chinese college students (final N=34; right-handed, no neurological/psychiatric history). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., self- vs celebrity, mother- vs celebrity) and regression/moderation analyses with tables of coordinates (Tables 2 and 3) and figures, with correction/threshold details—satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age-outside-range, or non-empirical paper issues). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of impression formation (perception/understanding of others), conducted in healthy adult participants (18–30 years, n=18 included). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (incongruent vs. congruent contrasts), with cluster-level results surviving FDR correction and coordinates presented in tables/figures. Thus it provides whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps relevant to social processing.

The study uses task-based fMRI to investigate self-recognition (a social-cognition construct: Perception and Understanding of Self), with a healthy adult sample (n≈35, ages 18–24). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (SPM5; contrasts, cluster- and voxel-level thresholds) with tables of coordinates and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult or clinical-only sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study is a proof-of-concept rt-fMRI/EEG neurofeedback correlation analysis targeting the right pSTS for social communication, but the manuscript reports correlations with a predefined ROI rather than reporting any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for a healthy adult group. No unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activation map (voxelwise results or coordinate table of a whole-brain contrast) is described in the abstract/full text provided. Therefore it violates the requirement for whole-brain evidence and appears to present ROI-based analyses only.

The study reports task-based fMRI during social evaluation (explicit approachability judgments of faces vs implicit sex judgment), directly addressing social-related processing. It describes group-level task contrasts showing activations (e.g., left amygdala, medial/middle/inferior frontal gyri) and BOLD correlations with trait anxiety, which indicates whole-brain task-evoked analyses were performed and reported. The sample is described as participants (healthy group) with trait anxiety measured, implying a healthy adult cohort. Thus it meets inclusion: I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activations reported), and I6 (results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) appear to apply based on the provided content.

Study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=10, mean age 25) using a Face Matching Task assessing perception of others’ emotions (social-related processing). The paper includes group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses (one-sample t-tests for contrasts: neutral+fear > control; fear > neutral; fear > neutral+control) reported at second level (results referenced in main text and Supplementary Material), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. The study therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps for healthy group), and I6 (maps/results described and available in supplement). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions).

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (memory for faces with emotional expressions—perception/understanding of others) in healthy adult participants (n=35, mean age 29). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results (FDR-corrected) and provides Talairach coordinates and cluster tables/figures for emotion and load contrasts, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social communication processing in healthy adults (N=20, mean age 22). The task examines processing of communicative vs noncommunicative vocal sounds (social communication). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (vocal > nonvocal and communicative > noncommunicative) thresholded with FDR q<.05 and provides peak coordinates and whole-brain activation maps, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a virtual-reality social cognition task that engages emotional and cognitive aspects of social processing (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (14 right-handed adults, age 18–45) with results reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/contrasts for the healthy control group (within-group Emotion vs Control and other contrasts), with coordinates and tables/figures (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and within-group healthy maps are provided. Full text appears complete.

The full text appears to be a brief conference abstract that does not report necessary methodological details. While the study describes fMRI during a social task (live eye contact) suggesting I3 is met, it does not provide participant details (number, ages, or clearly identified healthy adult group) to confirm I4, nor does it present or reference any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (I5). Because the paper lacks reported healthy-group whole-brain task activation results, it fails the review’s required reporting standards and cannot be included.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (college students) performing a social-related task (observation of others' goal-directed hand actions; relates to Perception and Understanding of Others). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise one-sample activation maps for the non-alexithymic (healthy control) group and the alexithymic group, with statistical thresholds and tables/figures of coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The sample consists of healthy adults (ages consistent with college sample) and results for the healthy subgroup (non-ALEX) are reported separately. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment of social perception (observation of touch to another’s hand), uses healthy adult participants (mean age 26, 18–65), and presents group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with FWE-corrected results, tables, figures, and MNI coordinates. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study uses fMRI in healthy adult participants during a social-related task (audiovisual integration of non-verbal emotional signals) and reports group-level statistics for STS ROIs. However, the analysis is an ROI-based approach with parameter estimates extracted from individually mapped STS measuring points; the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results).

This is an empirical fMRI study of charitable donation decisions (a social decision-making task involving empathy and perspective-taking), with healthy adult participants (N=22; ages 19–38). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (second-level one-sample t tests, whole-brain corrections, coordinates, figures, and supplemental tables). Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain results for healthy group), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines perception of emotional (fearful vs neutral) body actions, a social-related task (perception and understanding of others). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (12 adult males) reported separately from the ASD group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and conjunction analyses (e.g., Fearful vs Neutral; Dynamic vs Static) for the control/healthy group with tables, figures, and thresholded statistical maps described in the text.
