Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (facial emotion and age judgments invoking social cognition/Perception and Understanding of Others), includes a healthy adult control group (n=27; ages 18–65), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation results. The Methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FSL Randomise nonparametric testing) and the Results present within-group and between-group whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables (e.g., within-group activation maps, Tables/Figures for controls and overall sample). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; healthy-group whole-brain effects are reported; participants are within age range; empirical task fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates social processing (emotional face perception) and includes a healthy adult control group; however, the fMRI results are reported using an a priori amygdala ROI with statistical correction within that ROI and the reported group-level results focus on ROI activations. The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (no whole-brain coordinates/tables or whole-brain figures for the control group are reported). Therefore it fails the requirement for reporting whole-brain healthy-group task effects. Exclusion criteria met: E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level task map for healthy group). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (10 right-handed males) who viewed funny vs. non-funny cartoons (a social-communication/humor task). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) with coordinates and statistical values (Talairach X,Y,Z and Z-values, p<0.001 uncorrected) linking BOLD responses to trait cheerfulness; these are clearly identified as coming from the healthy sample. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task map), and I6 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: viewing/processing others' emotional faces) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–33). However, it does not report a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group (e.g., a main effect or within-group whole-brain contrast of faces vs baseline) — analyses focus on ROI percent signal change (FFA, amygdala) and seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity results. According to the review criteria, studies that report only seed-based connectivity without also providing a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map are excluded (E3). The paper principally reports PPI/interactions (sex × stress) without an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activation map, meeting exclusion E4 as well. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I5 (whole-brain task activation) and because it meets exclusion criteria E3 (and E4).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (biological motion perception), includes a healthy adult control group (n=15, mean age ~25) reported separately, and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation results for the healthy/control group (see Table 2; P<0.001 uncorrected). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical fMRI study).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (direct vs. averted gaze) and includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately (meets I3, I4). However, this manuscript reports psychophysiological interaction (PPI) seed-based connectivity (task-modulated connectivity) analyses rather than univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for the healthy group. The reported "whole-brain" results refer to PPI connectivity maps, not standard task activation contrasts. Therefore it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group (I5 not met). Per exclusion criterion E3 (seed-based connectivity only without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map), the paper must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing (perception of others' eye gaze and social attention) using task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants (n=9, mean age 24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts to identify face-responsive regions (clusters selected with z>4 and cluster-size thresholds), and provides atlas coordinates and tables/figures of activations using SPM. Thus it meets criteria for using fMRI during a social task (I3), includes healthy adults in the 18–65 range (I4), reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps (I5), and provides coordinates/figures as acceptable reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social evaluation/impression formation (social cognition) using task fMRI in healthy adults. The study includes a young adult group (ages 20–29), which satisfies the requirement for a healthy adult sample within the 18–65 range (I4). The methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and contrasts (social vs. non-social; social-meaningful vs. social-irrelevant), conjunction analyses, and corrected cluster thresholds with peak locations reported (satisfying I5 and I6). The task is explicitly social-related (forming impressions; I3). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, healthy-group whole-brain results are reported, and study includes an eligible age group). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=33, ages 18–21) that used a social-related task (viewing social vs non-social scenes) and reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (social > non-social contrast; whole-brain random-effects analysis, FDR corrected, with tables and coordinates). The paper includes full introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and none of the exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of perception/understanding of others (comparison of goal-directed vs non-goal-directed biological motion), satisfying the social-processing construct. Participants are healthy adults (N=12, mean age 29.4), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (BR minus BU) with statistical thresholds and peak coordinates (whole-brain corrected P<0.05 and ROI thresholds P<0.001 uncorrected), i.e., a healthy-group task effect. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (recognition of others’ ‘vitality forms’) in healthy adult participants (19 adults, ages 21–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., how vs what) with statistical thresholds (PFWE < 0.05) and coordinate tables/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for task relevance (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and whole-brain group-level results reported (I5); whole-brain results are also presented in tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is excluded because it does not report task-evoked whole-brain fMRI results in a healthy adult group. Exclusion criteria met: E3 — the paper reports resting-state fMRI analyses (seed/ROI and connectivity analyses) and effects of intranasal oxytocin in an ASD patient sample, but does not provide any group-level, whole-brain task activation maps from a healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no task-based social-related fMRI paradigm; analyses are resting-state), I4 (no healthy adult group; sample consists of adults with ASD only and healthy controls are not reported), I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from a healthy/control group). Full text appears complete and sufficient to make this determination.

This is an fMRI experiment examining neural correlates of receiving empathic vs. unempathic social comments (social-related processing). The sample comprises healthy adults (n=20, mean age 26) with no neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., empathic>unempathic, negative>positive feedback) with cluster thresholds and FWE-corrected results and tables of activations. Reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures meets acceptable reporting standards. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, etc.) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (intergroup competition, self vs. other moral processing) in healthy adults (N=21, Mage=23.1), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with corrected thresholds and provides tables/coordinates of supra-threshold clusters (Tables 1 and 2), meeting I5 and I6. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, and supplementary figures) is present in the provided content, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: the study is not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task activations, and is empirical with healthy adult participants. Therefore it should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social impression formation in healthy adults using task-based BOLD fMRI. Participants: N=19 healthy adults (mean age 19.1), within the 18–65 inclusion range. The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (functional localizer contrast form impression > remember order; main 2×2 ANOVA in dmPFC ROI with whole-brain cluster-correction procedures and tables of coordinates are provided), with tables/figures and corrected cluster thresholds described. The task is social (impression formation/perception and understanding of others), satisfying the review’s constructs. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state-only, no patient-only sample, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and can be included in the meta-analysis.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social interaction (cooperation vs. competition) in healthy adult participants (12 adults aged 21–28). Methods describe whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise contrasts (cooperation vs independent, competition vs independent, and direct contrasts), reported in tables and figures. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study of social processing using live bidirectional conversation (human–human vs human–robot) — a clearly social-related task probing mentalizing and social motivation. Sample: 21 healthy adult participants (mean age 25.8, no psychiatric/neurological history), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (HHI vs HRI and reverse), with statistical inference (p<0.05 FDR-corrected cluster-level) and whole-brain maps/figures; group data are available on NeuroVault/OpenNeuro. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (15 healthy males, mean age 26.7). The task involves social-related processing (matching fearful/angry faces) and shows group-level task-evoked activation maps (fearful vs control) for the healthy/placebo condition, reported in figures and analyzed with second-level random-effects models; whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (with ROI-based correction for the amygdala) and results are presented in text, tables, and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from healthy group), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats) are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This article reports an event-related fMRI study of social interaction (SI) recognition (a social-related task) using point-light displays (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult group (N=16, ages 20–41) with results reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (SI > NM) for the adult group using SPM8 with peak- and cluster-level thresholding and FWE corrections; activations for adults (e.g., bilateral pMTG/pSTS, IFG, dmPFC, caudate) are explicitly described (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, adult group within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports two fMRI experiments investigating understanding of intentions in social interaction, demonstrating anterior paracingulate cortex activation. The study addresses social-related processing (theory of mind/social interaction) using task-based fMRI in human participants and reports group-level activation (anterior PCC) consistent with whole-brain task effects. It was published in Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience (2004) and presents empirical fMRI results rather than a review. Therefore it meets the review objective and the inclusion criteria for fMRI social tasks, healthy adult sample reporting, and whole-brain results (reported as activation in anterior PCC). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply based on the available full-text abstract and bibliographic information.

This study uses task fMRI of social perception and includes a healthy adult control group (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper’s whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported only as between-group contrasts (patient vs control). The authors do not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (i.e., no whole-brain HC social>nonsocial map is presented; within-group HC effects are reported only via post-hoc ROI analyses based on between-group clusters). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: it used fMRI during a social-related task (interpersonal pleasant touch) probing social reward and context (I3); it included a clearly reported healthy adult control group (n=24, ages 18–35) analyzed separately (I4); and it reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation results for the control group (e.g., TOUCH > CLOSE and FEMALE > MALE contrasts with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and peak coordinates), satisfying requirements for whole-brain evidence (I5/I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the report appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: it uses fMRI during a social-related imitate/observe facial-expression task (I3); includes a healthy adult control group (ages 18–55) reported separately within the sample (I4); reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (imitate>observe contrasts) and notes that second-level group analyses were run separately for each site and group, with group/cluster maps presented in figures and supplement (I5); and whole-brain results are described in the text and figures/supplementary materials (I6). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Accordingly, I include this paper for the meta-analysis of social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

Meets the review objective and provides whole-brain task activation maps for healthy control participants during a social-related fMRI task (facial emotion processing). I3: Study uses fMRI during a social-related task (facial emotion processing). I5: Reports whole-brain, group-level within-group contrasts and one-sample t-tests for the control group, with FWE-corrected maps and tables (Table 3 and supplemental material). I6: Results and statistical maps/tables are clearly described in the text and supplemental material. I4: Healthy control group is reported separately; participants’ ages are given as 16–40 years (controls recruited from university and community). This implies the healthy sample falls largely within the adult range (18–65); although the minimum possible age is 16, the paper reports controls as a distinct group and presents their whole-brain results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion for the healthy adult whole-brain task activation criterion, with moderate confidence due to minor ambiguity about exact age distribution of the control subgroup.

This is an fMRI study using a social cognition task (theory of mind and empathy cartoon task), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=13, ages 19–36). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts analyzed with SPM2 (random-effects) and presents significant activation foci (thresholds, clusters, and tables/figures). Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for an fMRI social-related task in healthy adults and provides whole-brain group-level results.

I3 met: Study uses fMRI during a social-related task (simulation/empathy for others' pain). I4 met: Includes a healthy adult control group (24 HC, ages within 18–65) with results reported for that group in behavioral and ROI plots. I5 NOT met: The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. Whole-brain results are reported for the full sample (HC + SZ) and ROI analyses present HC and SZ contrasts, but no unmasked HC-only whole-brain activation map or coordinate table is provided. Because inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) were directly triggered, so exclusion is solely due to failure to meet I5.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (implicit interpersonal space/affiliation) in healthy adults, reporting group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (main effects and treatment×stimulus interaction) from the healthy sample. The sample comprises healthy adult males (ages 19–30). Whole-brain random-effects GLM results are described (significant clusters in dorsal striatum, ACC, medial frontal gyrus) and PPI connectivity is additionally reported; whole-brain task activation maps/cluster results are presented in the text/figures. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports fMRI of social cognition using a validated, naturalistic Theory of Mind task (MASC), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=18, age range 20–45), meeting the sample criterion. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation results (GLM contrasts ToM vs PI) with thresholding, cluster correction, and tabulated coordinates and figures, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Results for the healthy/control sample are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, and not a non-empirical paper). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

The study reports functional MRI during a social cognition task in which participants repeatedly inferred others’ emotions and received feedback—clearly a social-related task. The abstract indicates participants were scanned (perceivers) and no clinical/special groups are mentioned, implying a healthy adult sample. The paper reports trial-by-trial learning signals that tracked activity in ventral striatum, ventromedial PFC, and TPJ, which indicates voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results were analyzed and reported. Reporting in J Cogn Neurosci further supports standard whole-brain analyses. Although the abstract does not state exact ages, the sample is described as typical adult perceivers with no clinical exclusion; thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

This study includes an fMRI task probing social-related processing (social phobia–related words) — meets I3. However, the fMRI sample consists only of 25 female patients with social anxiety disorder; no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps are reported for a healthy/control fMRI group. The fMRI analyses focus on a bilateral amygdala ROI (ROI-based, cluster-corrected) and report correlations within patients rather than an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group activation map. Therefore the study does not meet I4 (healthy adult fMRI group results reported) nor I5 (healthy-group, whole-brain task activation map). It also fails I6 in practice because qualifying whole-brain healthy-group results are absent. Exclusion criterion E2 applies (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text is complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE (E2).

This paper reports task-based fMRI during social-related tasks (approachability and intelligence judgements) in healthy adult participants. A healthy control group (n=47; ages within 18–65) is analyzed and reported separately; a second experiment reports healthy male controls and ASD males separately. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (social vs gender) are reported using SPM2 with thresholding and cluster correction, with coordinates and figures described in the text. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), and I6 (results provided as coordinates/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used task-based fMRI to examine human perception of affective vocalisations (social communication/perception of others), matching the review’s social-related constructs. Sample: healthy adult participants (N=19, mean age 25.9) within the 18–65 range. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts are reported (e.g., species contrast human > chimpanzee > macaque) with MNI coordinates, tables and figures (p < .001 uncorrected), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social judgment task (dominance/trustworthiness of faces) in healthy adults (N=23, ages 21–43). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and provides voxelwise results with a table of peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE-corrected results for the Social Judgment > Perceptual Judgment contrast. Results for the healthy adult group are clearly reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of facial emotion processing (a social cognition task: perception/understanding of others' emotions) with a healthy adult control group. Healthy controls are adults (mean age 27±5) within the 18–65 range and their results are reported separately. The paper describes group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and presents group activation maps/tables for the control group (contrasts such as neutral vs fixation and emotion vs fixation; methods describe whole-brain permutation-based voxel and cluster thresholding), satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group results. Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group without healthy-group effect, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults (native Japanese speakers, ages 19–31) that used whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses to report task-evoked activation maps. The experimental tasks explicitly probe social communication (communicative vs descriptive speech) satisfying the review’s social-related construct. The paper reports whole-brain random-effects analyses and interaction and main-effect contrasts (with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds) clearly attributable to the healthy participant group. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of a social cognition task (third-party punishment), which clearly falls under social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). The sample comprises healthy adults (N=26; mean age 26, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (Decision Phase: Experimental > Control) with statistical thresholds and coordinates, and presents parametric and conjunction analyses (figures/tables/coordinates). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E2), not limited to connectivity/resting analyses (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within the age range (E5), and this is an original empirical fMRI study (not a review; E6). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplemental references, so full text appears complete.

This is an original fMRI study in healthy adult participants (students, mean age 25.7) that used a social-emotion task (guilt memories and hypothetical social scenarios) relevant to social cognition/perception of self and others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (thresholded whole-brain maps at p<0.001 with cluster extent and reported activated regions and coordinates) as well as SVC results. The sample is within the 18–65 range and results for the healthy group are reported. The study is empirical fMRI (task-based) and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a social-referential paradigm (Visual–Verbal Self-Other Referential Processing Task) that probes self vs other processing (social-related processing). The sample comprises 20 healthy adult women aged 18–52 with psychiatric history exclusion criteria, satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation results (SPM8 analyses) with group contrasts, tables of clusters, and voxelwise figures (e.g., Figure 2) clearly identified as coming from the healthy participant group. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Ultimatum Game (a social decision-making task) and reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts. The sample includes a healthy adult group (young adults age 19–28) with results for that group reported separately. The paper provides voxelwise contrasts (unfair–fair) and group-level statistical maps/tables for the adult group. Reporting of whole-brain results is in figures/tables and described in text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

E3 met: The study reports resting-state intrinsic connectivity (seed/network analyses) and PET-derived dopamine responses during mother–infant film viewing, but it does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked fMRI activation map for the healthy adult group. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes healthy adult mothers, ages 21–42, reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no task-evoked fMRI whole-brain analysis reported — fMRI results are intrinsic/resting-state connectivity rather than task activation), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is provided), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain task results reported in text/figures/tables). Full text appears complete (full methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded for this meta-analysis because it reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity and PET outcomes without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map.

This fMRI study investigates audiovisual speech processing (a social-communication task) and includes a healthy adult control group whose demographics are reported. However, the paper does not present a clearly identified, unmasked whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone. Results focus on a main effect of congruency across both groups and on group-by-congruency interaction effects rather than reporting a standalone whole-brain healthy-group task map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports interactions/between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (and thus no qualifying I6 application). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating neural responses to witnessing emergencies (bystander effect) using task-evoked BOLD contrasts. Participants were healthy adults (ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM, parametric and contrast maps) with results presented in tables and figures. The task is a social-related paradigm probing perception/understanding of others and action preparation in a bystander context. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only groups, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion requirements for the review objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=21, mean age 24) that uses action observation/execution paradigms probing mirror-system responses—relevant to social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task analyses (explicit whole-brain thresholding at p<0.001 uncorrected and ROI analyses with FWE correction) and provides peak coordinates/tables. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete.

This is an fMRI study of social gaze processing in a sample of 55 healthy adult males (satisfies I3 and I4). However, the analyses and results are reported as region-of-interest (amygdala and inferior occipital gyrus) ROI analyses using masked ROI statistics (FWE-corrected within ROI). The paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain (unmasked, voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain activation table for the healthy group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (reports interaction/contrast effects without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) apply. Full text appears complete. Given these points, the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind) in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the analyses are ROI-based MVPA and regionwise tests; the full text does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group (no whole-brain activation map, coordinates table, or clearly described group-level voxelwise contrast is reported in the provided content). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). It is excluded under E2 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (comprehension of others' emotions) using task-based functional MRI in healthy adults (N=22, ages 19–32). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., How>Why, Why>How) with tables of coordinates and SPM analyses, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult task activations).

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (self-other touch) in adults, reporting separate neurotypical control group data. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/contrasts for neurotypical controls (figures and text) with FWE correction. Sample ages (controls mean 23.7±3.6; ADHD and NC are adults) fall within 18–65. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps for healthy group), and I6 (maps reported in figures/text). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group map, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (perception of biological motion/social stimuli) in healthy adult participants (final N=26; ages 18–39). The paper reports both ROI analyses and whole-brain, voxelwise analyses: a whole-brain analysis of biological-motion selectivity and social-network measures yielded a significant cluster in the right pSTS (reported in text and supplemental Figure S1) with correction for multiple comparisons. Whole-brain results are clearly described for the healthy group. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adult participants (N=18, mean age 20), using social-related tasks (inferring others’ vegetable preferences and categorical age judgments) that probe perception and understanding of others. The methods describe whole-brain EPI acquisition and preprocessing, and group-level, random-effects GLM analyses with whole-brain contrast maps reported (Talairach coordinates, voxel clusters, tables/figures). Results include voxelwise activations in mPFC and other regions with coordinates and cluster sizes. All required inclusion criteria are met: fMRI during social task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported (I5), and whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly investigates social processing (linking person perception and person knowledge). The methods report an fMRI task manipulating social agent (bodies vs names) and social knowledge (trait vs neutral), with 21 healthy adult participants (age mean 24.6). Group-level whole-brain univariate results and connectivity (PPI) results are reported (Tables and figures described; voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction reported), and coordinates are provided. Thus the paper meets the review’s requirements for (i) task-based fMRI in social cognition, (ii) healthy adult sample, and (iii) reporting group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (reported in text/tables/figures). The supplied full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without whole-brain maps, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range participants, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates processing of narratives with moral/protected values — a social-related task (social cognition, moral evaluation, understanding others). Participants are healthy adults (three groups; mean ages ~24–26; n=78 after exclusions), within the 18–65 range and reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (e.g., reading stories vs rest, protected-value vs nonprotected stories) with cluster correction; whole-brain results are described in the text and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This publication is a review article (non-empirical) and does not report original fMRI data, participant samples, methods, or any group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from healthy adults. It therefore does not meet the requirement for original fMRI results in healthy adults and should be excluded.

This fMRI study includes a social-related task (altruism/other-focused decisions and TPJ/precuneus/ToM processes), reports results from healthy adult participants (N=55 overall, subset N=37 for food; ages within 18–65), and provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses with thresholded maps and reported MNI coordinates (whole-brain searchlight SVR maps, conjunctions, and cluster-corrected results). Whole-brain results are described in text, figures, and coordinates; supplemental/ROI tests are secondary. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of supramodal emotional (social) processing in healthy adults (N=24, ages 18–34). The task is social-related (perception/integration of facial and vocal emotions). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects GLM, conjunctions, FDR-corrected maps; tables/figures with coordinates reported). All inclusion criteria for the review are met, and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult group results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (feeling addressed) that meets all inclusion criteria. It reports task-based fMRI during a social-related task (participants judged whether they felt addressed) (I3). The sample comprises 37 healthy adult participants aged 20–39 (I4). Group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses are reported (SPM8), with cluster-corrected results and peak MNI coordinates for main effects and interactions (I5). Results are presented in figures and tables of coordinates (I6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (observation of human/robot agents interacting with objects) using a task during functional MRI in healthy adults (final N=23, mean age 26.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (main effects of agent form and belief, interactions) with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster/FWE correction and provides peak coordinates and tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete: provided content contains only an empty <body> tag and lacks Introduction, Methods, Results, or Discussion. Therefore I cannot verify whether the study used task-based fMRI of social processes (I3), included a healthy adult group reported separately (I4), or reported whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps (I5/I6). Because core inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded from the review until a complete full text is available. Inclusion criteria met: none confirmed. Inclusion criteria not met/unknown: I3, I4, I5, I6. Exclusion criteria met: none (insufficient information to apply E2–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self- and other-referential recollection), using task-based fMRI and addressing social cognition constructs. Participants were healthy adults (n=18, ages 19–29), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects), with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures (Tables 2 and 3; whole-brain and ROI/SVC reported), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting requirements. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core content appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study includes a task-based fMRI social cognition contrast (TOM vs Random) performed in a large sample of healthy adult participants from the Human Connectome Project (ages 22–>35), and provides group-level whole-brain task activation maps (reported and thresholded; Cohen's d and level-3 z maps are described). Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly reported and visualized, satisfying reporting via figures/tables and supplementary materials. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (acceptable forms of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=41 analyzed; ages 18–24) that directly probes social-related processing (decisions to share with others, perspective-taking, social-cognition ROIs). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses (select > content, share > content, share > select) with family-wise error correction and tables/figures of activations, clearly from the healthy sample. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that uses task-based paradigms probing social processing (take advice game and trust game) with fMRI acquisition and analyses. The sample consists of 31 healthy adult participants (age 24.3±3.8), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain task-evoked results (searchlight MVPA and whole-brain univariate contrasts) clearly identified as group-level effects for the healthy participant group, with cluster- and voxel-level corrected maps and tables described in the text and supplementary materials. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, neuroimaging acquisition and preprocessing, and statistical analyses, so the full text is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social perception in healthy adults (N=14, ages 20–32) using tasks that explicitly probe perception/understanding of others (point-light and shape-animation social interaction stimuli). It includes group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported peaks/figures (interaction > independent; animate > physical) and reports coordinates and maps, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The healthy adult sample is within 18–65 and results are reported for that group. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, figures, supplemental movies referenced) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI task that probes social perception (fearful faces with gaze direction), includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately, and provides group-level whole-brain within-group results for the control group (AVERTED>DIRECT) with statistical maps/figures and corrected voxelwise analyses. Full article text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy controls, participants are within 18–65).

Provided content includes title and abstract only; full text (methods, participants, results, figures/tables) is not available, so essential details cannot be confirmed. The abstract indicates an fMRI study of gaze processing (a social task), suggesting I3 is met. However the sample characteristics (healthy adults, ages 18–65) are not reported in the supplied content, so I4 cannot be confirmed. Likewise, although the abstract reports activation differences in fusiform cortex, the supplied content does not contain the full methods/results to verify the presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (I5). Because core article content is missing, I cannot safely verify all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly met based on the abstract alone, but incomplete full text prevents inclusion.

Excluded because exclusion criterion E5 is met: the sample includes participants older than 65 (up to age 68) and the authors do not report a separate analysis restricted to a healthy adult subgroup within 18–65. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (study reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps/analyses with voxelwise results and coordinates) and I6 (whole-brain results are presented in figures/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (sample does not conform to age 18–65 without a separately reported subgroup), and I3 (task is word/pseudoword repetition for probing speech production/aging; it is not a clear social-related task or explicit social-communication paradigm). Full text appears complete and sufficient for screening.

This is an fMRI task study probing social auditory processing (listening to one vs. two walkers), clearly addressing social-related processing. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=12; ages 22–37). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM results and statistical maps/coordinate tables for contrasts (e.g., STEP1+STEP2 – REST; STEP1 – NOISE1; STEP2 – NOISE2), normalized to Talairach space. Whole-brain contrasts and coordinates are explicitly described for the healthy participant group, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The study is empirical, not ROI-only, not resting-state, and includes direct task-evoked activations. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (gaze and social voice cues vs arrows/tones) addressing social communication/perception (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (N=22, mean age ~23) meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM12 random-effects, whole-brain thresholds and small-volume corrections) and reports results in text/tables/figures, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, includes participants in the 18–65 range, and is empirical with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study investigates communicative (social) speech production versus description, directly addressing social communication processes. Sample: healthy adult native Japanese speakers (n=30, ages 19–31), meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., ECOM–EOBJ, L2COM vs L1COM, interaction (L2COM–L2DES)–(L1COM–L1DES)) with tables of peak coordinates and cluster-corrected maps, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Whole article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, healthy adult group results reported separately). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social processing using the Reading the Mind in the Eyes task (social perception/understanding of others), conducted in healthy adult participants (native Japanese and white American adults aged 18–27). The methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (mass-univariate GLM in SPM5) and multiple group contrasts and tables/figures of activations (e.g., RME − GD, same- vs other-culture contrasts), clearly identified as coming from the healthy groups. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI during a social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain effects, participant ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, appendix).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15, ages 45–62) using a social-affective task (viewing film clips of people in distress) with explicit emotion-regulation conditions (Compassion, Reappraisal). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Compassion > Watch-Negative, Reappraisal > Watch-Negative), with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/figures describing results for the healthy participant group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used task-based fMRI (cyberball) to probe social interaction/rejection (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (20 female HCs) reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (flexible factorial and t-contrasts) and describes condition and within-group effects for HCs (post-hoc within-group effects and t-contrasts referenced in Supplementary Table S4), satisfying the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task-evoked map from the healthy/control group (meets I5). Results are reported in the main text and supplementary materials (tables/figures), consistent with I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–22) using a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) during BOLD fMRI, reporting group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (whole-brain cluster-corrected results and functional ROIs applied to cross-sectional data). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based fMRI during social-related processing (why/how social attribution questions about emotional expressions and intentional actions) (I3). The sample consists of healthy adults (N=19, ages 21–46) with results reported for the healthy group (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (conjunction and interaction contrasts, cluster-level FWE correction; whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5,I6). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment of methods and outcomes (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly manipulates social cognitive load (social working memory task) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric effects with coordinates and figures). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=16; mean age 20) within the 18–65 range. Whole-brain results for the healthy group are reported and linked to trait measures. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 24–37; N=10 for fMRI) using socially relevant non-verbal vocalizations and animated faces, addressing social-related perception/understanding of others. Group-level voxelwise statistical analyses (voxel-by-voxel two-tailed t tests, maps transformed to Talairach space, thresholded maps and ROI analyses) are presented as group activation maps (figures/tables), satisfying group whole-brain voxelwise reporting (not merely ROI-based). Healthy adult results are reported separately and clearly. Although slice coverage was focused on temporal cortex, the paper presents group voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and contrasts for the healthy sample, meeting the review’s requirements.

Exclusion criteria met: E3 and E4. The study reports only task-dependent seed-based connectivity (gPPI) and between-group connectivity contrasts, without reporting any unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during an emotional valence task with social stimuli such as faces — qualifies as social-related processing) and I4 (healthy adult control group of 25 participants reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it violates exclusion criteria E3 and E4 despite meeting I3 and I4.

This is an fMRI study of social processing: participants learned moral status (cooperator/defector) via interactive Prisoner’s Dilemma and were scanned while making gender judgments of those faces — a clear social-related task. The sample consists of healthy adults (scanned n=11, ages 21–36). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM2) with coordinates and tables/figures of activations. Results are not limited to ROI, connectivity, or between-group contrasts. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for task, sample, and whole-brain reporting.

(a) Exclusion criterion met: E4 — the study reports only patient-group effects (CET vs EST) and does not include or report an unmasked whole-brain task activation map from a healthy/control group. (b) Inclusion criteria met: none. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 — the fMRI task (POP) is a cognitive control (non-social) paradigm, not a social-related task; I4 — no healthy adult participant group is included or reported separately; I5 — no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported for a healthy/control group. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study does not meet the review eligibility and should be excluded.

This is an fMRI study using a social cognition task (Theory of Mind false-belief vs false-photo), including a healthy adult control group (n=25, ages 18–59). The paper reports whole-brain task analyses and explicitly states that control-group FB>FP activation maps were used to functionally localize left/right TPJ and posterior cingulate (i.e., a whole-brain, group-level healthy-control task effect is available and described). Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (whole-brain, group-level healthy-control task activation map reported/used), and I6 (results clearly described in text/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study using social-related tasks (viewing own vs. other child photographs and child behaviors), meeting the social processing requirement. Participants are adult mothers (healthy adult sample reported as a group; no indication that mother participants were clinical or outside 18–65), satisfying the sample criterion. The Methods explicitly describe voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects and whole-brain analyses with reported activations, coordinates, and figures, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are described in text, tables, and figures (acceptable reporting). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Although the sample is small and heterogeneous and some covariates (children’s ADHD) are present, these do not violate inclusion/exclusion criteria. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants imagined encountering neutral faces embedded in goal-relevant vs. goal-irrelevant everyday social situations (social communication / perception of others). Sample: healthy adult participants (17 analyzed; ages 20–36) within the 18–65 range. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (random-effects ANOVAs; cluster-corrected thresholds; tables/coordinates and figures provided), not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only results. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references, so appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. I recommend inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (explicit and implicit processing of emotional facial expressions), satisfying the review topic. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=9, mean age 27±7 yrs) reported separately alongside a clinical group. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain task analyses with cluster coordinates and descriptions of activations attributable to controls (e.g., control-specific activation of left cerebellum and left amygdalohippocampal region; main effects and diagnosis × experiment interactions reported in tables and text). Results are reported as group-level whole-brain contrasts/coordinates (not ROI-only). The full-text is complete (methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study investigating visual sensitivity to spatial relations between bodies (facing vs nonfacing), a social-related construct (perception/understanding of others). It tested healthy adult participants (n=20, ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., dyads > single bodies; facing > nonfacing dyads) with tables/figures of activations and coordinates. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are not required for inclusion.

This is an empirical task fMRI study of social perception (perception of emotional crowds and interactions) in healthy adults (N=16; ages 19–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANOVAs) with cluster-corrected maps and tables/figures of activations for main effects and interactions. Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objectives and all inclusion criteria.

The paper reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (theory of mind/intentions), includes a healthy adult control group (n=12) with ages in the 18–65 range, and presents group-level, whole-brain task activation results for the control group (within-group contrasts and tables/figures of coordinates). Reporting meets acceptable formats (tables, figures, coordinates). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only, age out of range, or non-empirical) are met. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI during social cognition (mental-state/judgment task), (I4) reports a healthy adult sample (N=28 after exclusion; ages 18–22), (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (searchlight RSA and repetition-suppression voxelwise maps with permutation TFCE correction), and (I6) whole-brain results are clearly described and reported in figures and text. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-related task (facial emotion recognition) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results with coordinates and familywise-error–corrected statistics (e.g., amygdala clusters, whole-brain regression results). Sample consists of healthy adult males (n=116, mean age 24.7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15, mean age 24.4) that investigates processing of angry prosody—a social-communication/emotion perception task—using a dichotic listening paradigm. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects, whole-brain contrasts) with coordinates and cluster results for healthy participants. Results for the healthy sample are presented directly (not only subgroup or connectivity analyses). Thus it meets the meta-analysis focus on fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults and satisfies whole-brain reporting requirements.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition (valuation/generation of others’ emotional facial expressions), involving 14 healthy adult participants (mean age ~29, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM2 with thresholds and reports activated regions and coordinates (whole-brain task contrasts). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It reports an fMRI task probing social-related processing (learning about others’ generosity) with a computationally matched non-social control (I3). The sample includes healthy adult participants (ages 19–37; N=30 recruited, N=26 analyzed) meeting the 18–65 requirement and results are reported for the healthy group (I4). The article reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLM contrasts, one-sample t-tests, cluster-correction) with coordinates and tables/figures (I5, I6). The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures, references) is present in the provided text and is sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore include.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception and understanding of others via voices; identity and emotion recognition), meeting I3. Sample includes healthy adult participants (15 sighted, 7 congenitally/early blind; ages within adult range), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (univariate whole-brain GLM results, searchlight MVPA group-level maps, tables and figures of voxelwise results) satisfying I5 and I6. Full article includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and contains whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps for inclusion in the review.

The study uses fMRI during social tasks in healthy adults (theory-of-mind and social attribution-of-attention) and meets I3 and I4. However, it does not report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation map for the healthy group. Task-related analyses were performed using localized ICA within a TPJ ROI (ROI-limited task decomposition) and task relevance was assessed via IC time-course regressions; whole-brain results are limited to seed-to-voxel functional connectivity maps (connectivity, not task-evoked activation). Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task activation reporting and meets exclusion criteria E2 and E3.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (self- and other-reflection). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=33, ages within 18–65) with results for the healthy group reported separately (within-group contrasts: Self>Facts, Other>Facts, Other>Self). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, cluster-level corrected (reported z thresholds, MNI coordinates, cluster sizes, Supplementary tables and figures). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling extraction of healthy-group whole-brain activation maps and coordinates. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This article is a theoretical/review paper discussing explanations for mirror-touch synesthesia and does not report original empirical fMRI data or methods/results from healthy adult participants. The abstract indicates conceptual/theoretical discussion and cites existing fMRI evidence but provides no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps from a healthy control group, nor any reported task-based fMRI methods/results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16, ages 25–49) that used movie stimuli depicting social/emotional interactions to probe perception/understanding of others and empathy, satisfying social-related task criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise intersubject correlation (ISC) maps and ISC-by-valence/arousal GLM maps with voxelwise FDR-corrected statistics (figures and supplemental tables), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=31, ages 18–35) using a social-perception task (gender judgments while viewing faces differing by facial disfigurement) that probes social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, stigma/dehumanization). The authors performed whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SnPM nonparametric whole-brain contrasts, cluster-level FWE correction) and report significant whole-brain activations and deactivations for the healthy sample (figures/tables and ROI/item-wise follow-ups are provided). Thus the paper meets the fMRI social-processing objective, includes a healthy adult sample, and reports unmasked group-level whole-brain task activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines social-cognitive processing during observation of toolmaking: participants performed tasks that require simulation (‘Imagine’) and judgement of the demonstrator’s success (‘Evaluate’), tapping perception/understanding of others and intentions. The sample comprises healthy adult groups (Naïve n=11, Trained n=10, Expert n=5). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses (e.g. Toolmaking–Control; Acheulean–Oldowan) with FDR-corrected thresholds, presented in text, figures and tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This empirical fMRI study investigates humor processing—a social cognitive/emotional process involving perception and understanding of others (ToM/ social cognition). It used task-based whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) reporting group-level contrasts (Cartoons vs Neutral, parametric modulation) with corrected statistics and conjunctions, and provides tables/figures of results. The sample comprises 29 healthy adult participants (mean age 27, range within 18–65). Reporting includes whole-brain maps/coordinates. Therefore it satisfies the review’s task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

This fMRI study uses a social-context decision task (SCDT) involving peer presence and examines counterfactual emotions (regret, relief, disappointment, elation), meeting the review’s social-processing scope. The sample includes a healthy adult group (young adults, age 21–22) reported separately alongside adolescents. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-sample and age-group second-level GLM contrasts) with cluster tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group results. Reporting of coordinates, clusters, and figures is present. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates neural processing of others' actions (auditory mirror system) — a social-cognitive task (Perception and Understanding of Others). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=26 behavioral; n=11 in fMRI; ages 21–29), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with statistical maps, cluster-level inference, and tables/figures of activations. Results for the healthy group are clearly presented. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that examines how collective (social) schemas shape memory representations. The task involved participants recalling museum pictures and analysing neural patterns related to collective/social knowledge (dmPFC/vmPFC). The sample consists of 24 healthy adults aged 22–39. The paper reports whole-brain searchlight analyses with group-level correction (TFCE, permutation testing) and presents whole-brain results (Extended Data Fig. 1), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults and satisfies the listed inclusion criteria.

Provided full text appears incomplete (abstract-level summary only). Inclusion criterion I3 is met: the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (action perception/recognition, i.e., perception/understanding of others). Inclusion criteria I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–65) and I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group) cannot be confirmed from the supplied content—the methods do not report participant ages/health status nor explicitly state whole-brain voxelwise results (named regions could arise from ROI analyses or whole-brain contrasts). Because I4 and I5 are not verifiable, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the provided excerpt. Recommend obtaining the complete article (methods and results) to re-evaluate.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in which healthy adult participants (n=36) performed an Other task requiring prediction of another person’s decisions—clearly a social-related task (simulation/theory-of-mind). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (significant clusters reported with corrected p-values and Talairach coordinates; Tables and figures show whole-brain results) based on the healthy participant group. Results for the healthy/control group are presented (behavioral and fMRI within-group effects). Reporting includes coordinate tables and figures consistent with whole-brain maps. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI social-processing studies in healthy adults.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses task-based fMRI to study prosodic speech processing, a social-communication construct; (I4) includes a healthy adult control group (8 males, age ~23) reported separately; (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps for the control group (one-sample t-tests, activation and deactivation maps with FDR correction); (I6) whole-brain results are described in text and tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although sample size is small and one clinical group is also present, control-group whole-brain results are clearly reported, so the study is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining mind perception (a social-cognitive process) using event-related fMRI during a mind-perception task and a separate behavioral gaze-cueing task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=22; mean age 24.4), meeting the 18–65 criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric regressors, FLAME1), with cluster-corrected whole-brain results and peak coordinates (e.g., significant vmPFC clusters) and figures/tables describing these maps. Thus it provides healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation maps in formats acceptable for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (viewing realistic first-person social interaction videos) in a healthy adult sample (n=20 males, mean age 24.6). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FDR-corrected thresholds) with peak coordinates and tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Behavioral and imaging results are clearly described for the healthy/control group. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study that directly probes social-related processing (empathy for pain/pleasure when observing human and robot agents) using task-based functional MRI (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–27 with results reported for the healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects task activation analyses (repetition suppression and discrete event-related contrasts), with cluster-corrected results and whole-brain maps referenced and deposited on NeuroVault (meets I5 and I6). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core content is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment on observation and motor imagery of face and limb movements, explicitly addressing social communication and gesture processing (social-related task). Participants were healthy adults (n=14, mean age 25.2). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects ANOVA, SPM2) with FWE-corrected thresholds and MNI coordinates in tables/figures. Results for the healthy control sample are reported directly (no exclusive subgroup-only or patient contrasts). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy age group only, non-empirical) are met. Thus the paper satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of perception of facial expressions (social communication/perception of others), using a task involving viewing facial expressions during fMRI. Participants were healthy adults (n=24, mean age 25.2). The authors performed group-level mixed-effects analyses and generated parameter estimate maps for each expression and registered them to MNI space; additionally a group-level faces>scrambled (localiser) contrast was used to define whole-brain face-selective ROIs. Thus the paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps from healthy participants and meets the review’s reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social communication and intention understanding in healthy adults (N=23, mean age 24), using a task with communicative vs private actions. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt; interaction effects) with stereotaxic coordinates, thresholding, conjunction and PPI results, and tables/figures describing activations. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (coordinates and figures provided).
