No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range sample) are met.

This is an fMRI study of communicative interaction (social communication) in healthy adult participants (54 right-handed males, ages 18–27). The task probes social-related processing (establishment of mutual understanding) and uses task-evoked fMRI with whole-brain group-level analyses (reported contrasts, parametric modulations, and cluster-level inference), including anatomical localization and coherence analyses. Whole-brain results are described in the main text and figures (with supplementary materials), satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, healthy adult group reported separately). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (learning about and simulating others’ inter-temporal preferences and social influence on valuation) using a task that requires evaluating self and others. The sample comprises healthy adult participants within the 18–65 range (behavioral N=27, fMRI N=29 with exclusions), with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (second-level random effects analyses, cluster-defining thresholds, FWE-corrected clusters) with coordinates and statistical maps described in the text and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, includes healthy adults, is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (maternal response to infant cry; attachment/affiliation), conducted in adults (primiparous mothers, mean age 24.1, within 18–65) who are described as not meeting current major depressive episode criteria at scanning. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (own cry > control/other cry) using FSL with cluster correction and presents coordinates, tables, and figures of activation clusters. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (results clearly described with tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes; mental-state and age-judgement versions) (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n≈25; ages 18–59) reported separately (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation results for healthy controls (see Supplementary Tables S2 and S3) with cluster-wise FWE correction and voxelwise thresholds, i.e., unmasked whole-brain statistical maps/analyses (I5). Results are presented in main text, tables and figures (I6). Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no resting/connectivity-only, healthy-group whole-brain effects are provided, and participants are within age range).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (charitable giving, empathy, perspective taking, attentional reorienting) in healthy adult participants (n=33, ages 20–34), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects group analyses, searchlight MVPA, GLM contrasts) with reported significant clusters and coordinates (Tables/Figures) clearly from the healthy sample. Whole-brain results are described and thresholded (p<0.05 FWE voxel-level), and results are presented in tables/figures. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (effortful control of interpersonal trust/distrust) in healthy adult participants (n=59–60, mean age ~20, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., trust > age, distrust > age, and combined contrasts) with family-wise error correction and provides tables/figures and MNI coordinates. Whole-brain results and coordinates are clearly reported in the text/tables/figures, and ROI analyses are supplementary but do not replace whole-brain results. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=26, ages 19–26) that used a task contrasting social vs non-social reading passages and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (Social>Non-social; Vivid>Abstract) with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinates (Table 1, figures). The task probes social cognition/Theory of Mind (perception/understanding of others). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. All required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing/inferring others’ preferences) using task-based functional MRI. Participants were healthy adults (n=64; ages 18–26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (parametric modulation by self–other discrepancy), with voxelwise thresholds, cluster sizes, and MNI coordinates (Table 1, figures, and Methods). Results are reported for the healthy participant group and not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (n=14, mean age 35.9) that explicitly manipulates a social interaction (human–human vs human–machine competition) to engage Theory of Mind/social processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (contrasts such as [H(I+C)>M(I+C)], [I(H+M)>C(H+M)], interaction [H(I>C)]>[M(I>C)]) with voxelwise thresholding (P<0.001 uncorrected) and tables/figures listing activated clusters and Talairach/MNI coordinates. Results for the healthy sample are presented clearly. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked maps reported (tables and figures).

This study used fMRI during a social cognition task (HCP Animated Triangles) and reports task-related BOLD activation for healthy control participants separately. Healthy controls (n=25) are analyzed and results for the control group are presented with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (MNI coordinates, T-values) thresholded at p<0.05 FWE whole-brain corrected and shown in figures/tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps for controls), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI hyperscanning study of joint attention and mutual gaze (social interaction, social communication/perception). Participants: healthy adult volunteers (ages reported, n provided). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (tables of coordinates, cluster-level FWE-corrected results, figures) clearly from the healthy/control group. Whole-brain results are described in text and tables. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15, ages 20–28) that includes social-related processing (social distance: friends vs acquaintances) and uses task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise searchlight analyses (cross-domain MVPA classification and representational similarity analysis) with statistical maps and cluster results (FDR-corrected) identifying right IPL and other regions; figures and tables present these whole-brain results. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (mental state judgments), in healthy adult participants (final imaging sample N=113, ages 18–31). It includes group-level, whole-brain analyses: a parcel-based whole-brain mega-analysis reporting spatial distribution of effects across 200 cortical parcels (with significance testing and figures/supplementary), and network-level whole-brain pattern analyses. Results are reported at the group level for the healthy sample and supplemental materials/figures provide whole-brain maps. Data and code are openly available. Therefore it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related task in healthy adults with whole-brain results.

This is a non-empirical review article that summarizes cases and neuroimaging literature on ecstatic experiences, epilepsy variants, Stendhal syndrome, and autoscopic phenomena. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (Non-empirical paper without original fMRI data in healthy adults). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not present an original fMRI social-related task in healthy adults), I4 (no original sample of healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from a healthy/control group), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete for a review article (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based functional MRI while participants performed a social-affective judgment task (rating emotions evoked by images of social groups), directly addressing social perception/understanding of others. Participants were healthy adult undergraduates (mean age 19.5), satisfying the sample-age criterion. The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and contrast results (e.g., mPFC, insula, amygdala activations) clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Results are reported as whole-brain effects (Talairach coordinates, t-values) and in-text contrasts, fulfilling the reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This fMRI study is an auditory attention/motion-detection task (identifying direction of crossing footsteps) in healthy adult participants (ages 20–29) and uses whole-brain, random-effects GLM contrasts (‘footstep minus rest’) reported at group level (maps in supplementary material) and subsequent connectivity analyses. It therefore meets inclusion criteria I4 (healthy adult sample) and I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map). It also satisfies I6 (whole-brain results presented in supplementary figures/tables). However, the task is not a social-related task targeting constructs such as affiliation, social communication, or perception/understanding of self/others—the paradigm manipulates auditory attention to motion and does not probe social processing. Therefore it fails I3 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (n=45, ages 18–34) using a reappraisal generation task (RGT) that requires participants to imagine anger-eliciting, interpersonal scenarios and generate reappraisals — a social-cognitive task involving perception/understanding of others, empathy/theory-of-mind processes. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and task contrasts) with FWE correction and reports activation clusters in standard tables/figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task results), and I6 (results reported as tables/figures in text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, age appropriate, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of theory-of-mind/false-belief processing in healthy adults (mean age 22.7) using task-based fMRI while participants watched Sally–Anne movies (social-related task). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts are reported (belief > photo/map; implicit false- > true-belief) with SPMs and peak coordinates. Results for the healthy adult sample are presented separately. Thus all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of Theory of Mind (a social cognition task). It includes a healthy control group of adults (age-matched controls, n=13) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation results (within-group activations and coordinates, Table 3; figures show whole-brain statistical maps for contrasts such as ToM vs Physical). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (direct and reflected self-appraisals; perception/understanding of self and others) and includes a healthy adult sample (N=12, ages 22.6–30.4). The manuscript provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, conjunctions, between- and within-group contrasts) clearly identified for the adult group, with reported coordinates, thresholds, and correction procedures. Adult results are reported separately from the adolescent sample. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results presented in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–32) that used task-based fMRI to compare person-related (social) fact learning with non-social categories and a nonsemantic control. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions, ANOVA, cluster-corrected maps) are reported and interpreted for the healthy sample. The task probes perception/understanding of others (social conceptual processing), satisfying the review objective.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective. It uses task-based fMRI during social-related processing (compassion/reappraisal to images of others’ suffering) (I3). The sample comprises healthy adults aged 18–45 with results reported separately for the healthy groups (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (e.g., Group × Redistribution Rank whole-brain interaction, IPC and DLPFC clusters, whole-brain corrected results), satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain task-evoked map (I5). Results are described in the main text and figures/tables (I6). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social perception (decoding emotion/age from faces) in healthy adults (final N=25, ages 21–33), and reports group-level whole-brain analyses (random-effects faces > objects contrast and whole-brain searchlight results, with tables/figures). The healthy/control group results are reported clearly for the within-group effects. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=40 behavioral, n=34 fMRI; ages 19.5–32.7) that used task-based fMRI during a social task (trust game with partner pupil manipulations). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (whole-brain GLM results, cluster thresholds, coordinates, and ROI analyses) clearly identified for the healthy/control group. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an fMRI investigation of a social task (Trust Game) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain voxelwise coordinates, but the reported second-level results are comparisons between two healthy subgroups (high-Mach vs low-Mach). The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group as a whole (or for an unrestricted healthy group), only between-group contrasts. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 19–30), I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain task-evoked map from a non-narrow healthy/control group). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 21–48) that used an active task (viewing erotic pictures and videos of other people) engaging perception of others and reward-related/social-affiliative processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (within-group male vs female stimulus contrasts for each orientation group) with corrected thresholds (p<0.05 FWE) and cluster reports, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The sample is healthy adults and results for the healthy groups are reported separately. Whole-brain results are presented in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criterion (ROI-only, resting-state-only, age outside range, non-empirical) is violated. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 for the meta-analysis.

The paper reports an fMRI experiment probing social cognition (self/other processing, cooperation/competition), fulfilling the social task requirement. Sample: healthy adult participants (final N=24, ages 19–31) meeting the age/sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results (family-wise error cluster-corrected whole-brain contrasts, Table 1 and associated figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements; whole-brain results are described in text and figures (acceptable reporting format). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This article is a non-empirical review/perspective (Exclusion E6). It does not report original fMRI data or any healthy adult participant sample — no task-based fMRI methods, no group-level whole-brain activation maps, and no reported within-group healthy-control results. Inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, discussion, etc.), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper is a narrative review/overview of amygdala structure/function in neurodevelopmental disorders, not an original empirical fMRI study in healthy adults. It does not report any group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from a healthy adult sample, nor does it present primary task fMRI data. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task in the report), I4 (a reported healthy adult group aged 18–65), and I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task maps). It meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Full text appears complete for a review article. Given these points, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an original fMRI study of social communication (vitality forms) in healthy adults (N=18, ages ~25), using task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (vitality vs. control), conjunctions, coordinates (MNI), and PFWE-corrected results (Table 1, figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (adequate reporting). No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Multifaceted Empathy Test) that probes cognitive and emotional empathy (I3). The sample includes healthy adult control groups (female, age-matched, N≈29–30) reported separately from the BPD patients (I4). The manuscript provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation results for the control/healthy group (tables of activations, coordinates, and main-effect maps/descriptions), using standard GLM mixed-effects analyses and reporting thresholds (I5). Results are reported in-text and in tables/figures (coordinates), satisfying acceptable reporting formats (I6). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only reporting, or non-empirical design). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is INCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI assessing self-related olfactory evaluation (a social-related construct: Perception/Understanding of Self). Participants were healthy adult women (ages 18–35), and group-level fMRI contrasts (e.g., ‘self’-peptide minus solvent; ‘self’-peptide minus ‘non-self’-peptide) were computed using SPM and reported with MNI coordinates and thresholds. The paper states that whole-brain analysis was performed and provides voxelwise activation coordinates and statistical values for group contrasts in the healthy sample. Results are reported in the main text and figures. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social/self task), I4 (healthy adults), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported for the healthy group), and I6 (coordinates/figures provided). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI study of reactive social aggression using a social interaction task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) with human opponents, probing perception/understanding of others and social decision-making. Sample: healthy adults (n=15 analyzed; mean age ~22.9), within 18–65. Methods report whole-brain random-effects, voxelwise GLM analyses and report group-level activation maps and stereotaxic coordinates (tables/figures) for decision and outcome contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, pediatric/older-only sample, or non-empirical paper). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (audio-visual social-norm inference) performed during scanning, meeting I3. The sample includes a healthy control group of adults (TD; 22 included; ages 18–35) reported separately from the HFA group, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (e.g., contrasts such as all-stimuli vs fixation, visual GLM contrasts, auditory GLM contrasts, congruency GLM) and describes voxelwise activations and group-level statistical results, satisfying I5 (whole-brain evidence). Results are reported in text and figures/tables with coordinate-level/univariate contrasts, satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, reports within-group (healthy) whole-brain effects, includes participants within 18–65, and is an empirical fMRI paper. Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of person-related (social) memory and knowledge retrieval (status, personality traits, identity), using task fMRI in healthy adult participants (Study 1: n=24, Mage≈23; Study 2: n=26, Mage≈20). The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate GLM contrasts (e.g., all memory > baseline; status > baseline; trait > baseline; face > name; name > face) thresholded at voxel-level FWE P<0.05 and provides coordinates/tables and figures for these maps. Thus it satisfies social task fMRI (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps (I5), with acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state/only connectivity, no between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses fMRI during a social task (Trust Game) and reports neural correlates, but the sample consists of adolescents across three developmental phases rather than healthy adults (18–65). No subgroup of healthy adults is reported separately. Therefore it fails the sample inclusion criterion (I4) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (participants only outside the 18–65 range).

This is an fMRI study of abstraction/concretization using Why-How and Categories-Exemplars tasks that probe social-cognitive processing (e.g., action identification, mentalizing). Sample: 24 healthy adult participants (ages 18–27) reported separately. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts and conjunction analyses are reported (thresholds, cluster correction, tables of regions and figures). The full paper includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–65). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion) (I3); the sample comprises healthy adults within the 18–65 range with group-level results reported separately for the healthy participants (I4); the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses and cluster-corrected maps and tables of coordinates for contrasts (social exclusion > fair play, same- vs other-gender exclusion) (I5); results are presented in text/tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: whole-brain analyses are reported (not ROI-only), it is not a connectivity- or resting-state-only study, not limited to between-group contrasts, participants are within the age range, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore INCLUDED.

Although this fMRI study investigates social-related processing (personal familiarity/close relatives) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for the healthy control group, it explicitly studies ‘healthy elderly’ participants. The manuscript does not report a healthy adult sample within the required age range (18–65). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (only participants outside the 18–65 range with no qualifying healthy subgroup). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I5 (whole-brain healthy-group task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results are clearly described). Inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample age 18–65) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used a social-related task (facial emotion discrimination) addressing perception/understanding of others, enrolled healthy adult participants (control group ages 19–35), and reports group-level whole-brain task activation results (within-group contrasts for the normal control group and clusters/tables of whole-brain results with FWE-corrected thresholds). Whole-brain results are presented in tables and described in the text (not ROI-only), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of explicit emotion recognition (socially relevant stimuli: angry, fearful, etc.) in healthy adult males (age 21–33). The paper reports group-level whole-brain (whole-slab) analyses with activation maps and voxelwise results (thresholds reported, figures shown) and provides coordinate-based results for several regions, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Thus criteria for fMRI social task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group results are met.

The study reports fMRI during a social-cognitive (visual perspective-taking) task and includes a separate healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the authors explicitly state they used a region-of-interest approach and restricted analyzed voxels to the combined ROI mask rather than performing a whole-brain analysis. No unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation map is reported, and the paper therefore meets exclusion E2 (ROI-only analyses). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain group-level task map for healthy controls) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of peer/social influence during decision-making in healthy young adults (ages 21–24). It includes task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (peer observation during the Stoplight risky-driving task and Go/No-Go) satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adults within the 18–65 range (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/contrasts (e.g., No-Go>Go; Risk>Safe) with thresholding and provides NeuroVault links to thresholded/unthresholded maps, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). The study is not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only analyses, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Therefore it should be INCLUDED.

This study includes a healthy adult control group (I4) and uses an fMRI task involving social processing (interpersonal rejection and imagined aggression toward others) satisfying I3. However, the paper reports whole-brain task-related functional connectivity/network results and between-group (BPD vs. healthy) connectivity contrasts but does not present any unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map or healthy-group activation contrast clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met. It thus meets exclusion criteria: E3 (connectivity-only analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports primarily between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (action observation/representation of others’ actions and interactions), conducted in healthy adults (n=29, ages 18–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Observation > Neutral, Squeeze > No Squeeze, 2H DIFF > 2H SAME) with FWE correction and includes tables/figures of peak coordinates and statistical maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception/understanding of others’ actions; mentalizing vs mirror systems) using a task where participants classify biological vs artificial motion, satisfying the review’s social-processing scope. Sample: healthy adult participants reported (n=12, right-handed, mean age 27.3±4.7), meeting the age and healthy-group requirement. Whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses are reported using SPM2 with FDR correction and tables of activated regions/coordinates (Tables 1 and 2) and figures; thus whole-brain evidence is available and clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult, or non-empirical paper). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-processing task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Task) contrasting mental-state vs age judgments (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (n=28) and age-matched control subgroups (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and corrected group Z statistic images from factorial models, and describes within-group/control-group effects (e.g., left MFG greater activity in controls; younger vs older control comparisons; Supporting Information, Table III), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment using a social-attribution task (subjects judged another’s awareness) in a healthy adult sample (n=50; ages 18–49), with subsequent group-level, whole-brain contrasts (H trials − E trials) reported and thresholded, plus tables of peak coordinates and figures. Whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps for the healthy/control group are clearly described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (MRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses task fMRI of social processing (cyberball) and includes a healthy adult control group (satisfies I3 and I4). However, the full text reports primarily between-group contrasts (BPD vs NSSI and conjunctions vs HC) and does not present or clearly describe an unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (within-group/ main effect) for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criterion I5 requires a healthy-group whole-brain map (or equivalent tabulated coordinates/figure) clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. Because the paper only reports between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain effect, it meets exclusion criterion E4.

This paper reports an fMRI study of emotional prosody comprehension—a social-communication task involving perception/understanding of others’ emotions—so it addresses the review objective. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=19, ages 18–51), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (e.g., emotional vs. neutral, complex vs. simple contrasts) with cluster-corrected results and tables/figures of coordinates. Thus whole-brain healthy-group task effects are clearly presented. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not a between-group-only contrast, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study used task-based fMRI to examine perception of face gender, which falls under ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’ (a social-related construct). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages 19–42) with group results reported for the healthy sample. Importantly, the paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxel-wise random-effects analyses (gender-different > gender-same), with cluster-corrected maps and reported activated clusters/coordinates, fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. ROI analyses are also present but do not preclude inclusion because whole-brain results are reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses task-based fMRI of emotional facial expression processing (a social-communication/social-perception task) in 12 healthy subjects and reports task-evoked BOLD signal increases across many brain regions (implicit and explicit contrasts), consistent with whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Although exact participant ages are not reported in the provided text, participants are described as healthy subjects (implying adults). Therefore the study meets the social-related fMRI, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain results criteria.

The study used fMRI with social/attachment narratives and enrolled healthy adult participants (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the paper reports only resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity analyses (post-narrative FC) and does not present any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only seed-based/resting-state connectivity reported without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 24.4) that investigates social-context modulation of empathy for others' pain. The task is social-related (perception/understanding of others' pain/intentionality). The paper reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise contrasts (main effects and interactions) with coordinates and FDR-corrected results across the healthy sample. Results are presented in tables and figures and report group-level activation maps and PPI connectivity, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports an fMRI investigation of emotional prosody processing, a social-related task (perception/understanding of others). It includes a healthy adult control group (mean ages 32, range 20–46) reported separately. The paper provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation results for controls (conjunction and separate within-group contrasts; FWE cluster-corrected whole-brain analyses) and reports coordinates and figures. Reporting meets acceptable formats (text, figures, corrected whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within age range). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of gesture–speech integration, a social-communication task (I3). It includes healthy adult samples (H-group, C-group) reported separately with ages in the 19–32 range and matched controls (I4). The manuscript presents whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results for the healthy/control groups (contrasts and conjunctions; coordinates and cluster tables referenced), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state analyses, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are explicitly reported. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (dynamic facial-expression perception and imagery) in healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age ~25), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level GLM/RFX analyses and thresholded statistical maps (localizer and imagery runs, whole-brain comparisons across groups) rather than ROI-only results. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses fMRI in healthy adult controls (n=10) and reports whole-brain group activation maps, but the task is a monetary-reward continuous performance task (attention/reward), not a social-related task. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for controls), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (task is not social-related; constructs like social communication, affiliation, or perception of others are not the task focus). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social cognition (Reading-the-Mind-in-the-Eyes Test), satisfying I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (H; n=18) with results reported separately, satisfying I4. The methods state that single-group (1-sample t) whole-brain second-level analyses were conducted for each of the five groups and the paper reports whole-brain task-evoked activation results (figures/tables and cluster-level PFWE-corrected results, and planned contrasts involving H), satisfying I5 and I6. The paper also provides coordinate tables, figures, and ROI analyses but contains whole-brain voxelwise maps for the task. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group main effect, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, figures). Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study used resting-state fMRI and connectome-wide (MDMR/seed-based) analyses correlating intrinsic connectivity with emotional intelligence; it did not use a task-based social fMRI paradigm or report any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps for the healthy group. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (resting-state analyses only without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes a healthy adult group aged 18–45 with results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI during a social-related task) and I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from healthy participants). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on task-evoked social fMRI in healthy adults.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (social reasoning/theory-of-mind and emotion understanding) in healthy adult participants (N=45; ages 19-23). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects results, multiple-comparison correction, peak coordinates in Appendix A, and whole-brain maps/figures), satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked maps from the healthy group. Results for social tasks are clearly described and contrasted with mechanical tasks. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only groups, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (reciprocity in the Trust Game) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise contrasts (e.g., defect > reciprocate; regressions; ROI analyses supplement) with MNI coordinates, thresholding procedures, and correction details. All required inclusion criteria are met: (I3) social-related task using fMRI; (I4) healthy adult sample (18–22) reported separately; (I5) whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are reported and described; (I6) whole-brain results are presented in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=60; ages 18–60) that uses a social-related task (observation of mouth actions/oral communicative actions and biting across human and animal actors) probing social communication and empathy. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (second-level random effects SPM analyses, p<0.05 FWE), with tables/figures of activations and within-group contrasts for the healthy participant groups. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an fMRI investigation with healthy adult controls and reports whole-brain within-group activation maps for the control group (I4, I5, I6 met). However, the fMRI tasks are verbal executive paradigms (verbal fluency and Hayling sentence completion) aimed at response generation and inhibition, not social-related processing. Although the introduction mentions social cognition behaviorally, no social-affiliation/communication or perception-of-self/others task was used during fMRI. Therefore inclusion criterion I3 (social-related task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social processing (emotion alignment with an interaction partner) using an interactive social task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=20; mean age ~24), and results are reported for the healthy scanner group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with clusterwise FWE correction across the entire brain and presents activation results in tables/figures (e.g., Tables 2–3, Figures 3–4). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) are met.

This study includes an fMRI social-cognition task (social interaction vs. random movement) and reports group-level task activation analyses. Participants are healthy adults from HCP (ages 22–36+; n≈100) and UCLA (ages 21–50; n=114), satisfying the age and sample requirements. The paper describes voxel-wise GLM activation analyses and presents group-level activation results (e.g., Figure 1 and accompanying text), fulfilling the whole-brain task-evoked map requirement. Reporting formats include figures and supplementary material; these are clearly identified as healthy/control group results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without activation maps, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

This is an fMRI study of self/other social cognition (trait judgments), using healthy adult participants (N=13, mean age 24.2). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and statistical parametric maps with tables of coordinates and figures (SPM analyses, whole-brain thresholds described). Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group-level results (I5), and allowance for coordinate/figure reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly probes social-related processing: participants performed meaning-relatedness judgments on social concepts (social vs. animal-function word pairs). The sample includes healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 29.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (categorical subtraction at whole-brain thresholds, conjunction analyses, and coordinates reported in tables/figures), and whole-brain results are clearly described for the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (kinship/ moral dilemma) in healthy adults. It used whole-brain, task-based fMRI during an ecologically valid movie-viewing social/moral task and a separate moral-decision task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 19–39). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from inter-subject correlation (ISC) analyses and a GLM analysis of the moral-decision task, with multiple-comparison correction and tables/figures of clusters and coordinates (and unthresholded maps referenced). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults. Participants: 19 healthy, right-handed adults aged 19–28 (meets I4). Task: categorical knowledge and feature verification tasks included social-category (stereotype) judgments (meets I3). Analyses: whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise contrasts reported (e.g., ‘social’>‘non-social’ and ‘non-social’>‘social’) with tables of peak voxels and figures (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within 18–65 (E5), and this is original empirical fMRI data (not a review; E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion included). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly investigates perception/understanding of others’ emotional facial expressions (social-related processing). Participants: 27 healthy adults (mean age 27) — meets age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., canonical disgust vs neutral; canonical disgust vs distaste) analyzed with random-effects SPM2 and reports cluster coordinates, tables and figures. Results are not limited to ROI-only analyses (an ROI SVC was used but whole-brain results are reported). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based functional MRI of social cognition (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception) in healthy adults (ages 18–32). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise contrasts (e.g., faces associated with behaviors vs. novel faces; negative vs. positive; disgust vs. aggression) with Talairach coordinates, cluster volumes, and statistical thresholds reported in tables and figures. Results for the healthy/control sample are reported separately and not limited to ROIs; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (mentalizing, empathy, prosocial behavior) in healthy adult participants (N=32, females, mean age 22.7). The tasks are social-cognitive (mentalizing, empathy for pain, prosocial decision), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., Mentalizing > baseline; Dissimilar > Similar; Painful > Non-Painful) with cluster-level correction and tables/figures of coordinates/results. Healthy adult sample and separate reporting of healthy-group results are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social evaluation (social judgments of target persons) in healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–29), meeting the review focus. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (a whole-brain multilevel model/MLM, cluster tables and MNI coordinates; ROI analyses are supplementary), with results clearly from the healthy/control sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment manipulating social context (collaboration, competition) during a handgrip effort task—i.e., a social-related task—and includes healthy adult participants (N=32, ages 18–39). The paper provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM results, cluster-level FWE correction) with tables/figures of activations (e.g., ventral basal ganglia, TPJ, mPFC), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related facial emotion recognition task (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (mean age ~23.6) with results reported separately (meets I4). The paper provides group-level whole-brain analyses and reports whole-brain clusters/coordinates for the healthy control group (e.g., NTOXT>PLA clusters in inferior frontal gyrus and fusiform gyrus), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (meets I5). Whole-brain results are reported in the text and tables (meets I6). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study using a real-world social task (speed-dating) that probes social/affiliative processing and learning from romantic interest/rejection, meeting social-related task requirement. Sample includes healthy adult participants (scanned N=38, ages 19–31) with participant screening described, satisfying the sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., yes vs no; Match vs Unrequited), thresholding and cluster-correction, and tables of coordinates and figures, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study used task-based fMRI of naturalistic social (theory-of-mind) processing, includes a healthy adult control group (n=22, ages 19–46) with results reported separately, and reports whole-brain, group-level within-group task contrasts (ToM > physical inference) for the control group with cluster-corrected activations and coordinate tables/figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Full text unavailable (paywalled). Only title, authors, journal metadata and DOI are provided; core article content (methods, results) is not accessible. Cannot verify inclusion criteria: I3 (unclear whether an fMRI social-related task was used), I4 (uncertain whether a healthy adult group (18–65) was tested and reported separately), I5 (no information on whole-brain, healthy-group task-evoked maps), I6 (no confirmation that whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria can be confirmed from the available metadata. Full text incomplete, so study is excluded pending access to full article for proper assessment.

The study is an fMRI task of social evaluation in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the manuscript reports group-level results that were small-volume corrected within a predefined vACC ROI and presents ROI-restricted activation clusters. There is no clear report of an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Because the paper appears to report only ROI-restricted analyses without accompanying whole-brain task-evoked results, it violates the review requirement for whole-brain evidence (E2).

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It uses task-based fMRI to probe a social cognition construct (empathy for pain) (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 18–40 with group-level results reported separately (stress and control healthy groups) (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses with family-wise error correction and presents whole-brain results (figures and coordinate tables) for contrasts (e.g., INJECTION>QTIP and BIOPSY>QTIP) and group comparisons (I5, I6). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 20–34) that uses a passive action observation task probing action perception/understanding (mirror system) — a social-related construct. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and contrasts, thresholded and reported with coordinates and peaks) for the healthy control groups and describes results across mirror system areas. Therefore it meets the fMRI social-processing task requirement, the healthy adult sample requirement, and provides whole-brain group-level task activation maps clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3, I4, I5, I6.

This study used task-based fMRI to examine neural responses to emotional speech prosody (a social-communication/social-perception task) in healthy adult participants (N=22, mean age 24.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation results (emotional > neutral prosody) with cluster-corrected statistics and figures/tables describing these effects. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-cognition task (why/how action processing; mentalizing/default-mode network analyses), with healthy adult participants (Study 1: mean age ~25, range 21–33; Study 2: similar), and reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps and contrasts (conjunction analyses, thresholding, cluster-corrections, figures/tables). All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this fMRI study examines social communication (dynamic facial expressions) in a healthy adult sample (meets I3 and I4), the reported analyses and results are restricted to ROI/small-volume-corrected statistics. The paper documents ROI-based SPM analyses (small volume correction using WFU PickAtlas) and reports FWE-corrected peaks within those ROIs; conjunction and interaction tests were conducted within specified ROIs. The manuscript does not present or describe an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (no whole-brain thresholded maps or whole-brain voxelwise results are reported independent of ROI/SVC). Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence and is excluded under E2 (ROI-only results).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals) using task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants (ages 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain contrasts (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical; individual mental > individual physical) with tables of significant regions, corrected thresholds, and figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Behavioral and imaging methods, participant characteristics, and univariate and multivariate analyses are fully described for the healthy sample. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social decision-making paradigm (modified Trust Game) directly probing reciprocity/trust (social-related processing). The sample comprised healthy adult participants aged 18–30 (reported group-level results for the healthy sample). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical contrasts (GLM one-sample/t-tests with cluster correction) and provides tables/figures of activation coordinates. Reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures satisfies the meta-analysis reporting requirement. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-adult sample) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (gaze/joint attention) in healthy adults. It uses task-based BOLD fMRI with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; within-subjects ANOVA; voxelwise t-statistics; multiple contrasts reported, tables of activated loci). Sample comprises healthy adult volunteers (behavioral N=10, fMRI N=12), ages 18–40, satisfying the adult age range. Reported whole-brain task activation maps and voxelwise contrasts (e.g., gaze shift − no movement; incorrect − correct; social − unsocial) meet the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range samples) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and figures/tables summary, so appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (mental state attribution/intentional stance) in healthy adults. The analyzed sample (N=12; ages 21–31) is within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (Composer > Computer) entered into a second-level random-effects analysis, with coordinates and cluster thresholds provided (tables and figures). Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group. Behavioral and imaging results directly target perception/understanding of others, meeting the meta-analysis objectives.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 18–33) performing a social-related task (perception/integration of others’ emotional facial and vocal cues), satisfying the review’s domain (social perception/understanding of others). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and provide tables of coordinates and whole-brain thresholds (explicit whole-brain contrasts and conjunctions are described), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, and is empirical).

This paper reports an fMRI experiment manipulating social competition (a social-related task involving social comparison/mentalizing). Sample: healthy adult participants (female, ages 18–35; N=20 after exclusion), satisfying the adult healthy-sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses and contrasts (e.g., competition > no-competition; working-memory parametric modulators), including cluster thresholds, Monte Carlo correction, peak coordinates, and figures/tables describing whole-brain results. Whole-brain results are explicitly described for the healthy/control group (not limited to a narrow subgroup). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception: participants (N=21 healthy adult males, ages 23–33) viewed and rated dyadic nonverbal interactions during task-based fMRI. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8 random-effects flexible factorial ANOVA) with contrasts and cluster-level corrected results and coordinate tables/figures for the healthy group. Core article content (introduction, detailed methods, behavioral and fMRI results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=7, ages 20–35) that uses a sentence-reading task whose stimuli include sentences describing social interactions and people. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (factor analysis across cortex, identification of voxel clusters and group-level brain locations associated with a ‘people/social interactions’ factor; results summarized in main text and Supporting Information), and thus provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps/cluster locations for the healthy participants. The task involves processing of social content (perception/understanding of others) as evidenced by a dedicated People/Social Interactions factor and associated brain regions. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports group × drug interactions and provides brain maps collapsed across group/drug, but does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related emotional face matching task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, ages 21–64, reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain healthy-group task map presented) and I6 (no healthy-group whole-brain results clearly described for controls in text/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related interpersonal distance (affiliation) task; (I4) the sample includes healthy adult participants (19 males, ages 18–30) with results reported for the healthy group; (I5) group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects GLM, FDR q<0.05) with reported main effects and treatment×protagonist interaction and listed brain regions; (I6) whole-brain results are described in the text (with follow-up ROI analyses reported separately). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only contrasts, ages within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of self-face recognition, which falls under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Self). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (10 right-handed adults, mean age 26.9), and results are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (self vs other, other vs self) with cluster-corrected thresholding and tables of MNI coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, or non-empirical) apply.

All inclusion criteria are met. I3: The study used task-based fMRI contrasting social vs. non-social images (valence appraisal task), isolating social-related processing. I4: The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=14 analyzed; ages 23–50), with psychiatric screening and separate reporting of healthy-group results. I5: The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (social–nonsocial contrast, voxel thresholding, FDR-corrected cluster results, conjunction maps). I6: Whole-brain results are presented in figures and cluster tables and clearly described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review objective of identifying fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult males (aged 18–35) using a social provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes social processing and decision-making after provocation. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (high>low provocation; decision and feedback phases) with MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction, clearly from the healthy/control sample. Hormonal/genotype groups are reported but healthy-group whole-brain task effects are presented and described. Therefore it meets the fMRI social-task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

Study reports an fMRI investigation of social communication (charades) probing mirroring and mentalizing processes—clearly a social-related task (I3). Sample includes healthy adult participants (n=18 analyzed, mean age 27.5) within 18–65 (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain differential Granger-causality maps and GLM results, thresholded and submitted to second-level inference (P<0.05 cluster-corrected), satisfying whole-brain reporting (I5). Results and maps are presented in main text/figures and supplementary material, consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain results (E2–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article reports an fMRI study of social impression updating (social cognition/perception of others), with healthy adult participants (N=21, ages 18–31). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., L2>F3 whole-brain contrasts, 2×4 ANOVA), reports corrected clusters and peak coordinates in tables and figures, and describes results for the healthy/control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, imaging acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (whole-brain contrasts, interaction, targeted contrasts), and Discussion, so core content is present and sufficient. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (social expectancy violations along warmth and competence) in healthy adult participants (mean age 20.4, n=12 analyzed). The task is explicitly social and uses task-evoked BOLD responses. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts and Talairach coordinates, cluster sizes, and corrected significance thresholds (i.e., whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants that uses a social-related task (perception/recognition of own vs. others' body parts — perception/understanding of self and others). Sample sizes and recruitment indicate healthy adults. The paper reports group-level voxelwise contrasts used to localize regions (e.g., body minus objects, objects minus body parts, with Talairach coordinates and voxel counts for EBA, V1/2, LOC) and provides coordinate-level whole-brain results in text/tables/figures. Although many analyses use ROI-extracted time courses and ANOVAs, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and coordinates are reported for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants and addresses social group processing (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (I5 not met). Analyses are reported at the ROI/region-averaged level (Harvard-Oxford 55-region masks and category/visual ROIs) and post hoc t-tests on regions, rather than an unmasked whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group activation map. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI/region-only analysis with no whole-brain voxelwise results).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=31, ages 18–26) that uses a social task (gambling for self, best friend, antagonist) directly addressing social-related processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and ANOVA results with coordinates (MNI) and tables, and describes whole-brain contrasts and interaction effects (Person × Outcome) with small-volume correction for a priori regions. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (pain empathy) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=21). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task analyses for each group separately (within-group contrasts and direct between-group comparisons), with results summarized in the main text and Supplementary Table S1 and figures, satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task map. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study (Study 2) that investigates social-cognitive processing (mentalizing/attribution of agency—perception and understanding of others) using a task of passive viewing of sexualized and clothed human targets. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (21 heterosexual men, age range within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (voxelwise threshold p<.001 with cluster correction via AlphaSim) and presents whole-brain contrasts and tables/figures (Tables 2 and 3, Figures 2–4) identifying activations and correlations with hostile sexism. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, or non-empirical) are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (impression formation about people vs objects) in healthy adults (N=14, ages 18.3–23.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical contrasts (e.g., person-impression > other trials) with thresholding (P<0.001) and tables/coordinates for peak activations, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Results are reported for the healthy sample (no clinical group confound). Thus it meets inclusion criteria for social fMRI in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps/coordinates.

This is an fMRI study of face perception that explicitly manipulates changeable, social aspects of faces (gaze direction, emotional expression, head/viewpoint) — constructs directly relevant to Social Communication (I3). The sample comprises eight healthy adult observers (healthy adult group reported; I4). The paper reports group-level statistical maps/analyses (FEAT Z-statistic images, Talairach coordinates, group-averaged time courses and reported coordinates/figures), meeting the whole-brain, voxelwise reporting requirement (I5) and presents coordinates/figures consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes a healthy adult task activation map, and is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Confidence is slightly reduced because exact participant ages (18–65) are not explicitly stated, but participants are described as typical healthy adult observers and ethical approval/consent was obtained, so inclusion is appropriate.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-cognitive task (neutral face processing, emotion recognition, affective ToM), in a sample of healthy adult participants (N=74; genotyping subset N=73). Whole-brain group-level analyses (one-sample t-tests, within-subject ANOVA) are reported with FWE-corrected results and figures; ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group are clearly described. Full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (masked fearful/happy eye whites) with a social-related task (eye-region emotion processing) in healthy adult participants (initial N=50, analyzed N=43; mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level SPM random-effects analyses and an exploratory whole-brain analysis with reported whole-brain activations (pulvinar, ACC, orbitofrontal cortex) and supplementary tables, and also reports within-group/placebo effects. Whole-brain results are clearly described for the healthy/control group. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROI-only, resting-state, or connectivity-only, and healthy adult group results are reported separately. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social decision-making paradigm (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) directly probing social cognition and trust, addressing the review objective. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (mean age 24.6, range consistent with 18–65) with group-level analyses reported for the healthy sample.
