The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise GLM results (group contrasts, interaction effects) with cluster-size correction and provide tables/figures and peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results for the healthy groups (prosocial vs proself) are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of prosody perception and production tied to social communication and empathy (social-related processing). Sample: 19 healthy, right-handed native-English adults aged 18–58 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., “happy-neutral”, “question-neutral”) thresholded and corrected (p<0.05 FDR, cluster k>5) and describes coordinates and supplementary materials; overlap/SVC and whole-brain contrasts are reported in text and figures. Results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. No evidence of ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range samples. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This empirical fMRI study reports task-evoked activation during an action imitation/observation paradigm, a social-related process (perception/understanding of others). It includes a healthy adult control group (N=16) with results for the healthy group reported separately. The paper reports within-group whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., imitation > nonimitative action; animated > nonanimated observation) with peak coordinates and corrected statistical maps described, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–55) using an explicit social task (imitate/observe emotional faces) probing perception/understanding of others. The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and group-level analyses (PLS and GLM) with voxelwise brain maps rendered in MNI space and thresholded voxel patterns reported, satisfying whole-brain task-evoked reporting. Healthy participant results are reported for the group (neuroimaging data from 20 participants used for final analysis). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain group-level task activation data.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (passive viewing of in-group/out-group facial expressions; disgust perception), with healthy adult participants (mean age ~21). The paper reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA, thresholding, reported significant clusters and tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports an fMRI experiment using a social interactive task (virtual handshake) probing social rejection — a social-related construct (mentalizing/perception of others). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=16, ages within 18–65) with results reported separately. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for the control group (refusal vs acceptance) are reported (regions, thresholds, cluster correction described). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social persuasion (celebrity ‘expert power’) using a social-related task (celebrity–object pairs) with healthy adult participants (young females, mean age 21.8). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects task-evoked activation analyses (thresholds, cluster correction) and lists activation clusters in tables/figures (whole-brain maps and ROI small-volume follow-ups). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study tests social interaction (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (n=30, mean age 21.2). The task probes social cooperation/defection (clearly a social-related construct). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (one-sample t tests, voxelwise thresholding p<.001, spatial extent thresholds) and whole-brain voxelwise exploratory correlations for the healthy sample, with results presented in text, figures, and tables. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI social task (anticipation of touching an animate vs inanimate target), uses healthy adult participants (ages 21–33), and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task results (paired-sample t-tests and FDR-corrected statistical maps and coordinates) clearly from the healthy sample. Whole-brain analyses with covariates (narcissism) are also reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-only, no between-group-only contrasts, age in range, empirical with original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory-of-mind: cooperation vs deception) in healthy adults (n=13, ages 22–38). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exploratory whole-brain ToM vs non-ToM with reported peaks, figures, and coordinate tables) and subsequent ROI comparisons based on those whole-brain results. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain effects). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI experiment explicitly probing social perception (judging facing-toward vs away of point-light and human-like walkers), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (N=16, mean age 22.75) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (ANOVAs, contrasts) with stereotaxic coordinates and thresholding (p<0.05 FWE) and tables/figures of activation; thus whole-brain evidence is available and reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Accordingly inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing using a socio-emotional preference task (Preference vs Gender) in healthy adults (N=21, ages 23–51). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (Preference>Gender and other contrasts) thresholded at p<0.05 FDR-corrected and provides tables of activation peaks and figures with coordinates. Core article content is present (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/tables/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (ages 23–39) using a social-judgment task (ambiguous social interactions) — matching the review’s social-related task domain. The sample consists of healthy adults within the 18–65 range. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, random-effects task contrasts (e.g., rough > no priming; rough > smooth) with FDR-corrected results, tables, and figures describing anatomical locations, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range participants) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study investigating processing of others' decisions (social cognition). It scanned 12 healthy adult participants (mean age 21) and reports group-level, voxelwise second-level SPM analyses (ANOVA contrasts and reported peak coordinates/figures), with small-volume correction applied to the ACC. Whole-brain voxelwise group results are described and coordinates/figures are provided for healthy subjects. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/figures acceptable). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a resting-state fMRI study (ICA/FNC) comparing ASD and TD groups; it does not use a task-based social processing paradigm and does not report any healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. The sample spans children and adolescents (ABIDE II age range includes 5–64 years) and no separate healthy adult (18–65) group results are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3 (task fMRI/social task), I4 (healthy adult group 18–65 reported separately), and I5 (whole-brain task-evoked map for healthy group). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (resting-state analyses without a healthy-group task map), E4 (no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect; only between-group/resting contrasts), and E5 (participants outside 18–65 with no separate adult-only healthy subgroup). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social attribution (a social-related task) that includes a healthy adult control group (ages 18–65) reported separately. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (group-by-empathy interaction and related group-specific effects) with cluster-level family-wise error correction and names specific brain regions showing effects in controls, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, healthy adult group data reported).

This is an fMRI study using the Cyberball social exclusion task (a social-related paradigm) with a healthy control group reported separately. Whole-brain, voxelwise within-group results are reported for healthy controls (main effect of condition in left anterior insula; voxelwise FWE-corrected p-values and coordinates provided). The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult control group), I5 (group-level whole-brain healthy-group task effect), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E2 met: the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) fMRI analyses with no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study uses task-based fMRI of social processing — social closeness judgments with friends vs unfamiliar faces) and I4 (sample includes healthy adult participants aged 19–30). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level task activation maps are reported; fMRI results are presented via ROI extractions rather than whole-brain voxelwise contrasts). Although the full text is complete and the study reports task fMRI in healthy adults, failure to provide whole-brain, group-level task activation maps means it cannot be included in this meta-analysis.

Exclusion reason: E2 (ROI-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — trustworthiness judgments) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, ages 18–35, with results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group is reported). The Methods and Results describe voxelwise preprocessing but all inferential results are presented as ROI-based percent signal change and ROI-based statistics; there are no whole-brain, unmasked healthy-group activation maps, coordinate tables, or figures reported for the control group. Therefore the study must be excluded per E2.

This is an event-related fMRI study of social attention (gaze following vs. finger pointing) in healthy adult participants (n=17, ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects second-level contrasts and cluster-corrected activations), figures of whole-brain activation patterns and ROI analysis; results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Thus it meets fMRI social-task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting requirements.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of self-face recognition, which falls under the social-related construct ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’ (I3). Participants are healthy adults (ages 19–24), meeting the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM), including reported coordinates and cluster-level statistics for contrasts (e.g., Morph 50% self vs. friend), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and acceptable reporting formats (I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participant ages within range, and it is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathy-for-pain (a social-related task) in adult participants including a healthy control group (ages 22–63). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., High Pain–Low Pain in Other, masked with Self) with coordinates and z-scores (reported in main text and Supplementary Table 1) and performs second-level random-effects analyses; results for control/healthy participants are reported separately. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full, and whole-brain results for the healthy group are clearly described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Exclusion rationale: E4 is met — the paper reports primarily between-group contrasts (patient vs. control) and region-wise percent signal extractions; it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group (control) task activation map or clearly reported voxelwise healthy-group contrast maps in the main text. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study uses task-based fMRI during a social-related attribution task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise map for the healthy/control group is provided), and I6 (while coordinates/tables are reported, they reflect between-group contrasts and are not clearly described as an unmasked healthy-group whole-brain effect). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

This is an fMRI task study of social-related processing: judgments of pride (a self-conscious/social emotion) and joy. Participants: 16 healthy adult (mean age 21.3–21.5) university students (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrasts (joy minus neutral; pride minus neutral; pride minus joy) with SPM, thresholding, tables of peak coordinates, and figures—meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results for the healthy/control group are reported clearly and separately. The full article text including methods, results, and discussion is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=24, mean age 25.7) using a social-related task (theory-of-mind/story paradigms contrasting social vs non-social conditions), meeting I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster results (Tables and text describing whole-brain contrasts for Background and Outcome segments), satisfying I5/I6. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within 18–65, and empirical with original fMRI data).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related task (emotion recognition of one’s own vs. unknown child), includes a healthy adult control group (mothers without ELM) with results reported separately, and provides group-level whole-brain task activation results (coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics). Specifically, whole-brain within-group effects are reported (e.g., CON mothers show a familiarity effect in the medial frontal gyrus) and whole-brain across-group and per-group contrasts (happy>neutral, own>unknown) are presented. Reporting includes voxelwise, whole-brain results (tables/coordinates and text). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

This is an fMRI study using a social-cognition task (modified Empathic Accuracy Task) that involves perception and understanding of others’ emotions. The sample comprises healthy adults (final fMRI sample N=34, ages 20–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects paired t-tests, TFCE FWE-corrected results) with tables and figures of significant clusters. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for healthy adult fMRI whole-brain task activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social/emotional face processing in healthy adults (N=30, mean age 24.2). The task is social-related (gender identification of angry and happy faces vs neutral shapes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain and ROI analyses are described; main effects of stimulus type and interaction contrasts are reported and supplemented with tables/figures), with results clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Whole-brain results are described in text and supplementary tables. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study uses fMRI during social-cognitive tasks (action observation/understanding) and includes a healthy adult control group, so I3 and I4 are met. However, the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group (control) task activation map or main-effect/within-group HC contrast. Reported whole-brain results are primarily between-group contrasts (ALS > HC and HC > ALS) and subgroup analyses; there is no clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task effect (HC main effect) presented in the full text. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task map). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E4.

Only abstract and metadata provided (full text incomplete). From the abstract, the study uses task fMRI in a social decision context, so I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) appears satisfied. However, the provided content does not report participant ages (cannot confirm 18–65), nor does it provide methods/results to verify a group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (I5) or that whole-brain results are reported in acceptable formats (I6). Therefore I4, I5, and I6 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be reliably applied based on the incomplete text. Recommend obtaining the full text to verify age range and whether whole-brain task activation maps are reported before inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of emotional face processing (a social-related perception/understanding of others task) in healthy adult volunteers. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Sample: 30 healthy, right-handed volunteers selected for genotype, screened for psychiatric disorders, with group-level results reported separately for the healthy groups. Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported (whole-brain comparisons at p < .001 uncorrected; Supplementary Table S3 referenced) and main effects across all subjects are presented, satisfying the requirement for an unmasked, group-level healthy control task activation map. Coordinate tables and figures with group-level statistics are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (integration of facial and vocal emotional expressions), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=24, mean age 26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts and FWE-corrected statistical maps and coordinates (e.g., multimodal > unimodal contrasts, congruency, emotion × modality interaction). Independent localizers and whole-brain results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 23.6) that used a social-related task (viewing two-person violent interactions with attention manipulated to aggressor vs. victim), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., focus on aggressor vs focus on victim) with statistical maps, figures and tables and describes preprocessing and GLM-based analyses, satisfying I5 and I6. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and core outcomes are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are in the 18–65 range, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Uses task-based fMRI to probe social-related processing (perception of others’ pupils/coherence between observer and observed), (I4) Healthy adult sample reported (N=14, mean age 22, 18–65 range), (I5) Reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (main effects and interactions reported with whole-brain thresholds and coordinate tables), (I6) Whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion provided. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of face perception/recognition (social perception of others) in healthy adults (n=18, age range 19–36). The task is social-related (face recognition/false recognition) meeting I3. The sample is healthy adults within 18–65 meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked analyses using Random Effects (RFX) and cluster correction and provides Talairach coordinates and figures for activations (e.g., right precentral and cingulate gyri), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Excluded because the paper does not provide a usable healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation map. Inclusion: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: agency/perception of self) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group) are met. Exclusion: E2 is met — the analyses rely on ROI results and report that whole-brain group-wise analyses produced no significant activations (no whole-brain task map/coordinates for the healthy group are provided). Inclusion criterion I5 (report at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map for the healthy/control group) is not met, so the study cannot be included. Full text appears complete.

The study uses task fMRI of emotion-word processing (a social-related construct: perception/understanding of self/others) and reports a healthy adult control group, but it does not clearly present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone. The results mostly report pooled (all participants) whole-brain maps, between-group (control > ASC) whole-brain contrasts, and ROI analyses; I cannot find a standalone, unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect (main effect or within-group contrast) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reporting between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported), I6 (whole-brain results are reported in acceptable formats). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task map).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (agreement with experts) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (I3, I4 met). However, the paper reports primarily between-group contrasts (controls > cocaine users) and ROI/SVC analyses; it does not provide an unmasked, within-group whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the paper does not report a whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related Theory of Mind task) and I6 (whole-brain results may be in tables/figures — task-related component maps and coordinate tables are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (although a healthy adult control group is included, results for the healthy group are not reported separately from the combined sample or as an unmasked control-group map) and I5 (no unambiguous whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map reported for the healthy/control group alone; reported maps are across all participants and between-group contrasts). Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports between-group contrasts and combined/group-mixed component maps without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social perception (processing of dynamic vs static facial expressions), involving healthy adult participants (mean ages ~25) and reporting group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrasts and coordinate tables (e.g., dynamic > static; ALE meta-analysis uses reported coordinates). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and provides whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates clearly identified as healthy-group effects. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of social gaze processing (social cognition/perception) using a task-based paradigm in healthy adults. Sample: 30 healthy adults aged 19–41, meeting the adult age range. The article reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (main effects and interactions) with thresholding and coordinates described, and whole-brain results are clearly attributed to the healthy group; supplementary PPI connectivity is reported but whole-brain task activation maps are also provided. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing using two social-cognitive tasks (Reading the Mind in the Eyes / EToM and basic emotion task / BET), fulfilling task relevance. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=14) reported separately from clinical groups. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise regression analyses for each group (controls, patients, siblings) with results described in the Whole brain regression section and specific regions listed, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly identified (regions correlating with TABS/SSPA and laterality indices). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=24, ages 19–31) performing a familiarity judgment for personally familiar, famous, and unfamiliar faces—an explicitly social-related task involving perception/understanding of others and social cognition. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were conducted using SPM5 with cluster-level correction and are reported in tables/figures (activation maps and peak coordinates). Post-scan behavioral measures and voxelwise contrasts (e.g., P1–Cp1, P1–F1, repetition suppression contrasts) are clearly described for the healthy/control group. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level reporting.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (impression formation of faces varying by race and status) in healthy adult participants (N=60 males, mean age 23.8). The task is clearly social (impression formation), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adults within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise multivariate PLS results (brain–behavior LVs) and displays/thresholds whole-brain voxel maps and cluster reports; GLM preprocessing and contrast images were used as input for PLS, providing group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state/seed-only, between-group-only, outside age range, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (prediction of others' behavior framed as desires vs. rules) in healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 18–44). The paper reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level flexible factorial models, cluster- and voxel-level correction, tables/coordinates and figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of explicit social trait judgments (trustworthiness, attractiveness) on vocal stimuli in healthy adults (N=44, ages 21–60). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts with cluster-level FWE-corrected maps and peak coordinates (MNI), and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Stimuli and tasks clearly probe social-related processing. There is no indication of ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses nor restriction to special/clinical groups. Full text (methods, results) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (self vs. other processing with romantic partner video vignettes) in healthy adults aged 23–40. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (one-sample t-tests, ANOVA) with voxelwise FWE correction and tables/figures of activations. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of anticipatory interpersonal touch (a clearly social-related task) in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task contrasts (e.g., Target, Modality, Target×Modality interactions) with cluster-level correction, figures, and a table of coordinates; analyses include conjunctions and voxel-wise results within a tactile localizer mask. Results for the healthy/control group are reported directly (not limited to a subgroup). The study is empirical and not ROI-only, resting-state, or between-group-only. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not provide healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked fMRI results. Exclusion IDs met: E2 (only ROI/seed/network-based resting-state and graph analyses with no whole-brain task activation maps) and E3 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity and graph metrics without any healthy-group task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no task-based fMRI of social processing; fMRI data are resting-state and the social ToM task was behavioral/outside the scanner), I4 (while a healthy volunteer group is included, participants span ages 12–24 and no separate healthy adult (18–65) subgroup is reported as required), and I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group is reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract provided). The abstract indicates this is an fMRI study of prosodic categorisation relevant to social communication (meets I3). However, the available text does not confirm key required details: participant sample characteristics and age range (I4) are not reported in the abstract, and it is not possible to verify that the paper reports at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group (I5/I6). Because these inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study cannot be included based on the available information. No exclusion criteria E2–E6 are explicitly met from the abstract alone.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (gaze perception) meeting the review objective. It includes a healthy adult control group (separate analyses reported). Voxelwise task contrasts are reported and described for the control group (e.g., controls direct gaze > averted gaze) with coordinates and figures/tables; whole-brain contrasts (faces vs. null) are referenced as FWE-corrected at the whole-brain level. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants examining neural responses to perceiving others' actions (mirror system) via auditory and visual modalities—clearly within the construct of Perception and Understanding of Others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (t contrasts, cluster correction, Talairach maps) for sighted and congenitally blind healthy adults, with results for the healthy groups reported separately. Participant ages and group descriptions indicate adults in the 18–65 range. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study uses a social-interactive task (pseudo-interactive joke task) and includes a healthy control group (TD adults) analyzed separately, but it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps for the healthy/control group. The authors explicitly state they focused on an a priori ROI (arMPFC) and could not perform whole-brain or connectivity analyses due to signal loss. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately) but fails I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map reported) and thus meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of a social task (face-to-face joint attention) including healthy adult control groups. Neurotypical adults (matched control n=13, ROI control n=22; ages 18–39) are reported separately. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and reports voxelwise contrasts (e.g., RJA vs SA, IJA vs SA) with thresholded maps and coordinate tables for the neurotypical groups. Thus it meets the meta-analysis requirements for (I3) social fMRI task, (I4) healthy adult sample reported separately, (I5) whole-brain group-level task activation maps from healthy/control groups, and (I6) acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures/text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study uses a social-related empathizing task (I3 satisfied) and includes a healthy control group with adults in the 18–31 range (I4 satisfied). However, the provided full text reports whole-brain results primarily as group-by-age interactions and between-group differences (ASD vs TDC) and does not present an unambiguous, unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map or within-group main effect map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Thus it fails inclusion criterion I5. Because the paper appears to report only between-group interaction/contrast maps without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect, exclusion criterion E4 applies. Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED because E4 is met; inclusion criteria met: I3, I4; inclusion criterion not met: I5.

Although the study uses task-based fMRI in a social context (adult expert advice) and includes a healthy adult group (ages 18–45), the paper does not clearly report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map specifically identified as coming from the healthy adult group. The reported whole-brain voxelwise analyses focus on developmental (between-group) contrasts and age-related effects, and subsequent within-age-group tests are reported as ROI/extracted-beta comparisons. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (a clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of emotional (affective) speech comprehension—a social cognitive task involving perception and understanding of others' emotions. It reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (EMO vs GRAM) with voxelwise SPM analyses and corrected statistical maps and peak coordinates. The sample comprises 51 healthy adults aged 18–53 (within 18–65). Whole-brain results are clearly described and presented (figures, tables, coordinates). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study directly examining neural correlates of persuasion—a social-cognitive/mentalizing process—during task performance. Participants are healthy adults (American and Korean samples; ages reported within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (persuasive > unpersuasive) with thresholding and tables of coordinates (Tables 1A, 2, 4) and figures, clearly identified for healthy/control groups. Although ROI analyses were also performed in Study 3, whole-brain task-evoked results are reported for the healthy samples. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind/emotion/pain judgments) in healthy adults. Methods report task-based fMRI with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (univariate contrasts and MVPA), with statistical thresholds and reported maps/tables/figures (e.g., contrasts B>Ph, E>Ph, Pa>Ph; Tables and Figures provided). Sample: 46 healthy adult females (age 18–31). The paper provides full introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables and text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=27, ages within 18–65) that used task-based fMRI to examine social interaction processing (cooperative vs. affective interactions). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports coordinate tables and figures (FWE-corrected and uncorrected results), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related emotion-processing task relevant to social cognition) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group aged within 18–65). However, the full text does not clearly report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map specifically identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported whole-brain findings are either the main effect across all subjects and between-group contrasts (group differences), and ROI analyses; there is no clearly described unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect reported. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 is met (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (perception/attribution of animacy/mental states to moving shapes), conducted in healthy adult participants (15 males, mean age 26.6, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects, cluster- and voxel-level thresholds) with coordinates and figures/tables of activations. Therefore it meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range). Full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (male college students, ages within 18–65) that uses a social/affiliation paradigm (rival-fan memory retrieval, perspective-taking, self-referential and social-cognition processes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM random-effects, parametric and categorical contrasts, tables of activations, and small-volume corrections), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and the paper is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of emotional perspective taking (empathy) using face stimuli—clearly a social-related task. Participants were healthy adults (n=26, ages ~24), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (SELF- and OTHER-task vs high-level baseline) analyzed with random-effects SPM and presents whole-brain thresholded maps and tables of peak coordinates. Results for the healthy control group are reported separately and meet reporting standards (tables/figures and text). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study that manipulates self-referential processing and perspective taking—clear social-related cognitive tasks—reporting activation in medial prefrontal cortex subregions. The text indicates group-level task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts (e.g., self vs. other; perspective taking contrasts) with reported loci of activation, consistent with voxelwise whole-brain results. Participants are described as 'participants' with no clinical or special-group mention, implying healthy adult subjects. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and reports whole-brain task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining attachment-related processing using masked facial emotions (socially relevant task: affiliation/attachment). Sample = 51 healthy adults (mean age 28.5), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (main effects of masked sad/happy faces and regression correlations with attachment avoidance) with coordinates and corrected thresholds (tables/figures). All required whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group are presented. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, age within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating perception of social actions (social-related processing) using task-based fMRI and representational similarity/searchlight analyses. Participants were healthy adults (ages reported within 20–32) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (searchlight RSA and cluster tables with Talairach coordinates and corrected maps; figures and tables show whole-brain group effects for the healthy sample). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within 18–65). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

The study uses task fMRI of vocal emotion processing (social communication) in healthy adults (N=22, ages 19–36), satisfying I3 and I4. However, the paper reports primarily region-of-interest analyses with small-volume correction (amygdala and TVA) and partial-volume acquisition focused on temporal lobe/amygdala; it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level task activation map for the healthy group. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion E2 (only ROI/SVC results reported, no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E2. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (empathy/sympathy) using task-based stimuli, meeting the review’s focus. The sample includes healthy adult participants (age range 7–40, thus includes adults 18–40). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (PCS–NPS and PCO–PCS) and voxelwise correlation analyses, with results presented as whole-brain maps and coordinates. Whole-brain results are clearly described and thresholded. Therefore it satisfies the requirements for task-based fMRI in healthy participants and provides whole-brain evidence suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using dyadic (dfMRI) scanning during a social task (face-to-face eye contact), meeting the review’s social-processing requirement. The sample is healthy adults (19 pairs; ages 18–33) reported separately, satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (group GLM for tasks A and B; paired t-tests for exogenous/endogenous systems), with cluster results, MNI coordinates, atlas labels, and thresholding described (Table 3, Figs 3–5). Thus whole-brain healthy-group results are available. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without task maps, between-group-only contrasts, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study examines face-based social/emotional processing (Thatcher Illusion) and explicitly probes social/mentalizing regions; it includes a neurotypical healthy adult control group (N=18, mean age 25.8) reported separately; and it presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and statistical maps for the healthy/control group (within-group NT activation maps and thresholds reported). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for (I3) fMRI social-related task, (I4) healthy adult sample reported separately, (I5) whole-brain group-level results for controls, and (I6) acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in figures/text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study uses a social-related task (implicit perception of emotional facial expressions) and includes a healthy adult control group (satisfies I3 and I4). However, the paper does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (i.e., a within-group main effect or contrast for controls). Reported healthy-control results appear only as between-group contrasts (controls > patients) rather than an independent healthy-group whole-brain map. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social perception (trustworthiness/fear appraisal) and includes a healthy adult control group; however, the paper does not clearly report a whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map explicitly identified for the healthy/control group alone. The reported whole-brain analyses appear to be across all participants or focus on group contrasts (BPD vs controls) and ROI analyses for the amygdala are reported for controls. Inclusion criterion I5 requires a clear, group-level whole-brain healthy/control task map; that requirement is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4 (reporting only between-group contrasts or pooled analyses without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (multiround trust game) probing perception/understanding of others and social behavior, satisfying the social-task requirement. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=21; ages 18–47) reported separately from clinical groups. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and second-level whole-brain ANOVAs and regressions (e.g., Figure 2A, cluster- and voxel-wise PFWE thresholds, and tables of clusters/coordinates), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results for the healthy group are clearly identified and presented. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) are met.

This full-text fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing (self and peer evaluations; social domain), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult sample (19 adults ages 22–31) reported separately, meeting I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group analyses (2×4×3 whole-brain repeated-measures ANOVA, corrected via Monte Carlo/AlphaSim) with tables/figures of significant clusters and parameter estimates for the healthy groups, meeting I5 and I6. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met. Overall, the study provides whole-brain activation maps from healthy adults during a social task and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI experiment on socially-induced cognitive emotion regulation (Social-Reg) involving a psychotherapist regulating participants’ emotions—clearly a social-related task (Affiliation/Attachment; social cognition). The sample comprises healthy adults (22 females, ages 22–32) with group-level analyses reported for the healthy participants. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Social-Reg > Social-Look) with cluster-wise FWE correction and tables/figures of activations and coordinates. Results from the healthy group are presented directly (not limited to a narrow subgroup). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=25 analyzed, mean age 26.3) that used task-based whole-brain fMRI while participants freely viewed socio-emotional film scenes and provided continuous valence and conflict ratings. The paradigm targets social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, socio-emotional conflict). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects group-level regressions with cluster correction) and presents results in text, figures and tables (coordinates), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, not between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical study). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an emotional face-matching task (social perception of angry/fearful faces), conducted in a healthy adult sample (n=98, ages 18–30). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation analyses including an exploratory whole-brain analysis (FDR-corrected) and presents results in figures/tables described in the text. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study includes a healthy adult control group (N=13, ages >18) and uses a social-related task (perception of fearful faces). The paper reports group-level, within-control-group task contrasts and provides whole-brain voxelwise results (main effect of faces for controls) with coordinates and tables, satisfying the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task activation maps; results are reported both in text and tables/figures. Though small-volume correction was applied to a priori ROIs, the analyses began with a whole-brain threshold and the control-group activations (including amygdala, IOG, MPFC) are clearly identified. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mental simulation of personally familiar people), with healthy adult participants (n=23 after exclusions; age 18–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight and feature-selected RSA analyses, including random-effects t tests, cluster-corrected statistical maps, peak coordinates and figures/tables of whole-brain results. Results are clearly reported for the healthy control sample. Thus it meets the fMRI social-task requirement, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level reporting criteria.

This fMRI study investigates implicit processing of facial emotions (fear vs neutral), which is a social-related task (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=24) matched to patients and within the adult age range (I4). The paper reports group-level control results used to localize the amygdala seed (peak MNI coordinate −26,0,−20) derived from a control-group voxelwise analysis and describes control-group activation in text/coordinates; this satisfies the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task effect (I5). Reporting of the control-group peak coordinate and description of the group-level activation meets the allowance for coordinate/figure-based reporting (I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: although the main analysis is PPI connectivity, a healthy-group task activation is reported, so E3/E4 do not exclude the study. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is INCLUDED for the review.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=22 males, mean age 24.2) performing social-related tasks (allocentric social hierarchy and social alliance judgements). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (second-level SPM), thresholded at p<0.05 FWE, with activation maps and tables of coordinates reported for the healthy participant group. Results are clearly described in text, figures, and tables. Therefore it satisfies the review objective and all inclusion criteria for whole-brain task-evoked fMRI in healthy adults.

This study is excluded because it does not include a healthy adult (18–65) participant group and the task is a non-social visual attention task. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (participants are children/adolescents; no healthy adult subgroup reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps for the control group) and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables and described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (the fMRI task is non-social visual attention, not a social-related task) and I4 (no healthy adult sample; all participant groups are boys/children/adolescents). Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This empirical fMRI study used task-based fMRI with socially relevant, attachment-related stimuli (own-infant and mother–infant interaction videos). Participants were healthy adult mothers aged 22–37 (N=23 analyzed), meeting the adult healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (own infant > stranger infant) with statistical maps and tables described in the text and figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment (exp. 3) in healthy adult participants (N=21) using a task that involves retrieval of real-life, socially relevant events (oral examination interactions) tied to self/other and bodily-self processing, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activations (baseline contrasts and interaction effects) with coordinates and corrected statistics (including hippocampal small-volume correction) and describes these results for the healthy/control group separately. Participants are healthy adults (students) within the target age range. The study is empirical and not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or resting-state analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This empirical fMRI study investigates gesture planning and execution, a form of social communication, using task-based fMRI in a sample that includes a healthy adult control group. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and within-group (healthy controls) results (within-group results noted in Analyses S2/S3 and whole-brain second-level analyses described with thresholds and clusters). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants with separate healthy-group reporting), I5 (whole-brain group-level healthy-control task maps), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of cross-modal person recognition (voice-face) in healthy adults (N=16), so inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample) are met. However, the paper reports results focused on ROI-corrected voxelwise analyses and PPI connectivity; the authors state there were no significant results at P<0.05 FWE for the whole brain without the covariate, and all reported activations are reported with ROI-based FWE correction or limited to predefined ROIs. The review requires at least one group-level whole-brain (unmasked/whole-brain) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group (I5), which is not provided. Therefore this study meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criterion met: E2. Full text appears complete.

The study uses fMRI of face processing (a social-related task) and includes healthy adult participants, and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses; however, the paper does not present a clear group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. The main whole-brain analyses appear to be conducted on a combined sample of patients and controls, and the independent (healthy-only) replication used an anatomical ROI approach rather than an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group activation map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain result). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) strictly apply. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I5.

(a) Exclusion met: E4 — the imaging results presented are predominantly between-group contrasts (schizophrenia vs control) and the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map or clearly identified voxelwise group-level statistical map for the healthy/control group alone. Figures and tables report between-group clusters and percent signal change by group, but no whole-brain healthy-group map or coordinate-based within-group healthy activation results are reported as a primary, unmasked healthy-group task effect. (b) Inclusion met: I3 — fMRI was used during a social-related (cognitive empathy/emotional perspective-taking) task; I4 — a healthy adult control group (n=24; ages 18–50) is included and reported separately. (c) Inclusion not met: I5 — no clear whole-brain, group-level healthy/control task-evoked statistical map is reported. I6 is therefore not satisfied because qualifying whole-brain healthy-group results are not present in tables/figures/text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because I5 is not met and E4 applies, the study must be excluded for this meta-analysis.

This study reports fMRI task activations during a social-related task (imaginary sentence completion about mother/father) involving attachment/affiliation and social cognition. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=15; mean age ~28) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation results for the control group (one-sample t tests; results presented in Table 2 and described in the text). Whole-brain maps/coordinates for the healthy group are provided, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within adult age range, and this is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (judgments about self, friends, and strangers; constructs: perception/understanding of self and others, affiliation/attachment). Participants are healthy adults (n=98, mean age 20.7) and results are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and maps (e.g., self > Bush; friends > strangers) presented in figures and described in the text (thresholded at p < 0.001), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social appraisal (preference judgments of faces), meeting the review objective. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=21) recruited to match the patient group and reports results for the healthy group separately (within-group contrasts and descriptions). Group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and coordinate tables for the PREF>GENDER contrasts are presented for groups (figures and tables explicitly display/control group activations and PPI results for controls). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or out-of-range age/sample-only reporting). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic investigator thumbs-up/thumbs-down feedback) during task-based fMRI. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=21, age range 21–39), meeting the 18–65 requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses and corrected statistical maps/activation tables for the healthy group (negative social feedback > positive social feedback under placebo and drug conditions), with coordinates and figures. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: it reports an fMRI task probing social/attachment processing (parents viewing own vs. unfamiliar infant videos), includes healthy adult participants aged 22–37, and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (whole-brain GLM contrasts own-infant>standard-infant and voxelwise intersubject correlation maps) reported in the text/results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and participants are within 18–65). Sample size is modest but does not violate inclusion criteria. Therefore include.

This is an fMRI study of compassion training using the socio-affective video task (SoVT), a social-affective paradigm probing responses to others’ distress (affiliation/compassion). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (94 right-handed women, ages 18–35), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (HE vs LE contrasts, parametric modulations, and whole-brain FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables) clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Whole-brain results are presented in text/tables and supplemented by ROI/SVC analyses; whole-brain task activations from the healthy group are available. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an fMRI study of face perception/recognition (social perception of others), using functional MRI during task-based viewing of faces (Experiment 1) and behavioral tasks linked to fMRI data (Experiments 2–3), meeting the social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (ages reported, mean ages in 20s; n=20 in main fMRI experiment), satisfying the sample criterion. The methods describe group-level, whole-brain mixed-effects (FLAME) analyses and an independent localizer contrast (faces vs scrambled) used to define ROIs from group data, indicating group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps are reported/used. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (only ROI analyses, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

(a) Exclusion met: E4. The paper reports task activation only as between-group contrasts (patients vs. controls) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map. (b) Inclusion met: I3 (uses fMRI with a social-related task — facial expression discrimination), I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, ages 18–65). (c) Inclusion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map clearly identified as from the healthy/control group), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain healthy-group results reported in tables/figures/text). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for failing I5 and meeting exclusion E4.

This fMRI study used a social-related task (Cyberball social rejection), fulfilling I3. The sample includes a healthy adult group (n=16 adults, female), meeting I4. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps (e.g., exclusion>inclusion main effects surviving cluster-level FWE correction) and provides peak coordinates and tables, satisfying I5 and I6. Results are not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses, and healthy participants are clearly reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates perception/recognition of visual feedback as self vs other (visuo-motor and visuo-proprioceptive synchrony), which maps to ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’ (a social-related construct). Participants were healthy adults (16, median age 24), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Aa–As, Pa–Ps) analyzed with SPM2 and provides tables/figures of whole-brain results. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI data).

The manuscript reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of social processing (eye-gaze perception), using healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 18–30). Whole-brain, group-level second‑level voxelwise analyses are reported (variable vs. constant gaze contrasts and AQ regressions), with corrected thresholds and peak coordinates provided in the text and supplementary ROI checks. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results reported), and I6 (coordinates and text description). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. The full article text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of emotion perception from dynamic avatars (social perception of others), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=19, mean age ~28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and random-effects GLM results (e.g., multi-subject contrasts for Emotional vs Neutral, parametric GLM maps; figures and corrected cluster thresholds are provided for N=17 and N=14 analyses). The task is social-related (perception/understanding of others’ emotions via gait), the sample is within 18–65 and healthy, and whole-brain voxelwise results for the healthy group are clearly reported in text and figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study that probes social-related processing (self-related and mentalizing/social cognition) during an article-reading/sharing task and links neural activity to behavior. Participants were healthy adults aged 18–24 in two samples (n=41 and n=39), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses and exploratory whole-brain maps and cluster tables (SI Fig. S3 and Table S5) with multiple-comparison corrections and permutation testing, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. The manuscript contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and whole-brain results are described in the text and supplements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and this is empirical work).

This is a task-based fMRI study of joint attention (social communication/understanding of others) in healthy adults (final N=13; mean age ~24.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (contrasts, conjunctions) with FDR-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of coordinates and statistical maps, clearly from the healthy/control group. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review (social fMRI task, healthy adult sample, whole-brain group results reported, and acceptable reporting via tables/figures).

This full-text reports empirical fMRI studies of social-affective processing in healthy adult participants. The paper includes two group-level fMRI experiments (fMRI1, fMRI2) using a social/empathy visuo-tactile paradigm, with whole-brain random-effects analyses (fMRI1 reported whole-brain results; fMRI2 used independent localizer-based SVC but also performed whole-brain analyses and reports group-level task contrasts and coordinates). Samples consist of healthy adult participants (female undergraduates) reported separately for each experiment. Group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts for the healthy groups are reported (interaction contrasts, peak coordinates, and tables/figures). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study examines social-related processing (rapid fearful face perception) in adults and includes a healthy adult control group whose results are reported separately. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not limited to abstract), and the authors report whole-brain analyses (FLAME whole-brain analyses described in Appendix A and Supplementary Table 1) with significant clusters for the control group for the fearful face > scramble contrast. Thus inclusion criteria are satisfied: I3 (fMRI social task: emotional face processing), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps for the control group are reported), and I6 (whole-brain results described in text/appendix and supplementary materials). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains healthy adults 18–65, empirical data). Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses task fMRI of self-referential (social-cognitive) processing and includes a healthy control group, it does not report a group-level whole-brain, task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. The paper focuses on ROI- and seed-based voxelwise functional connectivity/network reconstructions and between-group connectivity differences (aMCI vs controls). This makes it a seed-based connectivity/task-network connectivity study without an unmasked, healthy-group whole-brain task activation map, thus violating the review requirement for whole-brain task activation evidence. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (only seed/functional connectivity results without healthy-group whole-brain task activation) and E4 (reports mainly between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (implicit and explicit theory-of-mind) in healthy adults using a Sally–Anne type paradigm, meeting the review objective. Sample: 33 recruited, N=22 analyzed, mean age 24.4 (within 18–65), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports a group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM for the explicit general-belief localizer (contrasting false-belief vs false-photograph) and provides voxelwise results/coordinates (q(FDR)<0.05; Fig.2A and peak Talairach coordinates), which are clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. Although the primary implicit ToM contrast was analyzed with an ROI approach, the presence of the whole-brain localizer map satisfies the whole-brain results inclusion (acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social communication in healthy adult participants (female, age 19–28). The task manipulates perceived sender (friend vs computer) during text-message reception, engaging social cognition/mentalizing. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (univariate contrasts and searchlight MVPA/MVCA) with cluster-corrected statistical maps and tables of activated clusters, clearly for the healthy/control group. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used an explicit facial emotion identification task (social perception of others' emotions), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=22; mean age 31.7 years), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain ‘faces minus animals’ activation maps for the HC group (one-sample t tests and FDR-corrected results; figures and tables of activation foci are provided), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text (satisfying acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, and participants are within 18–65). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This task-based fMRI study investigates processing of natural interpersonal touch (touch delivered by another person), which is a social-related stimulus (social communication/affiliation). Participants were healthy adults (N=8, ages 22–39).
