The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise spatial maps derived from group ICA (thresholded IC maps shown and described) and present task-evoked component time courses demonstrating stimulus dependence; these constitute group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps. Although analyses used ICA rather than a standard GLM contrast, the reported group spatial maps and stimulus-related effects satisfy the requirement for whole-brain task activation evidence. The paper is empirical, not ROI-only, and reports healthy-group results explicitly. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social incentive delay task (social reward/punishment) meeting the review focus on social processing. Sample: 28 healthy adult women aged 20–42, reported separately from clinical subgroups, satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (an uncorrected whole-brain exploration at p<.001 and reported coordinates/observations outside the VTA, including nucleus accumbens), indicating whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group. Core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This fMRI study uses a social-related task (self/other evaluation with perspective-taking) and includes a clearly reported healthy adult control group; however, the full text presents combined-group whole-brain contrasts and between-group comparisons and ROI analyses, but does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. Therefore it fails to meet I5. Exclusion is based on E4 (reports mainly between-group contrasts/interaction and combined-group maps without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social task) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain healthy-group task map). Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI task probing self-referential processing and perspective-taking (social-related constructs: perception/understanding of self and others), meeting the review’s scope. It includes a healthy control group with within-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation contrasts clearly reported for the healthy/control group (e.g., self>other within HC; reported clusters/coordinates and figures/tables). Results for the healthy group are reported separately from the clinical UHR group. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results and discussion (core article content present). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. Minor uncertainty about explicit ages of healthy participants (HC age range not verbatim), but demographics and recruitment imply adult controls; confidence set to 0.85.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines neural responses to romantic and sexual stimuli (social/affiliation-related processing). Participants were healthy adult men (ages 22–50) meeting the adult age range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., sexual>neutral, romantic>neutral; between-group contrasts) analyzed with FSL and cluster-wise thresholding and presents results in figures and tables. Results for the healthy participant groups are reported separately. The study is not ROI-only, not a connectivity or resting-state study, and is original fMRI data in healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (women and comparison to previously collected healthy men; ages 18–22). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (e.g., CC vs CD) and whole-brain analyses with cluster-level correction and direct comparisons reported in the text, tables, and figures. Whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps and contrasts for the healthy/control groups are explicitly described. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results are clearly reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply.

This empirical study used task-based fMRI probing social-emotional face processing (fearful and calm faces), includes a healthy adult control group (mean age 39.8, n=13), and reports group-level whole-brain within-group activation maps for the control group (robust bilateral amygdala activation reported with P<0.05 corrected). The task is clearly social-related (perception/understanding of others). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Exclusion: E2 and E3. Inclusion: I3 and I4 met. The study uses fMRI during a social joint-attention task (I3) and reports a healthy adult sample (mean age ~24; I4). However, it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group (I5 not met). Analyses are ROI-based and report multivariate directed functional connectivity among a set of preselected cortical regions (connectivity-only results), meeting exclusion criteria E2 (ROI-only/no whole-brain results) and E3 (connectivity-only without whole-brain task activation maps). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study using a social-evaluative task (naturalistic approval/disapproval videos) in healthy adults (N=37; mean age 24.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (positive>neutral, negative>neutral, conjunction) with familywise-error corrected results and tables/figures of coordinates and maps. Although ROI analyses are also reported, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps for the healthy sample are clearly described. Thus all required inclusion criteria for fMRI social-processing studies in healthy adults are met.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (mean age 22.4, n=16 after exclusions) investigating visual perspective taking — a social-cognitive process (perception/understanding of others). The task is social in nature (self vs. other perspective judgments). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Inconsistent Other > Consistent Other; Consistent Self > Consistent Other) with cluster-level FWE correction and tables of results and coordinates. Whole-brain analyses are explicitly described and attributed to the healthy participant group. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI in healthy adults and provides whole-brain activation maps/coordinates.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related approach-avoidance task contrasting social vs nonsocial stimuli (relevant to social processing constructs); (2) Sample consists of healthy adults (male, mean age 21.35, N=76 analyzed) within the 18–65 range; (3) The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses and describes exploratory whole-brain results beyond ROI analyses (with reference to whole-brain results reported in the manuscript/supplement); (4) Whole-brain results are acceptable to be in supplementary materials per criteria. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes healthy adult task activation maps). Therefore INCLUDE.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (theory of mind/social exchange) in healthy adults. The sample analyzed comprises healthy adults (N=12, mean age 24.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (story and card contrasts) using SPM2 and a group random-effects model, with tables and figures of activated clusters and coordinates. Whole-brain results are clearly described and contrasted (social contract, precaution, descriptive) for the healthy/control group. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of facial emotion discrimination (a social-cognitive task: perception/understanding of others) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=12) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (emotional conditions versus baseline and versus neutral) analyzed for both groups, with voxelwise results, coordinate tables/figures, and FWE/uncorrected thresholds. Within-group contrasts for controls are described and illustrated (e.g., sad > neutral in controls shown in Fig. 3), satisfying the requirement for an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult nulliparous women (ages 19–29) using social-related tasks (perception of infant cries and faces), thus addressing social processing (Perception/Understanding of Others; affiliation/attachment). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., cry vs pink noise; happy vs neutral faces) with corrected whole-brain thresholds and displays coordinates and brain maps. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, empirical fMRI data reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses fMRI of social cognition (Theory of Mind and affective empathy) and includes a healthy adult control group, so it meets I3 (social fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported). However, the full text reports effects of diagnosis, between-group contrasts, and conjunction analyses showing where diagnosis influenced task responses, and presents VBM results restricted to those areas. It does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (no explicit within-group whole-brain healthy-control task effect map is reported in the text or tables). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports primarily between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Excluded on this basis.

I3, I5, and I6 are satisfied: the study used fMRI during a social Theory-of-Mind task (RMET) in healthy participants and reports a group-level whole-brain ‘mind minus age’ contrast with voxelwise results (figures and thresholds). However, it fails I4: the healthy participant group age range is 51–84 (M=68.4), so the study does not provide a healthy adult sample restricted to 18–65 or a separate subgroup in that range. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E4, E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult age 18–65).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory-of-mind task) in healthy adult participants (n=109). The Methods and Results report a group-level whole-brain task contrast (ToM > control) across all healthy subjects, thresholded and presented in figures/tables (P<0.01 FWE for main effect; voxelwise genotype effects also reported FDR-corrected). The task probes social-related processing (mentalising), sample comprises healthy adults, and whole-brain group-level activation maps/effects for the healthy group are clearly reported in text, figures, and tables. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied.

The study uses task fMRI of social processing with whole-brain analyses and reports group-level voxelwise results (tables/figures), satisfying I3, I5, and I6. However, participant groups fall outside the review age range: the younger group includes participants aged 17–27 (includes minors <18) and the older group is 65–75 (entirely >65). No group is reported that is exclusively within the target 18–65 age range, nor is a healthy adult subgroup (18–65) analyzed separately. Therefore the study violates the age-range eligibility and meets exclusion criterion E5.

This study reports an fMRI face-processing task (happy and fearful faces) in a community sample of young adults (meets I3 and I4). However, all fMRI analyses are ROI-based interregional correlation matrices over 25 predefined face ROIs and structural covariance analyses; the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). Because only ROI-based results are reported with no whole-brain activation maps, exclusion criterion E2 applies. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (imitation and observation of communicative gestures) in healthy adults (20 analyzed; mean age 24.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and cluster-corrected results with coordinate tables and figures (e.g., IMI>CT conjunction, S>NS contrasts, interaction analyses). Healthy-control results are reported separately and meet voxelwise whole-brain reporting standards. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, non-adult-only samples, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This study meets all inclusion requirements: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-emotional approach-avoidance task (I3), includes a large sample of healthy adults aged 18–43 with results reported for the healthy group (I4), and reports group-level whole-brain task analyses and contrasts (explicit whole-brain analyses and task effects are described and assessed at the whole-brain level) with results presented in text/figures/tables (I5,I6). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and core analyses are described, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not out-of-range ages, and is empirical).

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (three studies, combined N=59) performing social-related semantic tasks (person knowledge, socially relevant words), satisfying the review’s social-processing target. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., social > non-social semantics) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction and peak coordinates presented, clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control participants; ROI analyses are supplementary. Study 2 includes control participants reported separately from patient data. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

Although this study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses task-based fMRI of social processing: Social emotion/Belief tasks) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, n=17), the full text only reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (typically developing > ASD) and region coordinates for group differences. The manuscript does not present or clearly identify an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (no control-group one-sample whole-brain results or coordinate table/figure explicitly labeled as the healthy group main effect are provided). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria I5 (healthy-group whole-brain map reported) is not met. Full text appears complete. Hence the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports primarily between-group/cross-brain coupling contrasts (cBPD-HC vs rBPD-HC vs HC-HC) and ICA-derived coupling measures, but does not provide a clear, unmasked group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map explicitly for the healthy/control group (I5 not satisfied). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social joint-attention task) and I4 (healthy adult participants and HC-HC pairs reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain healthy-group task activation map in the provided full text). Full text appears complete for core content (methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.
